e: You write pricing rules. About every five minutes MAYA reads your bookings, runs your rules over the next 60 nights, and sends the prices that changed to your property system (with Mews, nothing is sent yet). Nothing is sent until you say so. The change log shows the latest changes and why each one happened.

A rule is a sentence you fill in: when a night looks like this, change the price by that much.

Here is one from The Harbour Inn, a 20-room property we use in every example: when a night is more than 80% full, raise the price by 10%. On the **Rules** tab that rule is a name ("Busy nights"), a condition (**Sellable occupancy (%)**, **Greater than**, 80), a direction (**Increase the rate**) and an amount (10%). That is the whole rule.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. When The Harbour Inn has 17 of its 20 rooms booked for November 14, that night is 85% full, so "Busy nights" fires and Standard goes from $150 to $165. When it has 16 booked, the night is exactly 80% full, which is not more than 80%, so the rule waits.

A rule can watch four things about a night:

| What a rule can watch | On screen | In plain words |
|---|---|---|
| Sellable occupancy | **Sellable occupancy (%)** | how full the night is |
| Booking speed | **Booking speed (recommended)** | how fast the night is booking compared with your own similar past nights |
| Booking window | **Booking window (days to stay)** | how many days away the night is |
| Pickup count | **Pickup count (advanced)** | how many more rooms were booked for the night, or how much room revenue it gained, in the last 1, 3 or 7 days |

A rule can combine up to four of these, one of each kind. All of them have to be true at once for the rule to fire. You build rules by filling in dropdowns, not by writing code. [Build your first rule](@30) walks through it click by click.

**1. You set the rules**

You add a rule on the **Rules** tab. With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, setup also adds starter rules built from your own booking history, when there is about 60 days of it. They are added for you and switched on, but while you are in simulation they only show what they would do. Nothing is sent. You can switch any of them off or delete them before you go live. Later, **Get suggestions from my data** can offer more as cards, which you accept or turn down. Each rule has an **On/Off** switch.

**Example: What this looks like on screen**

The **Rules** tab lists every rule in a table: its name, how many times it has fired, its conditions, the room types it applies to, the price change, and its **On/Off** switch. Under the table, **+ Add a rule** opens the builder. Above it, a panel called **How rules behave** plays two short animations.

**2. MAYA runs them**

About every five minutes, MAYA reads your bookings and room types from your property system, refreshes your own rates from it about once an hour, runs every rule over the next 60 nights, and sends the prices that changed. Sending only happens once you have gone live, and never to Mews yet. Until then MAYA runs everything and sends nothing.

This all happens on MAYA's side, day and night, whether or not anyone has MAYA open. Nobody needs to be signed in, and the office computer being off or your own internet being down does not stop it. What stops it is MAYA being unable to reach your property system's service (read [Connection lost](@100)), or a subscription that has stopped.

Every price change is recorded: which room type, which night, from what to what, which rule acted and why. For a booking speed change, a **How did we know?** button opens the past nights this night was compared with and the counts behind the change.

The **Change Log** tab shows the latest ones: about the last 50 minutes (the 10 most recent runs, about five minutes apart). Each run shows up to 40 changes, the biggest moves first. The detail behind every change is kept for 90 days. For a change older than the runs on screen, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) within those 90 days and we look it up for you. [The change log](@46) has the limits.

MAYA reads only what pricing needs:

- **Bookings**: the stay dates, the room type, the nightly rate, and the date the booking was made. Cancellations are read the same way and taken off the count.
Bookings

- **Room types**, and with Cloudbeds how many rooms each has. MAYA does not read room counts from ThinkReservations yet, and Mews does not normally report them. So with those two, MAYA uses one room count for every room type, which we set with you (on ThinkReservations, 100 until then). [Your room count and what you pay](@59) says why that matters.
Room types

- **Your own rates** for each night, read from your property system about once an hour, so your rate is the starting point a rule works from. This applies to Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations. Mews rates are not read.
Your own rates

- **Property details**: with Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, the property's name, time zone and currency are read once, at connection. With Mews we set them with you when we connect it.

Guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, notes and payment details are never stored. What is kept about a booking is its structure: dates, room type, price, party size as a count, and the booking channel. [What MAYA reads and writes](@15) lists every field.
Property details

One nightly price per room type, and nothing else.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes each room type's base rate. Rate plans set up to follow it move with it by Cloudbeds' own rules. [Cloudbeds](@12) has the details.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes the rate type named Best Available. Name your main rate type Best Available to be sure it is the one written. Rate types set up to follow it move with it by ThinkReservations' own rules. ThinkReservations accepts a price and applies it shortly after, and MAYA checks about an hour later that the price is there. [ThinkReservations](@13) says what happens when no rate type has that name.

Only prices that changed go out. A night whose price has not changed since MAYA last sent it is not sent again. On your first live run, every night in the 60-night window that has a price is sent once, including nights your rules left at your own rate. A price of 0 is never sent. For a free night, type 0 in MAYA and set 0 in your property system yourself.

- Reservations. MAYA never creates, changes or cancels a booking. So when a rule raises or cuts tonight's price, guests who have already booked keep the rate they booked at. The new price is for bookings made after it reaches your system.
- Availability, overbooking limits or room allotments.
- Minimum stays, closed-to-arrival, closed-to-departure or close-outs.
- Guests, guest profiles or guest messages.
- Packages, promotions or non-refundable plans directly. Plans set up to follow your base rate move with it by your system's own rules. A package or plan with its own separate rate does not move. With ThinkReservations, this holds once your main rate type is named Best Available.
- Booking.com, Expedia or any other channel directly. Your property system and channel manager carry your base rate to them, as they do today.

**Sellable occupancy** is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. Only room types you have ticked as rooms count, and rooms you have marked out of service come off first. Twelve Standard rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89%. [Sellable occupancy](@32) has a slider to try.
Sellable occupancy

**Booking speed** is how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with how many your own similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. MAYA turns that into one of seven levels, from Stalled to Surging, and a rule can fire on any of them. After a booking speed or pickup count rule has raised a night, booking speed rules that raise count only the bookings that came in since then. Cuts work the same way. So one burst of bookings brings one booking speed raise. Pickup count and occupancy rules are not limited this way. [Booking speed](@34) explains the levels, and [after the rule acts](@34#after-the-rule-acts) explains the counting.
Booking speed

- A rule raises or cuts the starting price by a percentage or a fixed amount, and the result stays between that room type's floor and ceiling. [Floors and ceilings](@28) says where they come from.
- Booking speed compares a night with your own similar past nights: the same weekday, the same time of year, the same position around a holiday, from the last three years. It is a comparison with your own past nights, and it says nothing about your future.
- MAYA does not read competitor rates, rate shoppers, weather, events or market data. There is no feed to switch on.

**Good to know: How a wedding counts** · With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, a wedding of 20 rooms on one booking counts once for booking speed, both now and on the past nights it is compared with. You set the rules, and MAYA runs them against your bookings and your own past years. Your rules act on what is already on the books: how full a night is now, how many days away it is, how many rooms it gained in the last 1, 3 or 7 days, and how fast it is booking compared with your own similar past nights at the same point. Booking speed describes the pace so far, not where the night will end up.

So a price moves after bookings arrive, not before them. When you know something your bookings cannot show yet, such as a festival or a wedding in town, type a price for those nights. [Hold a price for an event](@67) shows how.

Per room, per month, and the price per room drops as the property grows. There is no minimum: 5 rooms is $27.50 a month. Yearly billing saves 10% from 21 rooms up. Prices are in US dollars and exclude tax. Every size gets the same MAYA.

Find the row your room count lands in. Every room in the property pays that row's rate.

| Rooms | Per room, per month | Yearly |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 20 | $5.50 | 12 times the monthly price, paid once a year |
| 21 to 40 | $5.00 | 10% off |
| 41 to 60 | $4.00 | 10% off |
| 61 to 80 | $3.00 | 10% off |
| 81 to 500 | $2.50 | 10% off |

The whole property bills at one bracket: the one its room count falls into. There is no minimum charge and no other fee. Any adjustment for a room count change shows on your next invoice. Prices exclude tax, and any tax that applies is yours to pay under the Terms. Each property is its own subscription.

20 rooms: $110 a month. 21 rooms: $105 a month, or $1,134 a year with 10% off.

The calculator on the get-maya.com home page uses the same brackets. Both use the room count you type. After you connect, MAYA checks it against the rooms in your system, and how it counts them depends on the system: read [how the bill is worked out](#how-the-bill-is-worked-out-after-you-sign-up).

**Example: Some worked examples** · The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms: 20 times $5.50 is $110 a month, or $1,320 a year paid once. A 21-room property is in the next bracket: 21 times $5.00 is $105 a month, or $1,134 a year with the 10% off. 40 rooms: $200 a month or $2,160 a year. 100 rooms: $250 a month or $2,700 a year. A 3-room B&B pays $16.50 a month.

You may have spotted that 21 rooms costs less than 20. That is on purpose. The bracket is a step: when a property crosses into the next bracket, every one of its rooms moves to the lower rate. There is no blended or "first 20 rooms at one price, the rest at another" arithmetic to work out. One room count, one rate, one number.

You choose at signup, on the **Billing** control of the payment screen, between **Monthly** and **Yearly**.

- **Monthly** bills the bracket price each month, in advance, at the start of each month of service.
Monthly

- **Yearly** is one invoice for twelve months at the per-room rate, less 10% from 21 rooms up. The screen says so beside the button: **save 10%** for 21 rooms and up, and **pay once a year** for 1 to 20 rooms, because the smallest bracket has no yearly discount.

The yearly price is still worked out per room, per month, and then multiplied by twelve. The **Billing** page shows it as one price per year. To switch between monthly and yearly later, open **Update card, receipts & cancellation** on the **Billing** page and change the plan in Stripe's portal. A switch starts a new billing period that day. Moving to yearly charges the full year at once, less a credit for the unused part of your month. [Switching between monthly and yearly](@60#switching-between-monthly-and-yearly) has the detail.
Yearly

**Commitment.** There is no contract term beyond the period you have paid for. A monthly plan can be cancelled any time and ends at the next renewal date. A yearly plan runs to the end of the year you paid for, with no refund for the rest of it. Read [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@61).
Commitment

Accounts created directly at maya-rms.com (ThinkReservations, Mews, or Cloudbeds by code) get no trial unless a code grants one. Every property, trial or not, starts in simulation, where MAYA runs your rules and sends nothing, so you can watch before anything reaches your system. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).

**Do I pay while I am in simulation?** Yes. Your subscription runs from checkout, or from the end of the trial, whether your property is in simulation or live. Going live costs nothing extra, and there is no other fee.

**Careful** · A card is always collected, trial or not. Unless you cancel before the trial ends, it becomes a paid subscription and the card is charged. Cancelling takes effect at the end of the paid period, and there are no refunds for part of a period.

What you pay is not refunded, including for part of a billing period, rooms or features you did not use, a move to a smaller plan, or time when MAYA or your property system was down. Cancelling stops the next renewal, and MAYA keeps working to the end of the period you paid for. Lowering your room count gives a credit against future invoices, never money back. A free trial costs nothing if you cancel before it ends.

The Terms name the exceptions. If we end your subscription for our own reasons, on 30 days' notice, or stop offering MAYA altogether, we refund the unused part of the period you paid for. And where the law gives you a refund, you get it. Read [Terms and legal](@109#fees-cancelling-and-refunds-in-brief), and clauses 3.5, 7.10 and 12.3 of the [Terms of Service](https://www.get-maya.com/terms).

A code is something we give you. It can grant a trial of some number of days, a percentage off (for a set number of months, or for as long as you stay), or a dollar amount off each month (for a set number of months, or for as long as you stay). The payment screen tells you exactly what your code grants the moment you type it, and the price panel re-prices in front of you.

Four things to expect:

- One code per property. A code cannot be used twice on the same property.
- A code's trial replaces the Marketplace trial. The two never stack.
- There is no referral programme. Recommending MAYA to another hotel earns nothing today, and discounts come only from codes we issue.

Each property is its own subscription at its own bracket. Two 15-room properties are two subscriptions at $5.50 a room, not one 30-room property at $5.00. Brackets are never pooled. If your Cloudbeds login covers several properties, one card is taken for the first and offered for each of the others, and you pay for them one at a time. There is no volume discount beyond what a code grants. Read [Paying for a group of properties](@10).

You type a room count at signup. After you connect, MAYA counts the rooms again on every sync, counting only room types you have ticked as rooms. Where that count comes from depends on your system.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds reports how many rooms each room type has, so the count is read from Cloudbeds.

**ThinkReservations:** As soon as you have paid, and before you connect if you can, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) how many rooms each room type has. MAYA does not read room counts from ThinkReservations yet. Until we set yours, it gives every room type the same number, 100, so a 12-room inn with three room types would read as 300. The count is that number times the room types you have ticked as rooms. We set it with you, so your bill is not raised to a wrong count.

**Mews:** Mews does not normally report how many rooms each room category has, so MAYA uses one number for every category, set with us when we connect Mews. The count is that number times the categories you have ticked as rooms. Check the **Room count** section of the **Billing** page after we connect you, and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) if it is higher than the rooms you run.

If the count is higher than the rooms you pay for, you get an email and 7 days to set the count yourself. After that MAYA raises it to the measured number and adjusts your next invoice. Nothing is charged on the day. That is how it works today. Under the Terms, we can also charge the difference separately, and bill for rooms that were in use but not paid for over the previous 12 months. So set the count right as soon as the email arrives.
Prices exclude tax. Any sales tax or value added tax (VAT) that applies comes on top. Under the Terms, it is yours to pay.

Stripe hosts the payment page and holds your card. MAYA never sees the card number. You can always pay by card. US bank debit (ACH) is not accepted, and MAYA does not send invoices for you to pay by hand. Stripe's page shows the ways you can pay.
Self-serve signup takes any whole number from 1 to 500 rooms. Above 500, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Over%20500%20rooms) and we set it up by hand.

Under the Terms, we can change prices, brackets or plans by giving at least 30 days' notice. A change applies from the start of your first billing period that begins after the notice period, which on a yearly plan means your next renewal. If you do not agree, you can cancel before then.

**Not yet** · There is no free plan and no volume discount beyond what a code grants. US bank debit (ACH) and paying by invoice are not offered, but a card always works. Over 500 rooms, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Over%20500%20rooms) and we set it up by hand.

The app is one page: a header with Help, Billing, Team and Sign Out, five tabs (Calendar, Rules, Rate Simulator, Change Log and PMS), the Property dropdown beside the tabs, and banners above the tabs when something needs you.

At the top left is the MAYA logo with two short taglines under it. At the top right are four buttons: **Help**, **Billing**, **Team** and **Sign Out**.

**Billing** opens your billing page and **Team** opens your team page. Both are for a General Manager or Hotel Admin. Anyone else who opens them sees the page with a short explanation instead of the controls. Each has a **← Back to MAYA** link at the top. **Sign Out** signs you out and returns you to the sign-in page. **Help** opens the page of these docs about the screen you are on, in a new tab, so nothing you have half filled in is lost.
The tabs sit under the header. **Calendar** is the one that opens first when you sign in.

Click a day and the day detail opens: the date, a summary line, and one card per room type with **Booked**, **ADR** (ADR means average daily rate: that night's room revenue divided by the rooms booked), **Current price** and **Revenue**. When **Booked** reads 0, ignore the ADR line: the $150.00 there is a placeholder, not a rate of yours. Under each room type card is the box where you type a price for that room type on that night. **Prev** and **Next** step a month at a time, and the month and year dropdowns jump further. **Good to know** · Top right of the calendar, a small line reads "Updated", then the time in your browser's own format ("Updated 3:05:12 PM · live" in US English). The word live there means the calendar refreshes by itself when prices or bookings change. It shows in simulation too, so it does not mean your property is live. [Tell if you are live or in simulation](@86) shows where to look for that.

The heading **Pricing Rules**, with the **Get suggestions from my data** button beside it. Under that, a filter (**All**, **Enabled**, **Disabled**), a closed panel called **How rules behave** that holds two short animations, and the list of your rules with columns **Name**, **Fired**, **Conditions**, **Room Types**, **Price Change** and **Status**, plus a **Delete** button on each row. At the bottom, **+ Add a rule** opens the rule builder. Read [Build your first rule](@30).

Make up a night and see what your rules would do to it. Its intro says so, and adds that nothing here is saved and no rate reaches your property system. Five panels run down the page:

1. **The night**: a stay date, and a booking speed to pretend.
2. **Your rooms**: each room type that counts as a room, with a **Base price**, **Occupancy** and **Picked up** you can change. Its **Guardrails** are its floor and ceiling: no rule can take its price below or above them.
3. **Rules in play**: your real rules, switched-off ones included, each with a checkbox to leave it in or out of the test.
4. **+ Build a test rule**: a draft rule to try alongside them.
5. **What would happen**: the result for each room type.

**Save This Rule** adds the draft to the Rules tab switched off. Read [Trying rules out in the Rate Simulator](@43).

The latest pricing runs, newest first: about the last 50 minutes (the 10 most recent runs, about five minutes apart). The button at the top right toggles between **Show All Cycles** and **Show Changes Only**. Changes only is the default, so runs that changed nothing are hidden until you ask. Each run lists up to 40 changes, one per room type and night, biggest moves first, each with a sentence saying which rule acted and why. The detail behind every change is kept for 90 days. For a change older than the runs on screen, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) within those 90 days and we look it up for you. Booking speed changes carry a **How did we know?** button. A **Your corrections** panel under the heading collects any past nights you have set aside as not a fair comparison. Read [The change log](@46).

Under the connection is the **Room types** section. Each room type has a **Counts as a room** checkbox (untick a meeting room or a spa slot, and it leaves the occupancy count and the room count you are billed for) and a **+ Rooms out of service** link where you note units you have taken off sale for a stretch, so occupancy counts only what you can sell. Nothing is sent to your system. Read [The PMS tab: connection health](@52) and [Room types and rooms out of service](@51).

One checkbox: **I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy**. You see it when you create an account, when you accept an invitation, and once more whenever a new version is in force. MAYA records who ticked it, when, where in the app and from which browser, plus your IP address everywhere except when you create an account directly. The Terms are at get-maya.com/terms and the Privacy Policy at get-maya.com/privacy.

Every agreement in the app goes through the same box. Its text is "I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy", with the two document names as links. Both open in a new tab, so reading them never loses what you typed into the form. The box starts unticked, and the button under it stays greyed out until you tick it.

The two verbs are deliberate. The Terms of Service are a contract between your business and Modern Hospitality Solutions, so you agree to them. The Privacy Policy is a description of what happens with data, not a bargain, so you acknowledge that you have seen it. The wording is the same in every place the box appears.

| Moment | What you see |
|---|---|
| Creating an account at maya-rms.com/login | The box under the password fields. **Create Account** is greyed out until it is ticked. |
| Creating an account after **Connect App** in Cloudbeds | The same box on the same form. |
| Accepting a team invitation | The box on the "Set your password" page. **Set password & continue** waits for it. |
| A new version of the Terms or Privacy Policy is in force | A screen headed "Before you continue", once, over whatever page you opened. |
| Starting checkout with nothing on file | The same "Before you continue" screen, and checkout carries on by itself once you tick it. |

When a new version of either document is published, every signed-in person is asked once. The screen shows the MAYA logo, the heading "Before you continue", the box, a **Continue** button that reads "Saving..." while it saves, and a small **Sign out** link for anyone who would rather not accept right then.

It never covers the sign-in page or the invitation page, which carry their own box. When you tick and continue, the screen goes away and you are exactly where you were going. Nothing navigates.

Three messages can appear on it:

- **"The terms have been updated. Reload the page to see them."** You left a tab open across a new release, so the wording on your screen is older than the version MAYA would record. Reload the page and the current text and version load.
"The terms have been updated. Reload the page to see them."

- **"We couldn't save that just now. Please try again."** The record could not be written. Try once more. If it keeps failing, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Terms%20screen).
"We couldn't save that just now. Please try again."

- **"Not signed in"** means your session ended before the tick was saved, for example because you signed out in another tab. Press **Sign out** under the button, sign in again, and the screen asks once more.

**Good to know: Why you might be asked twice** · If MAYA cannot check whether your acceptance is on file, it lets you through and asks again later. A property is never locked out of its pricing by this record. So an occasional second ask means the check could not be made at that moment, not that your first tick was lost.
"Not signed in"

When you tick the box, MAYA records:

- Your email and account.
- The version number of the Terms and of the Privacy Policy you saw.
- Where it happened: creating an account, claiming a Cloudbeds property, accepting an invitation, or the "Before you continue" screen.
- The property, where there is one (a Marketplace claim records it against each property you claimed).
- Your browser's identifying string.
- Your IP address, when you claim a Cloudbeds property, accept an invitation or use the "Before you continue" screen (it is not recorded when you create an account at maya-rms.com without coming from the Marketplace).
- The time.

A second click, a retry, or the same tick from another tab writes nothing extra. The Privacy Policy describes the same record in its own words.

Your card is stored and may be charged for room-count changes (Terms 7.6)." On a yearly plan it says "every year". "Charged for room-count changes" refers to the room count check described on [Your room count and what you pay](@59): if your property system shows more rooms than you pay for and you do not set the count yourself within 7 days of being told, MAYA raises it and the difference lands on your next invoice.

For Mews, the dialog also says, above that line: "MAYA doesn't send rates to Mews yet, so nothing is sent. The hotel only shows as live." That is what happens. | A discount with free days in front | "14 days free, then 20% off for your first 3 months." |

The price panel re-prices as you type: the list price is struck through, the discounted first invoice stands beside it, and a line says how long it lasts and what follows. [Setting up payment](@8) shows the panel.

A code is 3 to 40 characters: letters, digits and dashes. Capitals do not matter. The field upper-cases as you type. MAYA checks the code a moment after you stop typing ("Checking…" appears), and checks it again if you switch between **Monthly** and **Yearly**, because a limited discount is worth a different number on a yearly invoice.

You can check a code up to 20 times in 10 minutes. After that: "Too many code attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again."

Each message means one thing.

- **"We don't recognize that code"**, followed by a suggestion to check it for typos. The code does not exist as typed. Compare it letter by letter with what you were sent.
"We don't recognize that code"
- **"That code has been turned off."** We have withdrawn it. Email us.
"That code has been turned off."
- **"That code has expired."** Its end date has passed.
"That code has expired."
- **"That code has already been used the maximum number of times."** It had a limit and the limit is reached.
"That code has already been used the maximum number of times."

- **"This property already used that code."** One code, one property, once. This includes restarting a cancelled subscription, because the old code is spent. This one does not show under the field: it appears in a red box above the pay button after you press it.
"This property already used that code."

- **"Your session expired"**, followed by a prompt to sign in again. Your sign-in ran out while the screen was open. Sign in and come back. Nothing you typed on the screen is kept, so type the details again.
"Your session expired"

- **"Couldn't check that code"**, with a suggestion to try again. MAYA could not reach the code check. Wait a moment and type the last character again.

A required field left empty shows no message. The pay button stays greyed out until a code is accepted.

A typed code is always checked, even when the field is optional. A mistyped code stops checkout rather than being ignored, so you never find out on your card statement that a discount did not apply.
"Couldn't check that code"

They never stack. On a Marketplace property, a code that carries free days replaces the 7-day trial with its own number of days. A code that carries a discount and no free days keeps the 7-day trial and discounts the invoices that follow it. A code cannot be added after checkout. If you have one, type it before you pay, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Code%20after%20signup).

On **Yearly** you pay once a year, so MAYA reshapes some discounts to fit that one invoice. What happens depends on the kind of discount.

- **A percentage for fewer than 12 months** is spread over the year. "20% off your first 3 months" is taken as 5% off your first year (20% of 3 months is 5% of 12), and the green line ends "which is the same saving."
A percentage for fewer than 12 months
- **A percentage for 12 months or more, or for as long as you stay,** is not changed.
A percentage for 12 months or more, or for as long as you stay,

- **Dollars off for a set number of months** becomes the whole total, taken once off your first yearly invoice, however many months the code covers. "$25.00 off your first 3 months" is taken as $75.00 off your first invoice. $25.00 off for 24 months is taken as $600.00 off the first invoice only, and the green line says so.
Dollars off for a set number of months

- **Dollars off for as long as you stay** becomes 12 months' worth off every yearly invoice: $25.00 a month is $300.00 off each year. The green line still reads "$25.00 off every month, for as long as you stay."

**Example: The Harbour Inn with a 3-month code**

The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms, so $110 a month. A code for 20% off the first 3 months makes the first three invoices $88 and the fourth $110. On **Yearly** the same code makes the first year $1,254 instead of $1,320, which is the same $66 saving, and the second year $1,320.
Dollars off for as long as you stay

The redemption is recorded when your checkout completes. MAYA connects to one property system per property. Cloudbeds: connect from the Cloudbeds Marketplace or from inside MAYA, and MAYA reads your bookings and sends prices back. ThinkReservations: connect from inside MAYA, and MAYA reads and sends. Mews: we connect it for you, and MAYA reads your bookings and shows prices but sends nothing to Mews yet. Any other system: not yet.

Your property system is where your bookings and your rates live. MAYA reads bookings from it about every five minutes, runs your rules, and (for Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) sends the prices that changed back to it. This page says which systems work today, what each one can do, and what to expect if yours is not on the list.

|  | Cloudbeds | ThinkReservations | Mews |
|---|---|---|---|
| How you connect | From the Cloudbeds Marketplace, or from inside MAYA | From inside MAYA | We connect it for you |
| Free trial without a code | Yes, for Marketplace arrivals (7 days) | No | No |
| A code may be needed | Only when you create your account at maya-rms.com rather than arriving from the Marketplace | Yes, a code may be needed | Not applicable (we set it up) |
| What MAYA reads | Bookings, room types, rate plans, property name, time zone, currency | Bookings, room types, rate types, property name, time zone, currency | Bookings and room categories |
| What MAYA sends | One nightly price per room type | One nightly price per room type | Nothing yet |

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds is the complete path. Install MAYA from the Cloudbeds Marketplace with one click, or sign in with your Cloudbeds account from inside MAYA after paying. MAYA reads your bookings, room types, rate plans and property details. Once you go live, it writes one nightly price per room type to that room type's base rate. Read the full [Cloudbeds page](@12).

**Mews:** Mews is read-only for now. We connect it for you with keys from Mews, and arrange a secure way to share them. MAYA reads bookings and room categories every few minutes and shows what your rules would do, but it sends nothing to Mews. There is no history import for Mews yet. Read the full [Mews page](@14).

When a property is live, MAYA sends the prices that changed to your property system every cycle, for tonight and the next 59 nights. One number goes to one rate per room type. Your system's own derived rates, channels and booking engine follow from there by its own rules. On Cloudbeds, MAYA also asks Cloudbeds to let it know if the app is uninstalled. MAYA never sends anything else: no bookings, no availability, no minimum stays, no close-outs. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15) for the full list.

Until you go live, no price is sent. Every property starts in simulation, where MAYA runs your rules and writes down what it would have sent. Read [simulation mode](@53).

- **About every five minutes**, MAYA reads new and changed bookings from your system, runs your rules over the next 60 nights, and (when live) sends the prices that changed. A very large first read can take a few cycles to finish.
About every five minutes
- **Once a day**, MAYA re-reads the whole booking window, so a booking that was missed in between is picked up within the day.
Once a day
- **Nothing to install.** You sign in on your system's own website (Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations), or we enter your keys (Mews). Nothing runs on your computers.
Nothing to install

- **Your password is never seen by MAYA.** Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations hand MAYA a token that lets it read and write on your behalf. If prices stop updating after you change your password there, a General Manager or Hotel Admin can reconnect from the **PMS** tab.
Your password is never seen by MAYA

- **One connection per property.** MAYA holds one property system per property. There is no screen for a second one.

**Good to know: Nothing to open on your network** · MAYA talks to your system's online service directly, over the internet, the same service its own website uses. There is nothing to install on a front-desk computer and nothing to open or allow on your network.
One connection per property

Booking history works the same way. The bookings MAYA has already read stay with the property, filed under your old system's room types. MAYA reads bookings only from the system it is connected to (and has no history import for Mews yet). It cannot read a system you have left, or a file. So older bookings that live only in a system you no longer use are not read. Read [how much history you need](@1#how-much-history-you-need).

These systems are on the roadmap on get-maya.com: StayNTouch, Little Hotelier, WebRezPro, Opera Cloud, ResNexus and Maestro. No dates are promised for any of them, or for sending prices to Mews.

If you run one of them, join the waitlist on get-maya.com. The waitlist asks only for your email, so also [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Notify%20me%20when%20my%20system%20is%20ready) with the name of your system, and we will tell you when it is ready.

Opera Cloud is on that roadmap. Older Opera versions, Guesty and any other system not named here are not supported today and are not on the roadmap. MAYA cannot read bookings from a spreadsheet or a file. It needs a live connection to one of the three systems above.

**Not yet: Not yet** · Two systems on one property, a system not named above, and a spreadsheet or file import are not possible today. For a second property on a different system, email us and we will set it up as its own property in MAYA.

Cloudbeds sends availability and restrictions (such as minimum stays) with your room types and nightly rates, and guest names with bookings. MAYA uses none of them and keeps none of them. It never asks for room blocks, allotments or other guest details.

A few Cloudbeds details:

- Bookings count when **Confirmed**, **Checked In**, **Checked Out** or **Confirmation Pending**, even before they are given a room. **Cancelled** and **No Show** come off on the next read.

- The **booking date** is the one Cloudbeds reports. MAYA does not shift it to another time zone.
- A **virtual room type** is read like any other. If it makes your room count too high, you can untick **Counts as a room** for it on the **PMS** tab. Unticking it also stops bookings made on that room type counting towards occupancy and booking speed. If guests book it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Cloudbeds%20virtual%20room%20type) before you untick it.
- **Blocked rooms** are not read. Record them under **Rooms out of service** on the **PMS** tab.

Once you go live, MAYA sends the prices that changed every cycle, for tonight and the next 59 nights, to each room type's **base rate**. Plans that follow it (derived plans, such as a non-refundable rate at 10% off) move by Cloudbeds' own rules. MAYA never writes to any other plan and never creates one.

**Example: Which of my Cloudbeds rate plans will MAYA change?**

1. **Does the plan follow another plan?** MAYA never writes to it. It follows its parent.
2. **Does it have a public name, like a package or a promotion?** MAYA never writes to it.
3. **Neither?** Then it is the base rate, and MAYA changes it.

At The Harbour Inn, Standard has "Standard Rate" (the base), "Non-refundable" (follows it at 10% off) and "Bed and Breakfast" (a package). MAYA writes to "Standard Rate" only.

A room type with no base rate is priced on the calendar but not sent, and the change log says "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Cloudbeds, so its rates can't be changed". Once you add one, the held prices go out on a later cycle. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@56).

**Careful: MAYA sends the number as it is** · MAYA reads and writes the same rate field. If your base rate includes tax, so do MAYA's prices. MAYA does not add or remove tax.

MAYA never writes bookings, availability, restrictions, minimum stays, close-outs, taxes, room types or settings, and never sends a price of 0 (set a comp night to 0 in Cloudbeds yourself). The "write reservations" permission MAYA asks for when you connect from inside MAYA is never used.

You disconnect in Cloudbeds, under **Marketplace**, then **My Apps**. If you uninstall MAYA in Cloudbeds, Cloudbeds usually tells MAYA within seconds and the connection reads **Disconnected**. Disconnecting does not cancel your subscription, so if you are leaving, cancel on the **Billing** page first.

To reconnect, a General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the **PMS** tab and signs in at Cloudbeds. Rules, history and settings are untouched. MAYA never sees your Cloudbeds password, so after a password change, reconnect only if prices stop updating.

Do not sign in there. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Cloudbeds%20reconnect).

When the person who connected MAYA leaves

Connect from inside MAYA after paying: pick **Think Reservations**, sign in on their site, and you are brought back. MAYA reads your bookings, room types and rate types, and sends nightly prices to your Best Available rate type. ThinkReservations accepts each price and applies it shortly after. MAYA reads your rates back within about an hour to check the price landed.

ThinkReservations connects from inside MAYA and receives prices, so a ThinkReservations property gets the full path: the history import, starter rules, the calendar, going live and sending. This page covers how to connect, what MAYA reads, which rate type it writes to, and what works differently from Cloudbeds, including how you connect, room counts, how a send is checked, and how a disconnect or a reconnect shows up.

There is one way in. You create your MAYA account, pay, and then connect. ThinkReservations has no marketplace listing for MAYA, so there is no free trial without a code, and a code may be needed at checkout. Read [codes and the free trial](@9).

1. **Create your account and pay.** At checkout, choose **Think Reservations** as your system. If the code field is required, enter the code we gave you.
2. **On the screen titled **Connect your property system**, click **Connect →** beside Think Reservations.** The card says **Sign in with your Think Reservations account**. There is nothing to copy and nothing to set up on the ThinkReservations side.

3. **Sign in on ThinkReservations' website and approve.** MAYA asks ThinkReservations for permission to read your bookings, rooms, rates and availability, to write rates, and to stay connected without asking you to sign in again. It does not ask for guest details. Finish within 15 minutes. If it takes longer, you land on a page headed "Think Reservations connection failed" that says "think does not support marketplace-initiated connections." Nothing is wrong: the sign-in link had run out. Go back to the connect screen and start again.
4. **You are brought back to MAYA.** MAYA names the property from ThinkReservations, reads its time zone and currency, and starts the history import. If a property with that name already exists on MAYA, a "(2)" is added. You can rename it in the questions step. Read [the history import](@23).

**Good to know: One permission MAYA asks for but does not use** · The list ThinkReservations shows you includes reading availability. MAYA asks for it but makes no availability call today. It never reads how many rooms are free on a night, and it never changes availability. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

- **"Think Reservations needs an access code to connect. Use the system you signed up with, or get in touch and we'll sort you out."** You paid without a code, because the system you chose at checkout did not need one, and ThinkReservations does. Any code used at checkout counts, whichever system you chose there. A code can only be entered at checkout, so [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Access%20code%20for%20ThinkReservations) and we sort you out.
"Think Reservations needs an access code to connect. Use the system you signed up with, or get in touch and we'll sort you out."
- **"Payment is needed before connecting a PMS."** The subscription has not gone through yet. Go back to the payment screen and finish it.
"Payment is needed before connecting a PMS."

- **A page headed "We hit a snag connecting your property"** with the reason and a **Try again** link. Most reasons end in "Try again in a moment." and mean exactly that. Read [messages you might see, explained](@103).
A page headed "We hit a snag connecting your property"

If your ThinkReservations login can reach several hotels, the connect step stops with "This Think Reservations login covers 3 properties. MAYA signs one property up at a time right now" (with your own number) and no **Try again** link. MAYA cannot tell which of them you paid for, and picking one could price the wrong hotel. Reply to your receipt or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20group) and we set the properties up by hand, each as its own property in MAYA. There is no group flow for ThinkReservations yet.

On every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA reads from ThinkReservations:

- **Bookings** made or changed since the last read. A booking that holds several rooms arrives with one entry per room. MAYA keeps each room's room type, its nights, and its nightly room charge.
Bookings

- **Room types**, by name. MAYA does not read how many rooms each type has yet (see below).

About once an hour, MAYA reads your **rate types** (their names, whether each is standard or follows another, and which room types each covers) and your **own nightly rates** for the next 60 nights from the rate type it sends to. Once a day it re-reads the whole booking window, so a booking missed in between is picked up within the day.

At connect, MAYA reads the property's **name, time zone and currency** once. They are not refreshed afterwards. If you change your time zone or currency in ThinkReservations later, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone%20or%20currency) and we change it in MAYA.
Room types

The **booking date** is the moment ThinkReservations recorded the booking, read on your property's own calendar. A booking made at 11 pm at a property in California is dated that day, not the next.

ThinkReservations sends guest details with every booking even though MAYA does not ask for them. MAYA drops them before anything is stored: names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, dietary notes, arrival times and special requests never reach MAYA's database. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

MAYA keeps a booking when ThinkReservations lists it as **scheduled**, **checked in** or **checked out**. A booking marked **cancelled** or **no show** is removed on the next read, and its nights come off the count. Cancelling changes the booking, so the cancellation arrives in the same five-minute read as everything else.

Nights run from check-in up to, but not including, check-out. A same-day booking is one night. Each room in a booking is one booked room on each of its nights.

For occupancy, each room counts. For booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. A 4-room booking for one night is 4 booked rooms and 1 booking. Read [booking speed](@34).

MAYA does not read your room counts from ThinkReservations yet, so it uses one number for every ThinkReservations room type at your property, and that number starts at 100. The **Room types** block on the **PMS** tab shows "100 units" beside each one.

That changes what occupancy reads. Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell, so with 100 in the bottom half of the fraction, a full house reads as a fraction of full. Occupancy rules will not fire the way you expect, and booking window rules that also check occupancy will not either.

Booking speed counts bookings, not rooms. But the similar past nights it compares with come from your seasons, and your seasons are read partly from how early past nights filled, measured against the room count. So while the count is wrong, your seasons can be off, and booking speed can compare a night with the wrong past nights.

We can change that number for you. It stays one number for the whole property, and it goes to every ThinkReservations room type alike. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20count) your counts whatever they are. If every room type has the same number of rooms, we set that number and occupancy is right from the next run. If they differ, we set the average: occupancy over the whole property then reads close, but one room type on its own reads wrong. So write occupancy rules that measure every room type, and lean on booking speed and booking window rules.

MAYA's room count for your bill uses the same number, once for each room type ticked as a room. Read [your room count and what you pay](@59).

**Careful: Expect a room count email** · Until we set your room count, MAYA measures 100 rooms for every room type, so a property with three room types is measured at 300 rooms, and you will likely get a room count email. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) your counts on day one, and reply to that email, so we can sort out your billed count before the 7 days pass.

A separate count for each room type is not possible for ThinkReservations yet, and there is no field in MAYA for you to set the number yourself.

**Example: One number for three sizes of room at The Harbour Inn**

The Harbour Inn has 12 Standard rooms, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suites. On Fri, Nov 13 2026, 9 Standard and 5 Deluxe rooms are booked. With the real counts, Standard reads 75% full and Deluxe 83%.

If we set the number to 12, Standard reads 75%, which is right. Deluxe gets 12 as well and reads 42%, and Suite, with 2 rooms, is read as 12. No single number is right for 12, 6 and 2. So we set the average, 7: the three add up to 21 rooms, close to the real 20, and a rule that measures all three reads close to the truth. A property whose room types all have 8 rooms reads right with 8.

**Rooms out of service** still works the same way: 3 rooms out of service come off whatever the count is.

ThinkReservations marks each rate type as standard or as following another rate type (derived). MAYA sends its prices to your **Best Available** rate type: the standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available". A rate type called "Best Available Non-Refundable" has those words too, and MAYA may write to it instead, so give exactly one standard rate type a name with "Best Available" in it.

If no rate type is called Best Available, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. That could be a non-refundable or a package rate type, because ThinkReservations marks those standard too. If two standard rate types tie for that, neither is used, and nothing is sent until one of them is named Best Available. A room type the chosen rate type does not cover is not sent to. MAYA never hands a room type's price to a non-refundable or package rate type instead.

Derived rate types reprice themselves from their parent by ThinkReservations' own rules, so writing the Best Available rate is the whole job. A non-refundable rate that follows Best Available at 10% off moves when MAYA moves Best Available. MAYA never writes to a derived rate type and never creates a rate type. A non-refundable or package rate type is written to only when it is the one chosen above, so name your main rate type Best Available.

**Example: Which of my ThinkReservations rate types will MAYA change?**

For your property, ask in this order:

1. **Is there a standard rate type called Best Available?** If yes, that is the one MAYA changes, for every room type it covers.
2. **If not, which standard rate type covers the most room types?** If exactly one does, MAYA changes that one.

At The Harbour Inn, "Best Available" covers Standard, Deluxe and Suite. "Non-Refundable" follows Best Available at 10% off. "Romance Package" is a package. MAYA writes each room type's price to Best Available. Non-Refundable follows on its own. Romance Package is untouched.

If no rate type MAYA can send to covers a room type, that room type is priced on the calendar but not sent, and the change log shows a "Rates not reaching Think Reservations" entry: "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed", with the action "Add a base rate for this room type in Think Reservations." Add the room type to your Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. MAYA re-reads your rate types and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@56).

ThinkReservations does not apply a price the instant it receives it. It answers "accepted" and applies the price shortly after, and there is no job for MAYA to ask about afterwards, as there is with Cloudbeds. So MAYA checks by reading. About once an hour it reads your rates from ThinkReservations, and a send counts as landed when that read finds MAYA's price there.

Until a send has been read back, a rate you change in ThinkReservations on that night is not kept as a manual price, because MAYA cannot yet tell your change from a price of its own that has not landed. Once the send has been read back and is at least 60 minutes old, a rate you change there is kept, exactly as on Cloudbeds. Read [rates you change in your property system](@50).

If ThinkReservations accepts a batch and then never applies it, MAYA's calendar shows MAYA's price while ThinkReservations still holds the old one. The next time that night's price changes, MAYA sends it again. Nothing is sent again at the same price on its own. If a night in ThinkReservations still shows the old rate an hour after MAYA's calendar changed, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20rate%20not%20applied) the night and room type and we check it.

**Careful: A price of 0 is never sent** · MAYA does not send a price of 0 to ThinkReservations. A night you set to 0 in MAYA is a comp night that you set to 0 in ThinkReservations yourself. The save says so: "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Think Reservations, so set the night to 0 there yourself."

If ThinkReservations lets MAYA read but refuses the write, the change log shows "Think Reservations won't let MAYA change Standard rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates", with the action "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Think Reservations, then reconnect on the PMS tab." Reads, pricing and the calendar carry on. The held prices go out on the cycle after you reconnect.

A refused write never disconnects a ThinkReservations property. The connection stays up, and only the sending waits.

ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA when access has been removed. MAYA reads the refusal when its next call fails. A failed read is tried again with a growing wait, up to an hour between tries, and nothing is priced or sent while reads fail. When ThinkReservations refuses to renew MAYA's access, the **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab reads **Error** and the banner "MAYA has lost its connection to Think Reservations" appears for a General Manager or Hotel Admin, with a **Reconnect Think Reservations** button. Until the status changes, the tab can still read **Connected** while calls are failing. If prices have stopped and the tab still reads **Connected**, a General Manager or Hotel Admin can click the quiet **Reconnect Think Reservations** link on the **PMS** tab anyway. Which ThinkReservations login you sign in with matters, so read the next paragraph first.

To reconnect, click **Reconnect Think Reservations** on the banner or on the **PMS** tab, sign in on ThinkReservations' site with a login that reaches this hotel and no other, and you are back on the dashboard. Your rules, history and settings are untouched. Finish signing in within 15 minutes. If it takes longer, you see the "Think Reservations connection failed" page described under Connecting. Nothing has changed: start again from the **PMS** tab. Syncing resumes within about five minutes, or up to an hour if reads had been failing for a while. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).

If **Last sync** stops moving after a reconnect, reconnect again with a login that reaches only this hotel. If your only login reaches several hotels (we set those properties up by hand), or you signed in to another hotel by mistake, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20reconnect) and we sort it out.

MAYA has no disconnect button of its own. To remove MAYA's access in ThinkReservations, cancel your subscription first, then [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20ThinkReservations) and we walk you through it.

The **Connection** card and **Last sync** are right for ThinkReservations. The **Recent requests to Think Reservations** table stays empty today, and the **Health (last 24 hours)** card reads **No recent activity**, because only calls to Cloudbeds are written to that log. It does not mean syncing has stopped. **Last sync** is the number to look at. Read [the PMS tab](@52).

The Harbour Inn's Best Available rate for Standard is $150 on Fri, Nov 13 2026. That night is booking faster than similar nights did, so the starter rule "Warm-date bump" raises Standard 10%, from $150 to $165. (It is a booking speed rule, which counts bookings rather than rooms, so it can fire whatever the room count is.) On the next cycle, MAYA sends $165 to Best Available for that night. ThinkReservations answers "accepted" and applies it a moment later. The Non-Refundable rate, which follows Best Available at 10% off, now shows $148.50 in ThinkReservations without MAYA touching it.

Mews is read-only for now, and costs the same as any other property. We connect it for you with keys from Mews. MAYA reads your bookings and room categories about every five minutes and shows what your rules would do on the calendar and in the change log, but it sends nothing to Mews. There is no history import for Mews yet, so there are no starter rules at connect.

With Mews, MAYA is a place to write rules and watch them run against your real bookings, without any price reaching Mews. It is useful for trying rules out. Here is what a Mews property does not have yet: sending, your own rates, a room count for each room category, the history import and a connect screen you can use yourself. This page says exactly what a Mews property gets today.

|  | Mews today |
|---|---|
| Connect from inside MAYA | Not yet. We connect it for you |
| MAYA reads your bookings | Yes, about every five minutes |
| MAYA reads your room categories | Yes, by name |
| MAYA reads how many rooms each category has | No. One number, set with us, is used for every category |
| MAYA reads your own rates | Not yet |
| History import and starter rules at connect | Not yet |
| Rules, calendar, change log, Rate Simulator | Yes |
| Going live | No go-live button (there are no starter rules). Email us |
| Prices sent to Mews | Not yet, including prices you type |

The screen titled **Connect your property system** lists Mews under **Coming soon** with the label **Not yet available**. You cannot click it. Instead, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Connect%20Mews) after you pay and we connect Mews for you.

Mews connects with keys rather than a sign-in. One key identifies MAYA and we hold it, so you never need to find a client token. The other is an access token for your property, which Mews creates when your property is connected to MAYA. If your Mews account covers more than one enterprise, we also need this property's Enterprise ID.

We arrange a secure way to share keys when we connect you, so never paste them into an ordinary email. We test the keys against Mews, save them, and mark the property as connected. MAYA only ever talks to Mews' own service, and nothing is installed on your computers.
Every property starts in simulation, and for Mews it stays effectively that way, because nothing is sent either way. Read [simulation mode](@53).

A Mews property pays the same as any other property: the same price per room, in the same brackets, monthly or yearly. There is no lower price while nothing is sent to Mews. Read [what it costs](@3).

You pay before we connect Mews, and you pick **Mews** on the payment screen. A code may be needed: the field reads **Your code** when one is required and **Your code (optional)** when it is not.

There is no free trial for Mews. The trial (7 days) comes only with the Cloudbeds Marketplace. So unless a code gives free days, your first charge is when you finish checkout. Read [codes and the free trial](@9).

On every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA reads from Mews:

- **Bookings** (Mews calls them reservations) made or changed since the last read, with their room category, arrival and departure, and total price.
Bookings

- **Room categories** (Mews' name for room types), by name. MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for all of them (read below).

Once a day, MAYA re-reads the whole window: 30 days back and about 13 months ahead. A booking missed in between is picked up within the day.

The **nightly rate** MAYA stores comes from the booking's total price. MAYA adds up the charges on the booking and splits the total evenly across its nights, so a 3-night stay at $450 is stored as $150 a night, even when its nights were charged at different prices. That total includes taxes, and it can include extras on the booking as well as the room, so it can sit above your room rate.

The **booking date** is the moment Mews recorded the booking as created, read on your property's own calendar.
Room categories

MAYA removes a booking only when Mews marks it **Canceled**. Every other state it reads counts as a booked room: **Confirmed**, **Started**, **Processed**, and also **Optional**, **Enquired** and **Requested**. So an option held for a group, or an enquiry not yet firm, counts towards occupancy and booking speed exactly like a confirmed booking.

If you hold many options that never firm up, occupancy and booking speed read higher than your firm bookings. There is no setting in MAYA for this yet. Cancelling an option in Mews takes it off the count on the next read. Mews records a no-show as a cancelled reservation, so a no-show comes off the count like any cancellation.

A Mews booking is one room, so one booking is one booked room on each of its nights and one booking for booking speed. Nights run from arrival up to, but not including, departure.

MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for every category at your property. We set that number with you when we connect Mews. The **Room types** block on the **PMS** tab shows it as "units" beside each category.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell, so this number is the bottom half of every occupancy figure. It is right for a category that has exactly that many rooms and off for every other. A rule that measures several categories adds their numbers together. Booking window rules that also check occupancy depend on it too.

**Example: One number for The Harbour Inn's room categories**

The Harbour Inn has 12 Standard, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suite rooms, and a Meeting Room that is unticked as not a room. On Mews, every category gets the same number, but the Meeting Room adds nothing because it is unticked. With 100, a night with 9 Standard rooms booked reads 9% full for Standard, and "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80) does not fire. With 7, the three room categories add up to 21 rooms, close to the real 20, so a rule that measures all three reads close to the truth. A rule that measures Standard alone then reads 9 booked of 7, which is 129%, and fires on a night that is not full.

Prices you type are saved and shown on the calendar the same way, and they are not sent either. In simulation the line after a save reads "Saved (simulation: not sent to Mews)." On a property we have set to show as live, it can read "Saved. Sending to Mews now." or "Saved. Sending to Mews on the next cycle (about 5 min)." Nothing is sent to Mews whatever that line says. If you want a price in Mews, set it there yourself.

Because nothing is sent, nothing is ever read back either. A rate you change in Mews is never shown as "Changed in Mews" and never kept as a manual price.

No date is promised for sending prices to Mews. To hear when that changes, join the waitlist on get-maya.com, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Sending%20prices%20to%20Mews) and we will tell you.

MAYA does not read your rate plans from Mews, so it has no "your own rate" for a night. A night's starting price is a price you typed for it, else the nightly rate of the newest booking on that night for that room category, else the starting price that night had last time. A future night with no bookings yet and no earlier starting price is not priced at all until one arrives. Read [how rules run](@39).

**Example: The Harbour Inn on Mews**

The Harbour Inn's newest Standard booking for Fri, Nov 13 2026 was taken at $150 a night. "Busy nights" fires and the night goes to $165. The calendar shows $165 and the change log names the rule. Mews still shows whatever rate The Harbour Inn has set there. Sam types $175 for that night in MAYA. The calendar shows "Manual · $175.00", and Mews is still unchanged. To sell at $175, Sam sets it in Mews.

Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations properties get a history import at connect, a review of what MAYA found, and starter rules built from that history. Mews does not have that yet. A Mews property's history is what the reads cover: 30 days back at connect, growing by a day each day. If you would like us to read further back once, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20history) and we can read up to a year back. Read [the history import](@23).

**Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab runs a fresh history import as well, so it does not work for a Mews property yet. Build your rules in the rule builder. Read [build your first rule](@30).

If your Mews keys stop working, MAYA's reads fail quietly. Nothing on screen warns you: the **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab still reads **Connected**, and no banner appears above the calendar. The sign to look for is **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab, which stops moving.

MAYA keeps trying, less often after each failed read, until it tries about once an hour. While reads fail, nothing new is priced. Your rules, history and settings are untouched, and the first read that works catches up on everything that changed in between.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys) and we arrange new keys with you and save them. Leave the keys themselves out of the email: we set up a secure way to share them. There is no button for this in MAYA.

When we remove the keys, the **Connection** card reads **Disconnected** and reads stop. The **PMS** tab and the banner above the calendar then show "Mews needs its keys re-entered", with the words "Send us a message and we'll walk through it". A Revenue Manager or Viewer sees "MAYA has lost its connection to Mews" instead. That panel says reconnecting takes one click. For Mews it does not: email us and we arrange new keys with you. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).

The **Connection** card changes only when we save or remove your keys, so it can read **Connected** while reads are failing. The **Recent requests to Mews** table stays empty today and the **Health (last 24 hours)** card reads **No recent activity**, because only calls to Cloudbeds are written to that log. **Last sync** is the number to look at. **Counts as a room** and **Rooms out of service** work the same as on any property. Read [the PMS tab](@52).

Cancel on the **Billing** page, then [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20Mews) and we remove the keys, so MAYA no longer reads from Mews. Nothing in Mews was ever changed by MAYA, so there is nothing to put back. Your rules and settings stay in MAYA. Read [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@61).

**Not yet: Not yet** · For Mews there is no sending (including prices you type), no read of your own rates, no room count per room category (one number is used for all), no warning on screen when the keys stop working (watch **Last sync**), no history import and no starter rules at connect, no **Get suggestions from my data**, no go-live, connect or reconnect from the app (email us), and no way to leave options and enquiries out of the count. No date is promised for any of these.

MAYA reads your bookings (nights, room type, nightly rate, booking date), your room types (and, on Cloudbeds, how many rooms each has), your rate plans, and your property's name, time zone and currency. It writes only one nightly price per room type to one rate plan (on Cloudbeds, MAYA also asks Cloudbeds to let it know if the app is uninstalled). On Mews it does not copy your rate plans or property details, and it writes nothing. It never stores guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses or card details.

This page is the full list, for anyone who needs to answer "what exactly does MAYA touch?" before connecting, or who wants to check afterwards. Where the three systems differ, the tabs say how. The short version: MAYA reads the shape of your bookings and your rates, and it writes nightly prices. Everything else in your system is yours alone.

**Cloudbeds:** About every five minutes: bookings made or changed since the last read, with every room in the booking and each room's own nightly rate, and your room types with the number of units in each.

About once an hour: your rate plans, with each room type's own nightly rate for the next 60 nights from its base rate plan.

Once a day: the whole booking window again, and your taxes and fees (Cloudbeds requires the request, but MAYA keeps none of it and uses none of it).

Once, at connect: the property's name, time zone and currency, and which properties your login covers.

Arrives but is never used or kept: availability and restrictions (minimum stays, closed to arrival or departure), which come with your room types and nightly rates, and guest names, which come with bookings.

**ThinkReservations:** About every five minutes: bookings made or changed since the last read, with each room and its room charges, and your room types by name. MAYA does not read room counts from ThinkReservations yet, so it uses one number for every room type (100 until we change it). Occupancy is exact only when your room types are the same size.

About once an hour: your rate types (name, standard or derived, which room types each covers) and your own nightly rates for the next 60 nights from the rate type MAYA sends to.

Once a day: the whole booking window again.

Once, at connect: the property's name, time zone and currency, and which hotels your login covers.

**Mews:** About every five minutes: bookings made or changed since the last read, with their room category, arrival, departure and total price, and your room categories by name. MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for every category.

Once a day: the whole window again.

Once, at connect: your property's details, only to check the keys work. MAYA keeps none of them. We set the property's name, time zone and currency with you.

Never asked for: your rate plans, availability, restrictions or guest details. Guest fields that come with a booking are dropped before anything is stored. Read the [Mews page](@14).

**Mews:** Nothing. MAYA does not send prices to Mews yet, including prices you type.

Until you go live, no price is written. Every property starts in simulation. Read [going live](@54).

MAYA never creates, changes or cancels a booking. So when a rule raises or cuts a night's price, guests who have already booked keep the rate they booked at. The new price is for bookings made after it reaches your system. MAYA never changes availability, so it cannot cause an overbooking. It never changes restrictions, minimum stays, close-outs, taxes, room types, rate plans or property settings. It never sends a price of 0. Read [how prices reach your property system](@55).

**Good to know: Two permissions asked for but never used** · When you connect Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, the permission list includes writing reservations. When you connect ThinkReservations, it includes reading availability. MAYA asks for both and uses neither. Nothing in MAYA creates, changes or cancels a booking, and nothing uses how many rooms are free on a night.

Simulation is the read-only way to use MAYA. Every property starts in it and stays in it until a General Manager or Hotel Admin goes live. In simulation MAYA reads your system and runs your rules. The results show on the calendar and in the change log, and no price is sent. On Cloudbeds, the only thing written is the notification subscription, set up when you connect. Read [simulation mode](@53).

MAYA has no read-only connection. When you connect Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, or connect ThinkReservations, the permissions it asks for include changing rates, because it needs that once you are live.

For each room in a booking, MAYA keeps one line per night: the night, the room type, the date the booking was made, the days between the two, and that room's nightly rate. It also keeps a short record of the booking's shape: its reference in your system, its status, its dates, how many adults and children, and the channel it came from. Where your system sends them, the record also holds the room the booking was given and the rate plan it was booked on. On ThinkReservations it also keeps the booking's subtotal, tax and total amounts. No price is worked out from these amounts. Bookings read by the history import keep no record at all beyond the line per night.

MAYA never stores guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, notes, dietary or special requests, payment details or loyalty numbers. Where your system lets MAYA choose, it does not ask for them: MAYA never asks Cloudbeds for guest details, and never asks ThinkReservations for customer records. Where they arrive anyway (a guest name on a Cloudbeds booking, a customer block on a ThinkReservations booking, a Mews booking's guest fields), MAYA keeps only the fields on a short list and drops the rest before anything is stored. A new field your system adds is dropped by default.

The same promise is in the [Privacy Policy](https://www.get-maya.com/privacy) and the [Terms](https://www.get-maya.com/terms). Read [privacy, security and your data](@108).

MAYA reads your rate plans for two reasons: to find the one plan per room type it writes to, and to read your own nightly rates from that plan about once an hour. Your own rate is what a rule starts from on a night MAYA has not sent to yet. Read [how rules run](@39).

MAYA writes to one plan per room type and never to any other.

- **Cloudbeds**: the room type's base rate, the plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Derived plans (a non-refundable rate at 10% off, say) follow the base by Cloudbeds' own rules, so they move when MAYA moves the base. Packages, promotions and long-stay plans are never written to. Read [which rate plan MAYA changes in Cloudbeds](@12#what-maya-writes-the-base-rate).
Cloudbeds

- **ThinkReservations**: your Best Available rate type, the standard rate type with "Best Available" in its name. If no rate type has that name, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. Derived rate types reprice themselves from it. A non-refundable or package rate type is written to only if it is the one chosen, so give exactly one standard rate type a name with "Best Available" in it. Read [which rate type MAYA sends to in ThinkReservations](@13#which-rate-type-maya-sends-prices-to).
ThinkReservations

- **Mews**: none.

There is no setting to choose a different plan, in MAYA or with us. On Cloudbeds, it follows from how your plans are built. MAYA writes to the base rate, so a plan you want to move with MAYA's prices should follow the base rate.

On ThinkReservations, it follows from the name. MAYA sends to the standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available", so you choose by giving that name to the standard rate type you want (and to no other). MAYA reads your rate types about once an hour, so a renamed rate type is picked up within about an hour.

MAYA never creates a rate plan or a rate type. Set up any new rate structure in your system first. If a room type has no plan MAYA can write to, it is priced on the calendar and not sent, and the change log says so. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@56).
Mews

MAYA writes $165 to Standard Rate for Fri, Nov 13 2026. Cloudbeds moves Non-refundable to $148.50 on its own. Bed and Breakfast stays where it was. Your booking engine and channels read Standard Rate as they always have.

On Cloudbeds, MAYA asks for your taxes and fees once a day, because Cloudbeds requires it of pricing tools like MAYA. MAYA keeps none of it and uses none of it. No price is worked out from your taxes, and nothing about tax is sent. If your property has not given MAYA permission to read them, Cloudbeds turns the request down and MAYA carries on as normal.

On ThinkReservations and Mews, MAYA does not read your tax settings at all. A ThinkReservations booking does arrive with its own tax amount. MAYA keeps it with the booking and works out no price from it. Read [what a stored booking looks like](#what-a-stored-booking-looks-like).

MAYA reads and writes the same rate field in your system, so prices come out on whatever basis your base rate is on. If your base rate in Cloudbeds is entered with tax included, MAYA's prices are with tax included. If it is entered without, so are MAYA's. The same holds for ThinkReservations. MAYA does not add or remove tax, and it shows you the number it works with.

The time zone matters more than it looks: the calendar, the 60-night window, the booking window and every "past week" count run on it. Read [time, weekends, currency and holidays](@105).

Cloudbeds reports the number of rooms in each room type, and MAYA re-reads it on every cycle, so a wing you open shows up on the next read. MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for every Mews room category, which we set with you when we connect (100 until then). MAYA does not read room counts from ThinkReservations yet either, so it uses one number for every ThinkReservations room type: 100, until we change it for you. On both, the number cannot differ by room type, so occupancy is exact only when your room types are the same size. The count is what sellable occupancy divides by and what your bill is based on. Read [room types and rooms out of service](@51) and [your room count and what you pay](@59).

**Not yet: Not yet** · MAYA does not use, keep or write availability or restrictions on any system (on Cloudbeds they arrive with your room types and nightly rates and are dropped).
