MAYA sends each room type's price to one rate plan, its base rate, and never to any other. Rates that follow the base rate move on their own by your system's rules. Packages and named promotional plans are left alone. If a room type has no base rate MAYA can send to, nothing is sent for it. Once you are live, the change log says so for that room type. Before you go live the change log says nothing about it, because nothing is sent in simulation. So check your rate plans by hand with the steps below.

**Cloudbeds:** For each room type, look at its rate plans in Cloudbeds and ask, in this order:
1. **Does the plan follow another plan?** Cloudbeds calls this derived. If yes, MAYA never writes to it.
Does the plan follow another plan?
2. **Does the plan have a public name?** Packages, promotions and long-stay plans do. If yes, MAYA never writes to it.
Does the plan have a public name?

3. **What is left?** The one plan that follows nothing and has no public name is the base rate. That is the one MAYA changes.

Once you are live, a room type with only derived plans is reported in the change log as "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because that rate follows another rate plan", with the action "In Cloudbeds, give this room type a base rate of its own that doesn't follow another plan." A room type with only packages is reported as "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Cloudbeds". Fix it in Cloudbeds. MAYA re-reads your rate plans and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Before you go live neither message appears, so ask the three questions above for every room type yourself.
What is left?

Once you are live, a room type not covered by that rate type is reported in the change log as "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed", with the action "Add a base rate for this room type in Think Reservations." Add the room type to Best Available. MAYA re-reads your rate types and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Before you go live this message does not appear, so check in ThinkReservations that Best Available covers every room type you want priced.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read or write Mews rate plans. Nothing to set up.

Your rules run on tonight and the next 59 nights, starting from the rate you keep in your system for each night. About once an hour MAYA reads that rate from your base rate plan.

A night whose rate in your system is 0 reads as closed: your rules leave it alone and nothing is sent for it, unless you have typed a price for it in MAYA. So if you close a night by setting it to 0 in your system, also clear any price you typed for it in MAYA. Otherwise MAYA may keep your typed price and send it once you are live.

A night with no rate loaded at all starts from the newest booking's rate for that night when there is one, otherwise from the starting point used the last time your rules ran on that night, and is otherwise left unpriced. So before you go live, load a rate on the base rate plan for every night you sell in the next 60. Nights further out are read as they enter the window.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. MAYA divides by the units of every room type ticked as a room, minus rooms out of service. So two things need to be right: which types count, and how many units each has.

**Which types count.** Your system lists every bookable thing as a room type, so a meeting room, a car park or a spa slot can appear. Untick **Counts as a room** for anything nobody sleeps in. It can still be priced. On the review, a room type whose name has a word like Meeting, Conference or Parking is already unticked. Any room type whose name or bookings do not read like a bedroom's (a name like Spa or Tennis Court, or only one-night bookings when your other rooms get longer stays) gets a card asking whether it is a room. Room types added after your first history read arrive ticked, so untick any that are not rooms on the **PMS** tab. Read [room types and rooms out of service](@51).
Which types count

**How many units.**

**Cloudbeds:** The units come from Cloudbeds on every read, so there is usually nothing to do. A virtual room type (one that sells rooms from another type) counts like any other, with the units Cloudbeds gives it, so your count can read higher than the rooms you have. Unticking it takes out its units, but also leaves out any bookings Cloudbeds records on it. If you sell one, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Virtual%20room%20type) before you untick it, and we check which room type its bookings are counted under.
How many units

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations does not report units. MAYA uses one number for every ThinkReservations room type at your property. It starts at 100, so the **PMS** tab shows "100 units" beside each room type. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20count) your room counts and we change that number, but it stays one number shared by every room type. If your room types are all the same size, occupancy reads right from the next run. If they differ, we set the average: whole-property occupancy reads close, and occupancy for one room type is off. Email us even if your sizes differ, because the room count you are billed for is checked against this number, and 100 for each room type can raise your bill. A count for each room type is not possible yet.

**Mews:** Mews does not report room counts, so every room category gets the one number we set with you when we connect. If your room categories are all the same size, occupancy reads right. If they differ, we set the average: whole-property occupancy reads close, and occupancy for one category is off. The room count you are billed for is checked against this number, so 100 for each category can raise your bill. Check the units on the **PMS** tab. If they read 100, or look wrong, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts).

MAYA does not read room blocks, out-of-order rooms or allotments from any system. A room you have blocked in your system still counts as sellable in MAYA until you record it under **Rooms out of service** on the **PMS** tab: the room type, from and to dates, how many units, and an optional reason. Those units come off the sellable count for those nights only. Nothing is sent to your system for that.

An allotment held for a group without bookings is invisible to MAYA. It neither reduces the sellable count nor counts as bookings. If a block matters to your pricing, record it as rooms out of service.

Try what a block does to a rule. Set 12 rooms, 3 out of service and 8 booked, and see how an occupancy rule reads.

Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.

MAYA never writes to any of these, so leave them as they are:

- Availability, restrictions, minimum stays, closed to arrival or departure, and close-outs.
- Bookings, guests and payments.

On Mews, a starting price taken from a booking includes tax (and can include extras on the booking). A price you type is used as you type it. MAYA does not add or remove tax.
- Room types and property settings.
- Rate plans other than the base rate. Derived plans follow it by your system's own rules. MAYA never creates a rate plan.

MAYA reads your bookings about every five minutes, your own rates about once an hour (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations), and the whole booking window once a day. A new booking, a cancellation, a date change or a room move shows in MAYA on the next read. A rate you change in your system is read within the hour. Blocked rooms, allotments and restrictions are not read at all, and property details are read once, when you connect, and never again (on Mews, we set them with you).

Three clocks set how soon a change in your system reaches MAYA. This page names them, then lists every change you can make and which clock it rides on. Where a system is different, its tab says so.

| Clock | What is read | How often |
|---|---|---|
| The cycle | Bookings made or changed since the last read, and your room types | About every five minutes |
| The rates read | Your own nightly rate on the base rate plan, for tonight and the next 59 nights, and your rate plans | About once an hour, or when your hotel day changes (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only) |
| The daily re-read | Every booking in the window, 30 days back and about 13 months ahead | Once a day |

"Next read" below means the next cycle, up to about five minutes on a healthy connection. "Within the hour" means the next rates read.

**Cloudbeds:**

| You do this in Cloudbeds | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a booking | Next read. A booking waiting in the unassigned list counts too |
| Cancel a booking, or mark it no-show | Next read. Its nights come off the count |
| Change a booking's dates | Next read. New nights are added and dropped nights removed |
| A guest checks out early (stay shortened) | Next read, once Cloudbeds shows the shorter stay. The nights it no longer covers count as free rooms again. If the booking still shows the old check-out date, MAYA still counts those nights as booked |
| Move a booking to another room type | Next read. The room's row gets the new room type |
| Confirm a Confirmation Pending booking | Nothing changes. Both count as booked |

**ThinkReservations:**

| You do this in ThinkReservations | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a booking | Next read |
| Cancel a booking, or mark it no-show | Next read. Cancelling changes the booking, so it arrives with everything else |
| Change a booking's dates | Next read. New nights are added and dropped nights removed |
| A guest checks out early (stay shortened) | Next read, once ThinkReservations shows the shorter stay. The nights it no longer covers count as free rooms again. If the booking still shows the old check-out date, MAYA still counts those nights as booked |
| Move a booking to another room type | Next read |
| Change a rate on a night MAYA has never sent to | Within the hour, and always before MAYA's first send to that night. Your rate becomes the night's starting point |

**Mews:**

| You do this in Mews | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a reservation, an option, an enquiry or a request | Next read. Every state but Canceled counts |
| Cancel a reservation | Next read. Its nights come off the count. Mews records a no-show as a cancelled reservation, so a no-show comes off too |
| Change a reservation's dates | Next read |
| A guest checks out early (stay shortened) | Next read, once Mews shows the shorter stay. The nights it no longer covers count as free rooms again. If the reservation still shows the old departure date, MAYA still counts those nights as booked |
| Move a reservation to another room category | Next read |
| Confirm an option | Nothing changes. Both count as booked |
| Change a rate | Not read. MAYA does not read Mews rates |
| Add a room category | Next read, with the one number set for your property's categories |

Three kinds of booking people ask about:

- **An extended stay or a date change.** The added nights belong to the same booking and keep the date it was first made. They count as booked rooms from the next read, but for booking speed they are an old booking, so they rarely show in **Past day** or **Past week**.
An extended stay or a date change

- **A day-use booking** (in and out the same day). It is not skipped. In ThinkReservations and Mews it counts as one night on its date. In Cloudbeds it counts on each date Cloudbeds lists a room rate for, so on its date when Cloudbeds lists one. Either way it reads as a booked room that night.
A day-use booking

- **A comp, house-use or owner stay at $0.** It counts by its status, like any booking: a booked room for occupancy and a booking for booking speed. It adds $0 to the calendar's revenue and lowers the ADR. Read [Comp, house-use and day-use bookings](@22#comp-house-use-and-day-use-bookings).
A comp, house-use or owner stay at $0

A test booking counts like any other booking while it is in your system. What happened depends on whether a read found it before you cancelled it:

- **Cancelled before the next read** (within about five minutes). The read finds it already cancelled, so it is never counted and no price moves.
Cancelled before the next read

- **Still there at a read.** It counts as a booked room and a new booking on its nights, and your rules run with it on that cycle. The next read after you cancel it takes it off the count.

If your rules ran with it, here is what happens to what they did:
Still there at a read

- **A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions** follows the count. A change that needed the test booking comes off on the cycle that reads the cancellation, and a change it was holding back can now happen.
A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions
- **A booking speed or pickup raise** comes off only when enough of the bookings behind it cancel, and one test booking may not be enough. Read [When a price change comes off](@40).
A booking speed or pickup raise

- **A cut from a booking speed or pickup rule** never comes off by itself.

In simulation nothing was sent. If you are live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, a price it moved was sent like any other (nothing is ever sent to Mews). To put a night straight back, type the price you want on the calendar. Read [Undo a price change](@66).

To test without moving any price, book a night more than 59 nights ahead and cancel it straight away. Your rules run on tonight and the next 59 nights only.
A cut from a booking speed or pickup rule

From any system: availability by night, room blocks, out-of-order rooms, allotments, restrictions, minimum stays, closed-to-arrival flags and closed-to-departure flags. Guest details that come with a booking are dropped before anything is saved. It reads your property's name, time zone and currency once at connect and never again (on Mews, we set them with you). Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

- **A large property's first read** can take several cycles. Each cycle reads for a fixed slice of time and carries on from where it stopped. Until the whole window has been read, your rules run on what has arrived and nothing is sent.
A large property's first read
- **A failing connection** is tried again with a growing wait, up to an hour between tries. Nothing is priced or sent on a cycle where the read failed, so bookings are never priced on stale data.
A failing connection
- **If your system keeps asking MAYA to slow down**, MAYA waits a minute or two before calling it again, and sends move to a later cycle.
If your system keeps asking MAYA to slow down
- **Nights 60 or more days out** (past tonight and the next 59) are neither read for rates nor sent until they enter the window.
Nights 60 or more days out

- **A rate you change within an hour of MAYA's send** is not yet kept as yours, and MAYA's next price for that night can write over it. Wait an hour after a send before changing that night's rate by hand, or type the price in MAYA instead. Read [rates you change in your property system](@50).
A rate you change within an hour of MAYA's send

**Not yet: Not yet** · There is no button to read your system right now. The cycle runs on its own about every five minutes. Blocks, allotments and restrictions are not read from any system. Time zone, currency and name are read once. ThinkReservations room counts are never read, and every ThinkReservations room type has the same count. Mews rates are never read.

Your system and MAYA use different words for the same things. MAYA's base rate is one of your rate plans (Cloudbeds) or rate types (ThinkReservations): the one per room type that MAYA writes to. A Cloudbeds reservation, a ThinkReservations reservation and a Mews reservation are all bookings in MAYA. A Cloudbeds room type, a ThinkReservations room type and a Mews room category are all room types in MAYA. This page is the translation table.

| MAYA says | Cloudbeds says | ThinkReservations says | Mews says | What it means in MAYA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Booking | Reservation | Reservation, holding one booking per room | Reservation, one room each | A stay. For occupancy each room counts. For booking speed a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. On Mews every room is its own reservation, so rooms booked together count once per room |
| Room type | Room type | Room type | Room category, space category or resource category | The kind of room a price is set for. Your rules set one price per room type per night |
| Units | Units | none (not reported) | none (not reported) | How many rooms a room type has. MAYA divides by it for sellable occupancy. On ThinkReservations and Mews it is one number for every room type, 100 until we set it with you |

On ThinkReservations, each rate type is standard or derived (it follows another). A package or a non-refundable rate can be standard too. MAYA writes to the standard rate type whose name contains Best Available. If none has that name, MAYA writes to the one standard rate type that covers the most room types, even if it is a package. If two tie, MAYA writes to neither. Name your main rate type Best Available and MAYA leaves your packages alone.

Your system marks each booking with a status. MAYA keeps some and removes others.

**Cloudbeds:**

| Cloudbeds status | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Confirmed | Counts as booked |
| Checked In | Counts as booked |
| Checked Out | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Confirmation Pending | Counts as booked. It holds a room, and Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts it |
| Cancelled (Cloudbeds spells it "canceled") | Removed on the next read |
| No Show | Removed on the next read |

Two more Cloudbeds words: a booking in the **unassigned** list (not yet placed on a physical room) counts as a booked room, and a **virtual room type** (one that sells rooms from another type) is treated like any other room type.

**ThinkReservations:**

| ThinkReservations status | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Scheduled | Counts as booked |
| Checked in | Counts as booked |
| Checked out | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Cancelled | Removed on the next read |
| No show | Removed on the next read |

ThinkReservations holds one **booking** per room inside a **reservation**. MAYA keeps each room's nights and room charge, and for booking speed the reservation counts once.

**Mews:**

| Mews state | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Confirmed | Counts as booked |
| Started | Counts as booked (the guest is in the house) |
| Processed | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Optional | Counts as booked |
| Enquired | Counts as booked |
| Requested | Counts as booked |
| Canceled | Removed on the next read |

Only Canceled removes a booking. An option, an enquiry or a request counts like a confirmed booking until it is cancelled in Mews.

Each Mews reservation holds one room. A guest who books three rooms has three reservations in Mews, so for booking speed that stay counts as three bookings. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations the same stay counts once. MAYA does not read Mews reservation groups.

**Complimentary, house-use and owner stays.** A booking counts by its status, not its rate. A comp or house-use booking at $0 counts as a booked room for [sellable occupancy](@32) and pickup count, and as one booking for booking speed, like any other. On the calendar it adds $0 to the night's revenue, so it lowers the ADR. There is no setting to leave $0 bookings out.
Complimentary, house-use and owner stays

**Day-use bookings (in and out the same day).** They are not skipped. In ThinkReservations and Mews, a booking with check-out on its check-in date counts as one night on that date: a booked room for occupancy, and a booking for booking speed. In Cloudbeds, a booking counts on each date Cloudbeds lists a room rate for, so a same-day booking counts on its date when Cloudbeds lists a rate for it. Either way, a day-use room reads as booked that night, even though it can still be sold for the night.
Day-use bookings (in and out the same day)

| Word | Whose | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Marketplace, **Connect App**, **My Apps** | Cloudbeds | Where you install MAYA and where you disconnect it. MAYA has no disconnect button of its own |
| **Sign in with your Cloudbeds account**, **Sign in with your Think Reservations account** | MAYA | The other way in: from the **Connect your property system** screen after paying |
| Access code | MAYA | A code that may be needed at checkout for some systems. Marketplace installs never need one |
| Client token, Access token, Enterprise ID | Mews | The keys MAYA uses to read Mews. We set them up with you |
| Group login | Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations | A login that reaches several properties. Through the Cloudbeds Marketplace it connects all of them. From inside MAYA it is refused |
| **PMS** tab | MAYA | The tab that shows the connection, its health, the last sync and your room type settings. "PMS" is the label. These docs say "property system" |
| **Connected**, **Pending**, **Degraded**, **Error**, **Disconnected** | MAYA | The connection words on the **PMS** tab. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16) |

These have no equivalent in your system.

| MAYA says | What it means |
|---|---|
| Cycle | One run for your property, about every five minutes: read bookings, refresh your rates if due, run rules, send changed prices |
| Window | Tonight and the next 59 nights. The nights your rules price and, once you are live, MAYA sends (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) |
| Sellable occupancy | Rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms and subtracting rooms out of service |
| **Counts as a room** | The checkbox that says a room type is somewhere guests sleep |
| **Rooms out of service** | Units you take off sale for a stretch in MAYA. Your system's blocks are not read |
| Manual price, "Manual · $175.00" | A price you typed for a room type on a night |

For every other product word, read the [glossary](@104).

**Example: One sentence, three vocabularies**

The change log at The Harbour Inn says: "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because that rate follows another rate plan". In Cloudbeds' words: the Deluxe room type's only rate plan is derived. In MAYA's words: Deluxe has no base rate. The fix is the same in both: in Cloudbeds, give Deluxe a rate plan that follows nothing and has no public name. On ThinkReservations the change log shows a different sentence for a room type with no base rate: "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed". The fix there is adding Deluxe to your Best Available rate type.

As soon as your property is connected, MAYA reads your past bookings: your current bookings first, then one year at a time back through up to ten years. You can close the page, because the import runs on its own. The first results (your starter rules and the review) are ready after three past years are in, or once everything is read if you have less than three years. Pricing comparisons reach three years back.

The import starts on its own. You do not press anything.

- **Cloudbeds, from the Marketplace**: it starts as soon as you create your MAYA account (or sign in) and claim the property, before you have paid. By the time you reach the payment screen it is usually already running, and paying does not start it over.
Cloudbeds, from the Marketplace
- **Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, from inside MAYA**: it starts the moment your connection succeeds.
Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, from inside MAYA

- **Mews**: there is no history import for Mews yet. See the Mews tab below.

You can start a fresh read later from the **Rules** tab with **Get suggestions from my data**. That read makes suggestions only and changes nothing on its own. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

**Good to know: A login that covers several properties** · If you came from the Cloudbeds Marketplace and your login covers several properties, MAYA reads one unpaid property at a time. Choosing **Not now** for a property pauses its import where it is, and it carries on from the same place when you come back to that property. From inside MAYA, a Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations login that covers several properties cannot connect yet, so nothing is imported: [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20login) and we will set them up.
Mews

The progress bar names each step as it goes. In order:

1. **Reading your property setup.** Your time zone and currency (only where MAYA has nothing yet), and your room types with how many units each has. The import never changes your property's name.
Reading your property setup

2. **Reading your current bookings.** The same read MAYA makes about every five minutes from then on: bookings from 30 days ago to about 13 months ahead. For a large book this takes several passes, and the bar says so: "Reading your current bookings (part 2)".
Reading your current bookings

3. **Importing past years.** One 365-day stretch at a time, going backwards from where the current read started. Up to ten stretches, so at most about ten years. It stops earlier when a year comes back empty.
Importing past years

4. **Building your starter rules.** After the first three past years are in, MAYA reads what it has so far and writes the review cards, sets floors and ceilings that were still at their defaults, and builds your starter rules. From here the bar reads "First results ready. Importing older years", and the review can open while the rest loads.
Building your starter rules

5. **Checking your full history.** Once every year is in, MAYA reads everything again. This pass refines the review cards: it can sharpen a card, add one, or take one away. With less than three years on record, step 4 is skipped and this is the only read, so your first results come once all of your history has been read.
Checking your full history

6. **Import complete.**

**Good to know: Why three years first** · Every comparison MAYA makes for pricing (similar past nights, seasons, the checks behind a "Not a fair comparison?" answer) reaches at most three years back. So three years is the smallest history on which the review and the starter rules work as they will with the full import.
Import complete

For each past stay night MAYA keeps six things: the booking's reference number from your property system, the stay date, the room type, the nightly price, the date the booking was made, and the number of days between the two. The reference number is how a booking with several rooms counts as one booking in booking speed.

It keeps nothing about the guest. No names, no emails, no card details. For past stays nothing else about the booking is stored, only those six fields. What MAYA keeps about your current and future bookings is covered in [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).

There is no fixed time, and MAYA does not promise one. It depends on how much history your property system holds and how quickly that system answers. A small property with two years of bookings finishes far sooner than a 200-room property with ten.

The import runs on our side in short bursts and picks itself up again between them, so it does not need your browser open. Close the page, come back later, and the progress bar shows where it got to.

Two things you may see on a large book:

- "Reading your current bookings (part 2)", "(part 3)" and so on. One pass was not enough to cover the window, so it is taking another.
- A very large history can stop before ten years. MAYA reads up to a set number of room nights (one room for one night), and the limit grows with the size of your property.

You can. Here is what to expect:

- The dashboard fills in as the import goes. Your current bookings arrive in step 2, so the calendar shows real occupancy early on, while older years are still loading.
- Your rules run during the import. About every five minutes MAYA runs them over tonight and the next 59 nights and writes the result in the **Change Log** tab. A run that changes nothing writes one line, "Prices checked".
- Your property starts in simulation, so no rule, starter or yours, changes anything in your system until you go live.
- With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, MAYA also reads the rate you already have for each night, about once an hour, and your rules work from it. Mews rates are not read.

The progress bar sits under the five questions and on the progress page. It shows the current step on the left and, on the right, how many room-nights have been read and, once an oldest stay is known, "back to" that month (for example "back to 2019-03").

The dot beside the step pulses while the import runs, turns green when it is complete, and turns amber if it has stopped.

The progress page adds three tiles: **Room-nights**, **Years covered** (the span between your oldest and newest stay, at least 1) and **Oldest stay**. It moves on by itself: to the review as soon as there is something to review, or to the dashboard if the import finished with nothing to review. If the work was already done when you arrived, it moves on straight away. Otherwise it waits a moment so you can see it finish.

If the bar reads "Import stopped" with an amber dot, the import gave up: your property system stopped answering for a long stretch, or a read kept ending in the same place. It will not restart on its own.

The screen says we have been told, but nothing reaches us automatically. Please [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Import%20stopped) so we can restart it for you. Your connection, your rules and everything already read are safe.

If your connection drops while the import runs, the dot turns amber, the bar keeps the name of the step it had reached, and the reconnect prompt appears on your dashboard. Read [Reconnect and disconnect](@16).

A Cloudbeds Marketplace property is the exception. If you pay for it (a free trial counts), clicking **Connect App** for MAYA in the Marketplace again picks the import up where it left off. If you have not paid yet, it picks up when the property next comes up on the payment screen.

The prompt takes the bar's place in one case only: a Cloudbeds Marketplace property you never paid for, left unused for 180 days, whose connection was removed (see [Reading again later](#reading-again-later)).

When the read has run, you have:

- your room types with their unit counts, and MAYA's first proposal for which of them are rooms,
- the review cards: closures, room types that may not be rooms, duplicates, rates that look like typos, stays with no rate, stays that point at deleted room types,
- floors and ceilings for room types that were still at their defaults,
- five starter rules, if you have enough history and no rules yet.

Your property's own rates (the starting point your rules work from) are not part of the import. The regular cycle reads them once your property is paid for. A free trial counts.

Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26), [Your starter rules](@27) and [Floors and ceilings](@28).

- **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab reads your whole history again and turns what it finds into cards you accept or reject one by one. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).
- A Cloudbeds property from the Marketplace that never paid may have its booking history removed after 180 days without use. When you come back, reconnecting starts a fresh import, and nothing is priced until it completes. Your rules and settings are kept.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA reads each booking with every room in it, each with its own room type and nightly rates. Every booking status is read. Confirmed, checked-in, checked-out and not-yet-confirmed stays are kept. Cancelled and no-show bookings are left out, and a booking cancelled since an earlier read has its nights removed.

A few Cloudbeds accounts refuse the detailed booking read. MAYA then reads a plainer list for your past years. From that list, a past booking's nightly price is an average of its total, and a past booking with several rooms may be counted as one room. The list holds only the kept stays, so a past booking cancelled since an earlier read keeps its nights. Current bookings are read in full either way.

ThinkReservations does not report how many rooms a room type has. MAYA gives every room type the same number of rooms, 100 until we change it, so occupancy reads low until then. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20count) your counts. Once we have set the number, occupancy is right from the next run if your room types are all the same size. [ThinkReservations](@13) has the details.

**Not yet** · There is no button to start, pause or restart the import by hand. It starts when you connect, and the only later re-read is **Get suggestions from my data**. If the bar says "Import stopped", or the dot is still amber after you reconnect, email us.

Hold My Hand asks five optional questions and walks you through what MAYA found in your history. Let Me Drive skips the questions and the guided review and takes you straight to the calendar. The import, the starter rules and the review cards happen either way. A dashboard banner links to the review while cards wait for your answer, and maya-rms.com/onboarding/review opens it any time.

Once your property is paid for and connected, the onboarding page shows two large buttons and nothing else.

- **Hold My Hand**, with "(Recommended)" beneath it.
- **Let Me Drive**. When you hover over it, or reach it with the keyboard, a note fades in. On a touch screen the note is always shown. It ends "For experts only."

Whichever you press reads "One moment…" while your choice is saved. If the save fails you see "Something went wrong. Please try again."

**Good to know** · Whatever the note under **Let Me Drive** says, MAYA reads your history on both paths.

You go to [the five questions](@25), one card at a time, with the import's progress bar underneath. Every question can be skipped.

After the last question (or **Skip the rest →**), MAYA takes you to the review if the first results are in and there is something to look at. Otherwise it takes you to the progress page, which moves you on to the review by itself once there is something to review.

On the review you check what MAYA found, tick which room types are rooms, see your starter rules, and can go live. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).

You go straight to the dashboard. The import keeps running in the background, so the calendar fills in as you look at it. Your starter rules are still built and switched on in simulation, floors and ceilings are still filled in from your history, and the review cards are still written.

When there are cards waiting for your answer, a blue banner appears at the top of your dashboard with a **Review →** link. That is the same review screen Hold My Hand walks you to.

If the import built starter rules but found nothing to ask you about, there is no banner. Open the review at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review, or find the starter rules on the **Rules** tab, switched on in simulation.

The five questions are not asked. Without them, your floors and ceilings come from your own rates instead of from your answers. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

|  | Hold My Hand | Let Me Drive |
|---|---|---|
| The history import | runs | runs |
| The five questions | asked, all optional | not asked |
| Review cards (closures, room types, typos) | walked through | written, waiting on the review screen |
| Starter rules | built, on, in simulation | built, on, in simulation |
| Floors and ceilings | from your answers, then your history | from your history |
| Where you land | the review, then the dashboard | the dashboard |

Your choice is recorded for you and for the property. It does not change how rules run, what is sent, or what you pay.

There is no button to switch paths, and you do not need one. Both guided screens stay open to you:

- The review opens any time at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. The dashboard banner links to it only while cards wait for your answer and you have not pressed **Finish** since the newest one arrived. Read [the banner on your dashboard](@26#the-banner-on-your-dashboard).
- The five questions open any time after your property is connected, at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions.

If you chose Hold My Hand and closed the tab part way through, nothing is lost. Your next sign-in lands on the dashboard. If cards are waiting for your answer, the banner brings you back to the review. If there is no banner, open the review by its address.

Sam connects The Harbour Inn on a Tuesday evening, presses **Let Me Drive**, and lands on the calendar with the next 60 nights already filling in. On Wednesday morning a banner at the top of the dashboard reads "We found 3 things worth a quick look". Sam clicks **Review →**, confirms one closure, presses **Not a room** on the Meeting Room card, and sees the five starter rules waiting in simulation. Nothing about Tuesday's choice held any of that back.

Five optional questions, one card at a time: your property's name, what a room turnover costs you, the lowest rate you would take on a dead Tuesday, the most you would charge when the town is full, and how you want your current pricing treated. The name renames your property, and the turnover cost only shapes the floor question. The lowest rate becomes every room type's floor, and the highest becomes the ceiling of each room type whose rates read so far fit under it. The last question is not used for anything yet. Careful: saving the floor, ceiling or last card again puts your saved floor back on every room type, over any floor set since.

The questions come after you press **Hold My Hand**. Each one is a card. Across the top you see "A few quick questions · 1 of 5 · all optional" and a **Skip the rest →** link. Under the cards sits the import's progress bar, because your history is being read while you answer.

Every card has a **Skip this question** link. A money card shows a **Continue** button once you have typed a number above zero. Press it, or press Enter in the box. While an answer saves, the button reads "Saving…".

Money amounts show your property's currency: "$" for US dollars, otherwise the currency code and a space, for example "EUR ". Whatever you type is rounded to two decimal places.

The card asks "Did we get your property's name right?" and shows the name MAYA read from your property system. Leave it and press **Looks right**, or type a better one.

A name you type wins. It renames the property everywhere in MAYA, and a later read of your system never puts the old name back.

If another property on MAYA already uses that name, the card says the name is already taken and suggests adding your city or neighbourhood.

"Ballpark: what does it cost you to turn over a room?" Cleaning, laundry, utilities and supplies for one night's stay, as a rough number. The placeholder suggests 35.

This number does one thing: it sets where the next question starts. It is saved with your answers and nothing else reads it. It is not a floor, and it never reaches a price.

The card reads "Picture a Tuesday in your slowest month. You're at 10% occupancy." and offers a rate: would you take this much for a room tonight, from someone walking in off the street? Two buttons: **I'd take $50** (the amount changes) and **Too low**.

The first offer is a little above your turnover cost ($40 if you skipped that question), and each **Too low** raises it by at least 15%, rounded up to the next $5. After two **Too low** presses a reminder appears: a night like this would otherwise earn nothing, so anything above your turnover cost is profit.

If you would rather name the number, press **I'll just type my floor**. The card changes to "What's your true floor?" with a money box.

A $35 turnover cost offers $50, then $60, $70 and $85.

**Careful** · Your answer goes to every room type, the Suite included. If your room types need different floors, answer with your cheapest room type's floor and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) to raise the others. Once you have answered, the import fills in only ceilings.

If you skip this question, the import works each room type's floor out from its own rates instead: about 40% of what it usually sells for. It does that only for a room type with at least 30 nights of history. A room type with less, or one whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom, stays at $1.00. To give it a floor, answer this question or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling).

The card opens "Now the fun one" and asks you to imagine the biggest concert of the year next door, with every room in town gone. What is the most you would charge for a night? The card also asks you to bear in mind the highest you have ever actually sold a room for, as a reference point. It does not show that number. The placeholder suggests 450.

What the answer does: it becomes the ceiling of each room type whose highest rate read so far is at or below your number. A ceiling is the highest price MAYA will publish for that room type. A room type whose rates read so far go above your number keeps its ceiling as it was.

"Read so far" matters, because you answer while the import is still reading. The check uses only the rates read by the moment you save, and a room type with no rates read yet gets your ceiling.

Once the progress bar reads "Import complete", check the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab. If a ceiling pins a room type down, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Lift%20a%20ceiling) and we will lift it.

Answer with a number above your floor. If you type a ceiling under the floor you gave, the card still moves on. That ceiling is not written to any room type, and nothing on screen tells you.

To fix it, open maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions to reopen the questions. Answer the ceiling question with a higher number, or the floor question with a lower one.

The last card asks how you want your current pricing treated, with two choices: the card that begins "My pricing works" (keep doing what you do, without touching it every day) and "Find money I'm leaving on the table" (show me what the data says).

What the answer does: nothing in MAYA today. It is saved with your answers, and nothing reads it yet. The card's small print says it tunes suggestions. It does not do that yet.

Saving it does one more thing: it writes your saved floor and ceiling answers to your room types again, as if you had answered those questions again. Your floor goes back on every active room type, and your ceiling on every room type whose rates fit under it. The first time through, that repeats what questions 3 and 4 wrote.

- **Skip this question** moves to the next card and saves nothing for that one.
- **Skip the rest →** ends the questions from any card.
- After the last card, or after **Skip the rest →**, MAYA opens the review if the first results are in and there is something to look at. Otherwise it opens the progress page, which moves you on by itself.

You can reopen the questions any time after your property is connected at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions. The cards do not show your earlier answers (the name card shows the property's current name). A new answer replaces the old one.

**Careful** · Answering only the ceiling question, or only the last one, also puts your saved floor answer back on every active room type, over any floor set since. That includes a floor you accepted from a suggestion card or one we set for you by email. Check the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab afterwards.

If a save fails you see "Couldn't save that" with an invitation to try again. Your earlier answers are unaffected.

The name card shows "Harbour Inn", the name Cloudbeds holds. Sam types "The Harbour Inn" and presses **Looks right**. Sam types 35 for the turnover cost and sees the first offer, $50. Two presses of **Too low** take it to $60, then $70. Sam has a number in mind for a Standard on a dead night, so Sam presses **I'll just type my floor** and types 80. Every room type gets an $80 floor. Sam skips the ceiling question, so the import sets the Standard, Deluxe and Suite ceilings from their own rates: $300, $400 and $600. On the last question, the bar under the card reads "First results ready. Importing older years". Sam picks the first card and lands on the review. Deluxe and Suite need higher floors, so Sam emails us and we set them to $110 and $180. If Sam ever saves the floor, ceiling or last card again, both go back to $80.

The review is two short screens, and the first checks your data: closures, room types that may not be rooms, duplicate room types, rates that look like typos, stays with no rate, and stays that point at deleted room types. Answer a card to confirm or dismiss it, or skip it and come back later. Only one card reports something already done for you: hiding an empty duplicate room type. You can undo it on the card. The second screen has the room count strip (where room types that are certainly not bedrooms arrive unticked), your starter rules and the go-live button.

The review opens on its own at the end of [the five questions](@25), or from the progress page once there is something to look at. It also opens from the dashboard banner (below), and after **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. You can open it directly at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review.

The cards come from the history import. MAYA reads your history twice on a first import: once after the first three years are in, and again once every year is in. If the review is open when the second read finishes, the cards refresh: one can be sharpened, added or taken away.

Anyone on the property can open the review and read it. Answering a card needs a Revenue Manager, General Manager or Hotel Admin. Below that, pressing any card button shows "Finding was already resolved", and the card stays.

The first screen is headed "First: does this match reality?". It appears only when there are data-check cards waiting. Each card is a question with two buttons, or a single **Got it** when there is nothing to answer.

At the bottom, **Continue to recommendations**. The small print under it says that anything you skip stays available later. That is true: an unanswered card waits for you.

MAYA found at least 14 days in a row with no rooms booked, with the property clearly open in the 30 days before and the 30 days after. Up to three short interruptions (a stray booking, a brief reopening of 14 days or fewer) are bridged into one closure. The stretch before your first ever booking is not a closure, and neither is a gap that runs up to today.

The card shows the two dates and how many straight days it found. Buttons: **Yes, we were closed** and **No, we were open**.

- **Confirm**: those dates are recorded as a closed period for the whole property. From then on they are left out of every comparison MAYA makes: they are never one of a night's similar past nights, and they play no part in how your seasons are read.
Confirm

- **Dismiss**: MAYA never asks about those dates again.

A closure changes nothing about future nights. Your rules still run on every night in the window, closed or not. To keep a future night off sale, close it in your property system.
Dismiss

The same closure at the same time of year in at least two different years (starts within 21 days of each other) becomes one seasonal card, labelled like "mid-December to mid-February" or "all of August". The card says in how many different years the closure appears. The years need not be back to back. Buttons: **Yes, that's our season** and **No, we were open**.

Confirming records every instance it found. When older years reveal more instances of a confirmed season, they are added without asking again. After a **Get suggestions from my data** run, new instances are proposed as a card instead. Dismissing a season means none of its years is asked about again.

Property systems list every bookable space as a room type: event rooms, spa slots, courts, parking. MAYA asks about a type when one of two things is true:

- its name does not read like a bedroom (words like parking, boardroom, meeting, treatment, or a word like spa, court or hall with no bedroom word beside it), or
- it has at least 20 bookings, every one exactly one night, while your property's typical stay is two nights or longer.

A type that is a tiny share of your bookings (under half a percent) at an unusual rate is mentioned as extra weight, never as the reason on its own.

Buttons: **Not a room**, which takes the type out of your counts, and **It's a real room**.

- **Not a room**: the type leaves your sellable occupancy, your RevPAR (revenue per available room: a night's room revenue divided by your rooms, which sets the calendar's colours) and the room count you are billed for. A rule that changes it still prices it.
Not a room

- **It's a real room**: the type is recorded as a room, in your name, and MAYA does not ask again.

Either answer needs a Revenue Manager or higher. Below that, the button shows "Finding was already resolved" and the card stays. You can change the answer any time on the **PMS** tab under **Room types**. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@51).
It's a real room

Two active room types shared the same name once punctuation and capitals are ignored, and one of them had no bookings at all. On a first import MAYA hides the empty one straight away, so it does not sit in your occupancy as rooms you cannot sell. The card records this and adds a line beginning "We already did this for you".

Buttons: **Good call** keeps it hidden. **Undo** makes the type active again.

After a **Get suggestions from my data** run the empty duplicate is only proposed, and nothing is hidden until you confirm.

**Careful** · Once you have pressed **Good call** there is no button to bring the type back, and a later read of your system does not reactivate it. If you need it back, email us.

For a room type with at least 30 nights on record, its single highest rate is far above what the room type normally sells for: about ten times its usual rate or more. The card names the highest rate and the usual (median) rate. Usually it is a test booking or a mistyped rate.

**Example: The exact test, for the curious**

The highest rate must be above 10 times the room type's median rate. Once the type has 200 nights or more, it must be above the larger of 10 times the median and 3 times the rate that 99 in 100 of its stays sold under.

Buttons: **Probably a typo** and **Those are real**. Either answer is recorded and changes nothing else. MAYA never builds a ceiling from a room type's single highest rate.

A mistyped high rate can still matter in one way. The ceiling you gave in the five questions only goes on a room type whose highest rate read so far fits under it. If Suite's $9,999 typo had already been read when you saved a $600 ceiling, your $600 does not go on Suite, whichever button you press here. (If the typo was read only after you saved, Suite got your ceiling like the others.) The **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab shows the ceiling each room type has. Email us with the room type and the ceiling you want. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

More than 2% of the stay nights MAYA imported came through with no rate. Usually comps or gaps in the data. The card says how many. One button, **Got it**. There is nothing to fix, and the card shows "$" whatever your currency.
Some stay nights point at room types your property system no longer has. They still count in your history totals but cannot be priced. The card says how many. One button, **Got it**.

The second screen is headed "Recommendations from your data". The heading's small print promises rules and guardrails your history supports. On a first import there are no cards here: the starter rules and your floors and ceilings are built for you (below), and the box reads "No new recommendations this time." Suggestion cards appear on this screen only after **Get suggestions from my data**. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

When nothing at all is waiting, the box reads "Nothing left to review" and says your data looks clean. Under it, in small text, "N items already handled" counts the cards you have answered.

Then, in order:
1. **The room count strip** (next section).
The room count strip

2. **Your starter rules**, in a box headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules", with the **Turn them on for real** button. The box goes once anyone on your team runs **Get suggestions from my data**, so go live before anyone presses it. Read [Your starter rules](@27) and [Going live](@54).
3. **Finish**, to go to your dashboard. It marks the review as done and opens the dashboard. It reads "Finishing up…" while it works. Marking it done needs a Revenue Manager or higher. Below that, the dashboard still opens, but the review is not marked done and the banner stays.

You do not have to press **Finish**. Close the page whenever you like and everything you answered is kept.
Your starter rules

The strip reads "We're counting 4 room types as rooms" and asks whether anything there is not one. One chip per active room type, with its name and how many units it has. A chip is ticked unless the type has been marked as not a room.

Ticked types are what MAYA divides by for sellable occupancy, and what it counts for the revenue per room behind the calendar colours and for the room count you are billed for. Untick anything nobody sleeps in. An unticked type is still priced if a rule changes it.

- Room types whose name is certainly not a bedroom (parking, boardroom, meeting, treatment and the like) arrive unticked, as MAYA's proposal. Tick one to say it is a room.
- A tick saves at once. There is no confirm, and nothing here holds up **Finish**.

- Thirty changes in ten minutes is the limit, per person. The same thirty also cover prices you type or clear by hand and rooms you take out of service in those ten minutes. Past it you see "That's a lot of room-type changes at once. Give it a minute and try again."
- If a tick fails to save it snaps back and you see "That didn't save" with an invitation to try again.

The "?" beside the strip is the only "?" on the review. Its panel is titled "What counts as a room" and says the same as this section, ending "You can change this any time from the PMS tab."

A blue banner appears at the top of the dashboard when your property is connected, the first results are in, there are cards waiting, and you have not finished the review since the newest card arrived. Its heading says your booking history has been read, the line under it says how many things are worth a quick look, and it ends with the link **Review →**. It shows once per page load. Pressing **Finish** (as a Revenue Manager or higher) clears it until a newer card arrives, for example from the second read of your history.

You can leave the review at any point and come back through the banner or the review's own address.

Answered closure cards, "Is X actually a room?" cards and duplicate cards are not asked again. Cards about typos, $0 rates and deleted room types can come back after **Get suggestions from my data**, because each read is a fresh look. A typo card can also come back at the second read of your first import, if the older years hold an even higher rate for that room type.

What you can still change:

| Card | Change it later? |
|---|---|
| Is X actually a room? | Yes, on the **PMS** tab under **Room types** |
| Were you closed / normally closed | Not yet. Email us |
| Hid duplicate room type | Only before you press **Good call**. After that, email us |
| Rates look like typos | Nothing to change. The answer only records your view |
| $0 rates, deleted room types | Nothing to change |

If a card answers itself with "Finding was already resolved", either a colleague or another tab got there first, or your role is below Revenue Manager, so the card cannot be answered from your login. The list refreshes, and a card you could not answer stays. Read [Messages explained](@103).

If your property has about two months of booking history or more, and no rules yet, MAYA adds five booking speed rules during the import: two that cut a night booking slower than similar nights had, and three that raise a night booking faster. They start switched on, in simulation, so they change nothing in your system until you go live. Turn any of them off, or delete it, from the **Rules** tab.

On the review, a green box headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules" lists each rule with a sentence about what it does, then the **Turn them on for real** button. Read [Going live](@54) for that button. The box goes once anyone on your team runs **Get suggestions from my data**, and the rules stay.

After that they live on the **Rules** tab like any rule you build yourself, with a **Fired** count, an **On** / **Off** switch and a **Delete** button. Every change they make is written in the **Change Log** tab with the rule's name.

Each is a [booking speed](@34) rule. Booking speed compares how many bookings a night received recently with how many similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival, and reads as one of seven levels from Stalled to Surging. The **Conditions** column on the **Rules** tab shows each rule like this:

| Name | Conditions, as the Rules tab shows them (each begins "booking speed") | Price change |
|---|---|---|
| Slow-date rescue | at most Much Slower Than Normal (past month), then waits 1 week | -15% |
| Slow-date trim | Slower Than Normal (past month), then waits 1 week | -7% |
| Warm-date bump | at least Faster Than Normal (past month), then waits 3 days | +10% |
| Hot-week surge | at least Much Faster Than Normal (past week), then waits 2 days | +25% |
| Sudden-spike catcher | at least Surging (past day), then waits 1 day | +25% |

"At most Much Slower Than Normal" means Much Slower or Stalled. "Slower Than Normal" on its own means exactly that level. "At least Faster Than Normal" means Faster, Much Faster or Surging.

When a night is booking far behind similar nights (Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled, over the past month), the rule cuts it 15%. It then waits a week, counts only the bookings made since the night was last cut, and cuts again if those are still that far behind. MAYA asks you once it has cut the same night three times.

When a night is booking a little behind similar nights (exactly Slower Than Normal, over the past month), the rule trims it 7%. It checks again a week after each trim, counting only the bookings made since the night was last cut, and trims again if those are still behind.

When a night is booking ahead of similar nights (Faster Than Normal or more, over the past month), the rule raises it 10%. It waits 3 days, then raises again only if the bookings made since the night was last raised are still ahead. If enough of the bookings behind a raise cancel, the raise comes back off.

When a night's past week runs much faster than similar nights had at the same point (Much Faster Than Normal or more), the rule raises it 25%. It can raise again every 2 days while new bookings keep coming that fast, and MAYA asks you once it has raised the same night three times.

When bookings pour in for a night within a single day (Surging, over the past day), the rule raises it 25%, and can raise again each day while the rush lasts. Your ceiling is the cap, and MAYA asks you once it has raised the same night three times.

A booking with several rooms counts once. A 20-room wedding booking is one booking for booking speed (and 20 booked rooms for occupancy). Only bookings in the room types a rule measures are counted.

Each rule waits after it adjusts a night, per night and per room type. Once the wait is over, the rule does not count the same bookings twice:

- A rule that raises counts only bookings made since the night's last raise, whichever rule made it.
- A rule that cuts counts only bookings made since the night's last cut.
- The similar past nights are read over the same days, so the comparison stays fair.

So one burst of bookings raises a night once, by the one rule that caught it. A stronger rule steps in on top only when the bookings since that raise read faster on their own. A cut rule keeps cutting a night that stays behind, and a raise rule keeps raising while real demand keeps coming.

A raise made by Warm-date bump, Hot-week surge or Sudden-spike catcher comes off when enough of the bookings behind it cancel: the bookings still on the books from the days it counted fall back to what a night like it usually gets. The change log then reads that the rule stopped applying an earlier raise because enough of the bookings behind it cancelled.

A cut never comes off on its own. A night Slow-date rescue cut stays cut until you set a price yourself (in MAYA, or by changing the rate in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations on a night MAYA has sent to), delete the rule, or the night passes. Turning the rule off freezes the cut in place.

Once one of these rules has adjusted the same night three times, an amber banner appears at the top of the dashboard (the Rules that keep adjusting banner). It is headed with a sentence naming the rule and how many times it adjusted, such as ""Slow-date rescue" would have cut 3 nights, 3 times each." While you are in simulation it says "would have cut" or "would have raised". Once you are live it says "has cut" or "has raised".

The banner asks you, night by night: keep adjusting, or stop for this night. Until you answer, the rule keeps going. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@42).

The starter rules measure and change every room type that counted as a room when they were built. A meeting room or court you had unticked is left out of both. They apply every day of the week, with no date range.

A room type your system adds later is not added to them. Build a rule of your own for it.

When two booking speed or pickup rules both want to act on the same night and room type, only one fires per run. Starter rules always rank above rules you build, so on a night where a starter rule and one of yours both match, the starter rule fires first. While it waits and still matches, it holds the night and yours does not fire under it. Yours gets its turn once the starter rule no longer matches.

Among the five, the order is: Sudden-spike catcher, Hot-week surge, Warm-date bump, Slow-date rescue, Slow-date trim. Read [How rules run](@39).

MAYA builds them once per first import, and only when all of these hold:

- at least 60 past nights on record had a booking (about two months of history),
- the property has no rules at all, not even one switched off (someone built a rule before the import finished, or an earlier import left one),
- at least one room type counts as a room,
- the history import ran at all. Mews has no import yet, so no starter rules.

**Let Me Drive** does not stop them. If you delete them, the same import does not build them again. Later, **Get suggestions from my data** offers all five again whenever your property has no booking speed rule at all. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

- **Delete** opens a dialog headed with the rule's name. **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes** removes the rule and every price change it made, so the next run prices those nights as if it had never existed. **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes** is the switch, from the dialog. Deleting cannot be undone.

You need to be a Revenue Manager or higher for either.

To rebuild one your way, the rule builder's **Speed** dropdown, **Measured over** and **Then waits (advanced)** can set the same condition, window and wait as four of the five. Slow-date trim is the exception. The builder turns a slow level into "at most", so the closest you can build is "at most Slower Than Normal", which also fires on Much Slower and Stalled nights. A rule you build also ranks below any starter rules you keep, so a rebuilt copy waits behind them where the original would not.

**Not yet** · A starter rule cannot be edited, and neither can any rule. To change its number, its wait or its room types, delete it and build your own with the rule builder. Read [The rule builder](@31).

An illustration with made-up numbers, not your property. Each example assumes at least five similar past nights.

**Example: Slow-date rescue on a Tuesday six weeks out**

Similar Tuesdays at The Harbour Inn had about 20 bookings in the month before this point. This one has 8. That reads Much Slower Than Normal (6 to 10 would, and 5 or fewer would read Stalled, which the rule also fires on). Standard drops 15%, from $150 to $127.50. A week later, MAYA counts only the bookings made in that week and compares them with the same week of the similar Tuesdays. If those still read Much Slower or Stalled, it cuts again, to $108.38. After a third cut the amber banner asks whether to carry on.

Similar nights had about 5 bookings in the month. This one has 9: Faster Than Normal (10 or more would read Much Faster or Surging, and the rule fires on those too). Standard rises 10%, from $150 to $165. Three days later MAYA counts only the bookings made in those three days, against the same three days of the similar nights. If those are still ahead, it raises again, to $181.50. If enough of the 9 cancel, the raise comes off.

**Example: Hot-week surge on a Saturday**

Similar Saturdays had about 5 bookings in the week at this point. This one has 10: Much Faster Than Normal (10 to 17 would). Suite rises 25%, from $300 to $375. Two days later the rule counts only the bookings made in those two days. It raises again only if those alone read Much Faster.

A floor is the lowest price MAYA will publish for a room type, and a ceiling is the highest. Each night's price is held between them, and a price you type outside them is refused. Every room type starts at 1.00 and 99,999.99 in your property's currency, which stop nothing in most currencies. If a room type sells above 99,999.99 (in yen or rupiah, say), set a real ceiling before you go live. Real ones come from your answers to the five questions, from your own rates during the import, or from a suggestion card you accept or change.

The **Change Log** tab says so when it happens: "That would have gone past your $300.00 ceiling for Standard, so it stopped there." or "That would have dropped under your $80.00 floor for Standard, so it stopped there." Amounts are in your property's currency.

A limit also stops rules from piling up beyond it. A booking speed or pickup rule that raises does not fire on a night already at its ceiling, and one that cuts does not fire on a night already at its floor. It starts no wait, and the attempt does not count towards the three-times question. When the night's price moves back inside the limits, the rule can fire again.

$200, up 10% to $220, then up 25% to $275. The $300 ceiling is not reached, so $275 is published.

Standard's base rate for a Saturday in August is $200. Its ceiling is $300. "Busy nights" raises it 10% to $220. Hot-week surge then raises it 25% to $275. Warm-date bump's 10% on top would be $302.50, so the published price is $300 and the change log says it stopped there. Sudden-spike catcher, which would raise it again, does not fire while the night sits at $300.

The other way: Standard at $150 with an $80 floor. Slow-date rescue cuts 15% four times over four weeks: $127.50, $108.38, $92.12, then $78.30, which is under the floor, so $80.00 is published. A fifth cut does not fire.

There is no settings page that lists floors and ceilings. You meet them in four places:

- The **Rate Simulator** tab's room table has a **Guardrails** column showing each room type's floor and ceiling. Only room types ticked as rooms are listed there. For an unticked type, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) to check its limits.
- The **Change Log** tab, in the sentences above.
- The **Rules that keep adjusting** banner, in a line like "If it keeps cutting, the price can fall to your $80.00 floor for Standard." When the limit is still the default, the line reads "Your ceiling for Suite is still MAYA's $99,999.99 default, so the price can climb that far." with a "?" beside it.
- The manual price editor, when a price you type is outside them.

There are three ways a floor or ceiling gets set, and no editor beyond them.

1. **The five questions.** The lowest rate you would take on a dead Tuesday becomes every active room type's floor. The most you would charge becomes the ceiling of each room type whose highest rate read so far fits under it. If you answer while the import is still reading, a room type whose higher rates arrive later can keep that ceiling: check the **Guardrails** column once the import is complete, and email us to lift one. Read [The five questions](@25).
The five questions

2. **The import, from your own rates.** Once the first three years are in, and again when the full history is in, MAYA fills in a floor and a ceiling for every room type still at its defaults, using the history numbers in the next section (with the exceptions it lists). This happens without a card. It never overwrites a limit that has already been set.
The import, from your own rates

3. **A suggestion card.** After **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab, the review shows a card for each room type still at a default: "Set a floor for "Standard"?" or "Set a ceiling for "Suite"?". The suggested amount sits in a box labelled **Amount to set**. Accept it with the **Set it to 80** button, or type your own number first and the button follows it. **No thanks** leaves the default. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

The banner's **Ask MAYA for a floor** and **Ask MAYA for a ceiling** buttons take you to the **Rules** tab, where the suggestions button is.
A suggestion card

During the import, your answers to the five questions are applied first, and then the history numbers below fill whatever is still at a default. On a card, your answer is offered where it fits. For a floor, the number from your history is offered only if you never answered. If your answer does not fit, there is no floor card.

**Floor**

- On a card: your own answer from the five questions, if you gave one.
- Otherwise, a floor of about 40% of what the room type usually sells for. It needs at least 30 nights of history for that room type.
Floor

**Ceiling**

- On a card: your own answer, if you gave one and it sits above nearly all of the room type's past rates. A ceiling lower than that would pin the room type down, so the next line is used instead.
- Otherwise, about one and a half times the room type's normal top rate. It needs at least 200 nights of history for that room type. It is never built on the single highest rate, so one mistyped rate cannot become your ceiling.
Ceiling

A room type whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom (the same tests as the "Is X actually a room?" card) never gets a floor or ceiling from its own rates, and never gets a floor or ceiling card, even after you confirm it is a real room. It stays at $1.00 and $99,999.99 unless the five questions or an email set one. MAYA also skips a ceiling that would land at or under the floor, and a floor that would land at or above the ceiling.

The rationale on a card tells you which line it came from: "You said the lowest rate you'd accept is $80, so MAYA suggests that as the floor." or "Standard has typically sold for $150 a night, so MAYA suggests a floor of $60."

- A floor must be above 0.
- A ceiling must be at least the floor. A card that would break this is refused with an error. The five questions do not check it. If your ceiling answer is under your floor answer, the questions move on without a word, and they never write that ceiling to a room type. Read [The five questions](@25).
- One floor and one ceiling per room type. Not per night, per season, per weekday or for weekends.
- Amounts are in your property's currency, to two decimal places. The defaults are plain numbers in your currency too: 1.00 and 99,999.99, whatever the currency.

In most currencies the default ceiling stops nothing. In a currency where a room sells for more than 99,999.99, such as yen, won, rupiah or dong, it does. Until a room type has a real ceiling, any price your base rate and rules reach above 99,999.99 is published at 99,999.99, even when your own rate for the night is higher. A price you type above it is refused. So before you go live, give every room type a real ceiling: answer the ceiling question in the five questions, accept a suggestion card, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Ceiling%20in%20my%20currency) with the numbers. The import sets one from your own rates for a room type with 200 nights of history or more.

The limits apply to you too, with one exception.

- A price you type under the floor is refused: "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." Over the ceiling: "Above this room type's ceiling of $300.00." Nothing is saved. Read [Setting a price yourself](@49).
- The exception is 0. A night set to 0 is a comp night. It is saved, no rule raises it, and MAYA does not send 0 to your property system, so you set the night to 0 there yourself. That is why a floor cannot be 0: a comp night is a per-night choice, not a limit.

**Careful** · Saving the floor card, the ceiling card or the last card of the five questions again puts your saved floor back on every active room type at once, over any floor set since. Check the **Guardrails** column in the **Rate Simulator** tab afterwards.

On the **Rules** tab, **Get suggestions from my data** reads your booking history again and compares it with your rules and your floors and ceilings. You get cards on the review screen to accept or reject one by one, and your rules, prices and limits stay as they are until you accept one. It can offer the five starter rules, offer to remove a pickup rule a booking speed rule already covers, offer to move an occupancy rule's threshold, and offer a floor or ceiling for a room type still at its default. If you have not gone live yet, wait: a read it starts takes the go-live button off the review.

On the **Rules** tab, beside the **Pricing Rules** heading, sits **Get suggestions from my data** (with a handshake symbol in front of it). Pressing it opens a small panel headed "Here's exactly what happens". The panel says MAYA re-reads your booking history and compares it against your current rules and price guardrails, that nothing changes by itself, and that you approve or reject each suggestion individually. Two buttons: the one beginning "Sounds good" starts the read, and **Never mind** closes the panel.

While the read runs, the button turns into a pulsing dot with a short waiting line. MAYA is reading your bookings again and counting. The dot stays as long as the **Rules** tab stays open, even after the read has finished. To see the result, press another tab such as **Calendar** and then **Rules** again, or reload the page and open **Rules**.

If the read found something to offer, the button is now a link reading "3 suggestions ready →" that opens the review. The number counts every card waiting for your answer. If the read is still going, the dot shows again. If there was nothing to offer, the plain button is back. After a reload, the blue banner at the top of the dashboard also opens the review with its **Review →** link.

- A property with a subscription in good standing. Otherwise: "This property's subscription is not active, so MAYA has paused work on it."
- A property with a connected system. Otherwise the message begins "Connect your property system first".
- Five runs per 15 minutes per property. Past that, a message asks you to let the last read finish before starting another. Read [Messages explained](@103).
- One read at a time. If a read is already running (yours, a colleague's, or the first import), pressing the button joins it rather than starting another. If that read is the first import, it finishes as a first import, with no suggestion cards. Press the button again once it is complete. Either way the press counts towards the five runs.

Mews has no history import yet, so on a Mews property the read cannot complete. Do not press the button there: the dot pulses for a few hours while the read retries, then the plain button comes back with no suggestions and no message. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Suggestions%20on%20Mews) instead. Read [The history import](@23).

**Careful: Before you go live, wait** · A read the button starts points the review at the new cards, and the card with **Turn them on for real** goes. Your starter rules stay. If it happens, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) and we switch the property live.

It is the same history import that ran when you connected, in a different mode. MAYA reads your property setup, your current bookings and your past years again, then compares what it finds with what you have. Nothing is written without a card you accept:

- Closures are proposed on cards, never recorded on their own. New instances of a season you confirmed earlier are proposed too.
- A duplicate room type with no bookings is proposed, not hidden.
- Cards about rates that look like typos, stays with a $0 rate and stays that point at deleted room types can come back, because each read is a fresh look.
- Room types are never unticked as rooms by a re-read. A type whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom gets an "Is X actually a room?" card instead.
- Your existing rules and limits are left exactly as they are.

Offered only when your property has no booking speed rule at all. A booking speed rule that is switched off counts as one, so pausing the starter rules for the season does not bring five fresh copies. When you have none, all five starter rules are offered, one card each, with the rule's own sentence and a line saying nothing currently watches for nights falling behind (or ahead of) their normal pace.

Buttons: **Add this rule** and **No thanks**. An added rule is on and applies every day with no date range. It measures every room type that counts as a room and changes every active room type. Starter rules built at import leave unticked types out altogether. It needs at least 60 past nights with a booking, like the starter rules. Read [Your starter rules](@27).

Offered for a pickup count rule that is switched on when a booking speed rule that is also switched on covers everything it does: the same room types or more, in both the measured and the changed sets, the same days, and the same dates or wider. The card explains that the pickup rule reacts to a fixed booking count that the booking speed rule already covers by comparing with your own similar past nights, so keeping both would stack two price reactions on the same bookings.

Three buttons:

- **Remove it** deletes the rule and undoes every price change it made.
- **Turn it off, keep it** switches it off. The changes it made stay, and you can switch it back on from the **Rules** tab.
- **Leave it running** changes nothing.
