The Standard card reads "Booked 8/12", "ADR $160.00", "Current price $165.00" (the "Busy nights" rule has not fired, because the property is 60% full, but the "Warm-date bump" booking speed rule has raised it 10%) and "Revenue $1280.00", the 8 booked rooms at $160 a night on average.

Not counting as a room does not stop a type being priced: the Meeting Room starts from its $90 like any other type. Had its rate in Cloudbeds been 0, the night would be closed, and "Current price" would show a dash.

When a manual price is open on a room type for that night, a small amber badge sits beside the room type's name:

- "Manual · $180.00" for a price someone typed in MAYA. Hover it and you see "Set" followed by the date and time it was typed.
- "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00" (or "Changed in Think Reservations · ...") for a rate you changed in your property system on a night MAYA had already sent to. Hover it and you see "Seen" followed by the date and time MAYA read it.

**Cloudbeds:** Both badges can appear. The second needs the property to be live and the night to have been sent to and confirmed at least an hour earlier. [Rates you change in your property system](@50) has the conditions.
Before you have opened the **PMS** tab in this visit, the badge and the manual price help may say "your PMS" instead of naming your system. Open the **PMS** tab once and the name fills in.

A dash after "Current price" means MAYA has not published a price for that room type on that night. There are four ordinary reasons:

- **The night is beyond the window.** Your rules run on tonight and the next 59 nights (60 nights). A night further out has no price until it enters the window. The exception is a manual price you saved further ahead: that save prices every night up to the last one you chose.
The night is beyond the window

- **The night is closed in your system, or has no rate to start from.** On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, a night whose rate in your system is 0, with no manual price typed in MAYA, is left unpriced on purpose. Load a rate there and the next hourly read picks it up. On Mews, MAYA does not read rates. It starts from the newest booking's rate for that room type on that night, or from the starting point it used there before. With neither, the night stays unpriced until you type a price.
The night is closed in your system, or has no rate to start from
- **The night has passed and had no price.** A night that has passed is not priced again. The card keeps the last price the night had before it passed, or a dash if it had none.
The night has passed and had no price

- **No run has happened yet.** A newly connected property shows dashes until its first pricing run.

The price your rules start from (the base price) is not shown on the day card. The change log names it in every change: "from $150.00 to $165.00".
No run has happened yet

The calendar updates on its own, within a few seconds of a change to a booking, a published price, a manual price or an out of service block. While the history import is running it refreshes less often, so the page stays calm.

Behind that, while you are on the **Calendar** tab, MAYA re-reads the month every 5 minutes, and again whenever you come back to the browser tab. After you save or clear a manual price the calendar refreshes at once. A month you opened a moment ago can show from memory when you step back to it.

The "· live" marker shows whenever the month has loaded.

**Good to know** · A new booking in your property system reaches MAYA on the next read of your bookings, about every five minutes. So the calendar can show it within about five minutes of the booking, not the same second.

Your rules run in your property's own time zone: "tonight" is today's date there, and that is where the 60-night window starts. The "Updated 3:05:12 PM" time is your browser's clock.

**Example: Why does yesterday still say "revenue on the books"?**

The day detail's summary line switches from "revenue on the books" to "revenue" at midnight UTC (the world reference time), not at midnight at your property. In the Americas that is the afternoon or evening, 4 PM in winter and 5 PM in summer at The Harbour Inn, so tonight can already read "revenue". In most of Europe, and in Asia and Australia, it comes after your own midnight, so yesterday can still read "revenue on the books" for a few hours. Only the label changes, never a number.

**Not yet** · There is no row of weekday names above the grid, no list or week view, and no export. The day card does not show the base price a rule started from, and it does not list the bookings behind a night. The cards and the day detail always show "$", whatever your property's currency (the sentences in the change log follow your currency, but its bold line shows $ too). To see a night's bookings, open your property system.

The **Change Log** tab covers your 10 most recent pricing runs, about the last 50 minutes, newest first. It lists a night when a rule is on its price, someone set its price, or its price differs from its starting point (the price before any rule). Each listed night shows its starting price and new price, then plain sentences saying what each rule on it did and why. A price that goes back to its starting point, with nothing left on it, is not listed.

A pricing run is one pass of MAYA over your property: it reads your bookings, runs every rule that is on against every night in the window (tonight and the next 59 nights), and publishes a new price wherever one changed. When you are live, the changed prices are then sent to your property system. In simulation the run happens in full and the log fills in the same way, but nothing is sent.

Runs happen:
- **About every five minutes**, each time MAYA's scheduled read of your bookings succeeds. A read that fails prices nothing that time, and a property whose subscription has lapsed is skipped.
About every five minutes
- **Straight after you save or clear a manual price**, as far as the last night you saved.
Straight after you save or clear a manual price

- **Straight after you change a room type** (ticking or unticking **Counts as a room**, adding or clearing rooms out of service).

A run that finds nothing to change still leaves a mark in the log. That is what **Show All Cycles** reveals.
Straight after you change a room type

The button in the top right toggles between the two views:

- **Show All Cycles** is what the button says while you are in the default view. That view keeps runs that list at least one night, every "Rates not reaching" problem, and every answer you gave to a rule that kept adjusting.
- **Show Changes Only** is what the button says once you have opened the full view. The full view adds the quiet runs, each reading "Prices checked" followed by a note that nothing needed to change. A run whose only price moves are ones the log does not list reads the same way (see "Moves the log does not list" below).

When none of the 10 runs lists a night, the default view shows no runs at all, and no message says why. Any "Rates not reaching" problem and any answer you gave still show. Click **Show All Cycles** to see the quiet runs.

Each run is a box. The first line reads:

"Pricing run · Fri, Oct 2, 2026, 3:05 PM PDT (4 min ago)"

The time is shown in your browser's time zone, with the zone's abbreviation, so two people in different places see different clock times for the same run. Hover the line and the exact moment shows as a raw timestamp in UTC, the world reference time, such as 2026-10-02T22:05:12.345+00:00 (3:05 PM in US Pacific time). The part in brackets says how long ago: "just now", "4 min ago", "2 hr ago", "yesterday", "3 days ago", up to 6 days. Older runs carry no bracket.

Under the first line comes either the list of changes or, for a quiet run, the "Prices checked" line.

Each change starts with a bold line:

"Standard · stay 2026-11-13: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%)"

That is the room type, the stay night, the night's starting point, the price the run published, and the whole move between those two as a percentage. A cut reads "down to" with a negative percentage.

The starting point is the night's price before any rule: your own rate for that night (on Mews, the rate on the newest booking), or a price someone set. It is not the price the night had before this run. So when a second rule stacks on a night an earlier run already raised from $150.00 to $165.00, the bold line still starts from $150.00:

"Standard · stay 2026-11-13: $150.00 up to $206.25 (+37.5%)"

1. **What came off.** If the run stopped applying an earlier change, that comes first: "Warm-date bump" stopped applying an earlier 10% raise here: enough of the bookings behind it cancelled. This line shows only while something else is still on the price: another rule, your floor or ceiling, or a price someone set. When the change that came off was the last thing on the price, the night goes back to its starting point and gets no entry at all.
What came off

2. **Each rule on the price, then why.** Every rule still applying to the night is listed, not only the one that acted in this run. The first reads "Warm-date bump" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. A second rule on the same night reads Then "Hot-week surge" raised it 25%, from $165.00 to $206.25. The "from" price of each later rule is the price the earlier one left, which is how stacking shows itself.
Each rule on the price, then why
3. **The limit, if one stepped in.** That would have gone past your $300.00 ceiling for Standard, so it stopped there.
The limit, if one stepped in

4. **A fallback** when there is nothing else to say: The rate moved from $150.00 to $160.00.

Only one booking speed or pickup rule can fire on a night for one room type in one run. So when two are listed, the first fired on an earlier run and still applies. Its reason then carries no numbers, because those were read on the run it fired.

Under the sentences, a change carries a **How did we know?** button when the run read booking speed for that night. With a booking speed rule that measures the whole property (every starter rule does), that is nearly every change, whichever rule made it, typed prices included. [The numbers behind a change](@47) covers what it opens.
A fallback
Every "why" sentence is built from your own rule: the mark you typed, the room types it measures, and the numbers the run saw. The shapes below use The Harbour Inn's rules.

These two share one sentence, because you set them as one condition.

| Rule | Sentence |
|---|---|
| Occupancy Greater than 80 | It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set. |
| Occupancy Less than 50 | It was 40% full, under the 50% mark you set. |
| Booking window Less than 3 | It had 2 days to go, past the 3-day mark you set. |
| Booking window Greater than 21 | It had 30 days to go, beyond the 21-day mark you set. |
| Both, "Last minute" | It was 40% full with 2 days to go, under the 50% mark and past the 3-day mark you set. |
| Measuring other room types than it changes | Standard and Deluxe were 83% full, past the 80% mark you set. |
| No numbers recorded | This night was past the 80% mark you set. |

Read "past" as "on the far side of the mark in the direction you asked for". A booking window counts down, so a night 2 days out is past a 3-day mark, not short of it.

For a pickup rule, a room night counts as one, so a 3-room booking for one night reads as 3 here. [Pickup count](@37) has the detail.

A pickup rule with **Pickup measures** set to **Revenue (currency)** fires on the money booked, but its sentence still shows the room nights and calls your amount a booking mark. A rule set at 500 reads "9 bookings arrived in the last 3 days, past the 500-booking mark you set." The 500 is the amount you typed, in your property's currency, and the 9 is the room nights gained in those days.

The sentence opens with the level the rule is written for, then the count, then what a night like this usually has:

| Level in the rule | Opening words |
|---|---|
| Stalled | Bookings all but stopped this past week |
| Surging | Bookings surged this past week |
| Normal | Bookings came in at the normal pace this past week |
| Any other level | The level in lower case: "Bookings came in faster than normal", "Bookings came in much slower than normal", and so on |

"this past week" becomes "this past day" or "this past month" to match the rule's **Measured over** setting. Then:

"Bookings came in faster than normal this past week: 9, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now."

The count can read "none" or, after cancellations, "more cancelled than booked". When similar nights usually have fewer than 1 booking by that point it reads "where a night like this usually has almost none by now".

**After the night has already been raised or cut.** A rule that raises never re-counts bookings an earlier raise already acted on. Once a booking speed or pickup rule has raised a night, a booking speed rule that raises counts only the bookings that came in after that raise. One that cuts counts from the night's last cut the same way. The day of the raise or cut is the first day counted, and the sentence names those days:

"Bookings came in faster than normal in the 4 days since this night was last raised: 6, against the 2 a night like this usually gets in those days."

When only the day of the raise or cut has been counted so far, it reads "later on the day this night was last raised" (or "last cut") and "usually gets in a day". [How rules run](@39) explains why the count restarts.

When the rule measures other room types than the ones it changes, the subject changes: "Standard and Deluxe bookings came in faster than normal this past week: ...". A rule that measures and changes the same room types reads "Bookings", with no names, even when those are only some of your room types. **How did we know?** names the room types whenever a rule measures only some of them.
When an occupancy rule measured room types that do not count as rooms, those were left out of the figure, and one more sentence says so: "That 82% leaves out Meeting Room."

A booking speed or pickup rule can act on the same night again after its wait. The second time reads Then "Hot-week surge" raised it another 25%, from $206.25 to $257.81. The repeat only carries a "why" sentence when the run has fresh numbers for it.

**Example: Two rules and a ceiling on one night** · Deluxe on Friday, November 13, 2026 starts at $200. "Warm-date bump" raises it 10% to $220. "Hot-week surge" then raises it 25% to $275. The Deluxe ceiling is $400, so $275 is published. Had the ceiling been $250, the log would add: That would have gone past your $250.00 ceiling for Deluxe, so it stopped there.

A manual price shows as its own change, led by a sentence naming who typed it:

"Priya set the base rate to $180.00."

The name is the person's profile name in MAYA. If no name is stored it reads "A manager". A rate you changed in your property system on a night MAYA had sent to names no person: "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $180.00." (or "in Think Reservations").

With nothing stacked on top, that one sentence is the whole entry, and the bold line reads "$180.00 up to $180.00 (+0%)". If a rule later fires on top of your price, its sentences follow the lead sentence in the usual way.

When you answer the **Rules that keep adjusting** banner, the answer is logged as its own item headed "Your answer · Fri, Oct 2, 2026, 3:12 PM PDT". One item covers every night the answer settled:

- Priya stopped "Hot-week surge" on 4 nights. The raises it already made stay, unless enough of the bookings behind them cancel.
- Priya stopped "Slow-date trim" on Fri, Nov 13 2026. What it already cut stays.
- Priya told "Hot-week surge" to carry on with 4 nights.
- Priya let "Hot-week surge" run again on 4 nights. It can start adjusting again from the next pricing run.

A deleted rule reads "A rule" here. At most 20 answers are shown, within the span of the runs on screen. [Rules that keep adjusting](@42) explains the banner and the choices.

When you are live and a price cannot be delivered, the log carries an amber item headed "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" (or "Think Reservations"). How soon it appears depends on the cause:

- **A problem that needs you**, such as lost access or a price your system refuses: at once.
A problem that needs you

- **Your system cannot find the rate MAYA writes to**: after one more try. MAYA reads your list of rates again and sends once more on the next run, about five minutes later. If the rate is still missing, the item appears then.
Your system cannot find the rate MAYA writes to

- **A problem that often clears on its own**, such as your system not answering, asking MAYA to slow down or not confirming a send: only once a night has failed at least 5 times over at least 2 hours.

A few holds MAYA applies itself never appear here.

While the problem lasts it sits at the very top, above every run. Once it ends it drops to where it ended, and only stays while that moment is within the runs shown. Mews never has these items, because nothing is sent to Mews.

The item names the cause in one sentence, counts the nights and room types affected, says "Still happening" or when it was resolved, and tells you what to do when there is something to do. **Show 12 tries** opens the attempts behind it. [When your property system does not accept a price](@56) walks through every cause.
A problem that often clears on its own

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs on screen | The 10 most recent, about the last 50 minutes. A quiet run counts as one of the 10. |
| Changes per run | The 40 biggest moves, largest first, each measured as the whole move from the night's starting point. A run with more changes shows 40 and nothing says how many more there were. |
| What counts as a change | A night whose price differs from its starting point by at least one cent, has a rule still on it, or has a price someone set. |
| Problems and answers | Up to 20 of each, within the span of the runs shown. |
| Detail behind a change | Kept for 90 days. That is how long **How did we know?** can open for a change. |

Runs happen about every five minutes, so 10 runs reach back about 50 minutes. Saving a price or changing a room type adds a run, so on a busy day the log reaches back less far. Older runs are not lost the moment they leave the screen, but there is no way to page back to them in the app.

The log lists a night only when, after the run, its price differs from its starting point, a rule is still on it, or someone set its price. Two kinds of real price move meet none of these, so they get no entry:

- **A price going back to its starting point.** The last thing on the price comes off. The only rule on the night stops holding (for "Busy nights", the night falls to 80% full or less), the bookings behind its only raise cancel, or you clear a price you set on a night no rule is on.
A price going back to its starting point

- **A price that moves only because its starting point moved**, on a night no rule is on. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, that includes a new rate MAYA reads from your system (about once an hour) on a night it has never sent a price to. On Mews, it is a newer booking with a different rate.

When nothing else in that run is listed, the full view shows the run as "Prices checked" with a note that nothing needed to change, even though a price moved. To see where a night stands now, open the **Calendar** tab.
A price that moves only because its starting point moved

The log shows only the 10 most recent runs, about the last 50 minutes. A price that moved more than about an hour ago is no longer on screen, and a change from earlier today has usually left it. MAYA keeps the detail behind every change for 90 days: the night's starting price and the price published, which rules acted, and the numbers each one saw. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) with the room type, the night and roughly when the price moved, and we can look the change up for you within those 90 days. After 90 days the detail is gone.

The sentences under each change follow your property's currency: "$" for US dollars, "€" for euros, "£" for pounds, and the three-letter code in front of the amount for any other currency. The bold line above them, like the calendar and the simulator, always shows "$". So a property in euros sees "€150.00" in a sentence and "$150.00" in the bold line for the same price.

Everyone on the property can read the change log, whatever their role.

An occupancy rule set to Greater than 80 writes: It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.

**Not yet** · The log cannot be exported, and MAYA does not email it or send notifications when a price changes. You cannot see more than the 10 most recent runs (about the last 50 minutes), or page back through older ones. To keep a record, open the log and copy what you need.

Under a change in the change log, click **How did we know?** to see the numbers behind it: how many bookings arrived for that night, how many a night like it usually has by then, and the level that reads as. It shows on a change when the run read booking speed for that night. **Why did you expect that?** shows how the similar nights were chosen. **Show me the nights you compared** lists them one by one, and each one can be set aside if it was not a normal night.

**How did we know?** sits under a change in the change log, after its sentences. It appears under any change on a night where the run took a booking speed reading. A booking speed rule that measures the whole property (every starter rule does) reads each night it is not waiting on, and that reading goes under every room type's change on the night. So with such a rule on, nearly every change has the button, whichever rule made it: an occupancy, booking window or pickup rule, a price you typed, or a rate changed in your system. The evidence describes how the night was booking, not necessarily the rule that made this change.

The button is missing when the run took no booking speed reading for the night: you have no booking speed rule on, or each one was in its wait on that night. A rule that measures only some room types puts its reading only under the room types it changes.

To find the block behind a booking speed rule's change, read the first sentence of each. Usually it is the block for the rule's **Measured over** setting, starting "In the last 7 days" for a 7-day rule. But a rule that raises may find the night already raised within that stretch by a booking speed or pickup rule. Then it counts only from that raise, and its block begins "This night was last raised on". A rule that cuts works the same way after a cut, with "This night was last cut on".

Say "Warm-date bump" raised a night on a Friday and "Hot-week surge" raises it on the Monday after. The surge's block starts "This night was last raised on" and covers those 4 days, not 7. When "Warm-date bump" raises a night again within 30 days of the last raise, its own block starts the same way, and the block starting "In the last 30 days" is usually the one read for the rules that cut. Two rules that count from the same raise over the same days show the same numbers, so two blocks can look alike.

If a change turns out to carry no reading, the panel says "No booking-speed observation was recorded for this change." If the fetch fails you see the error and **Try again**. **Close** folds the panel away.

Three sentences, then sometimes a fourth.

**What arrived.** "In the last 7 days, 9 bookings arrived for this night, with 40 days still to go before arrival." The stretch matches the rule's **Measured over** setting. When the rule measures some room types only, the count names them: "In the last 7 days, 9 Standard and Deluxe bookings arrived for this night, ...". A booking that holds several rooms counts once.
What arrived

**What is usual.** "By this point on nights like this one, we would expect about 5 bookings over the same stretch." When similar nights had fewer than 1 booking over that stretch it reads "almost none". The number is what the similar nights had received over the same stretch of their own booking curves, at the same distance before arrival. It is their average, with the highest and lowest left off when there are 5 or more similar nights, and rounded to a whole number wherever it is shown.
What is usual
**The reading.** "That reads as Faster Than Normal." This is the level the count and the usual number produce together. [Booking speed](@34) has the seven levels and where the lines fall.
The reading

**A note when a fixed check moved the level.** Sometimes the raw numbers point one way and a fixed check keeps the reading nearer Normal. One of three notes then appears:

| Note | What happened |
|---|---|
| "The raw numbers leaned away from Normal, but the gap was small enough to be ordinary noise at this volume, so we held the call at Normal." | The difference between the count and the usual number was too small to mean anything at that volume. |
| "The raw numbers pointed at an even stronger call, but not by enough evidence to justify it, so we softened it one step." | The count was high, but not by enough bookings to support the strongest level. |
| "We found only a few genuinely comparable nights, so we kept the call within one step of Normal no matter how strong the numbers looked." | Fewer than 5 of the similar nights had any bookings on record, so the reading is capped one step either side of Normal. |

**Example: The Harbour Inn, a Friday six weeks out**

Friday, November 13, 2026 received 9 bookings in the 30 days to Friday, October 2. The similar Fridays in MAYA's reading of the last three years had about 5 by the same point. The first layer reads:
A note when a fixed check moved the level

In the last 30 days, 9 bookings arrived for this night, with 42 days still to go before arrival.
By this point on nights like this one, we would expect about 5 bookings over the same stretch.
That reads as Faster Than Normal.

"Warm-date bump" measures over 30 days and fires at Faster Than Normal or above, so it raised Standard 10%. Blocks for the past week and the past day usually sit under this one too, read for "Hot-week surge" and "Sudden-spike catcher". Each has its own level.

A rule never re-counts bookings it already acted on. Once a booking speed or pickup rule has raised a night, a booking speed rule that raises counts only the bookings made after that raise. One that cuts counts from the night's last cut by such a rule. An occupancy or booking window rule's change never restarts the count. The first sentence then names the stretch:

"This night was last raised on Fri, Oct 2 2026. In the 4 days from that raise on, 3 bookings arrived for it, with 39 days still to go before arrival."

When the raise was earlier the same day, the sentence reads "Later that day," instead: "This night was last raised on Fri, Oct 2 2026. Later that day, 2 bookings arrived for it, with 42 days still to go before arrival." After a cut it reads "last cut on" and "from that cut on".

A night with no usable similar nights and nothing nearby to read from gets no reading at all, and no booking speed rule is allowed to act on it. The first layer then reads:

"We do not have enough history yet to say what would be normal for this night, so no expectation was formed."
"No booking-speed call was made, and rules that watch booking speed were not allowed to act on this night."

You will see this on a change made by some other rule on a night whose booking speed was checked but could not be read.

Click **Why did you expect that?** and a short list appears under the first layer. Each line is one rule MAYA followed when choosing the similar nights.

When the night had already been raised or cut, the first line says so: "Once a night has been raised, rules that raise count only the bookings made after that raise, whichever rule made it, the rest of that day included, and read the nights it is compared with over the same days." There is a matching line for cuts. "Whichever rule" means any booking speed or pickup rule: an occupancy or booking window rule's change does not count.

Then, for an ordinary comparison:

- **The weekday.** "We only compared against other Friday nights", followed by the reason: booking rhythms differ too much between days of the week to mix them. Weekends are Friday and Saturday nights. The line also appears on a night near a holiday, where it is not always accurate: around a fixed-date holiday such as Christmas or July 4, the compared nights are the same dates in earlier years and usually fall on other weekdays. The dates under **Show me the nights you compared** show which nights were used.
The weekday

- **The holiday or the season.** A night near a US holiday reads "This night sits in the orbit of Thanksgiving, so we matched against the same position relative to that holiday in earlier years, not the same calendar date." Any other night reads "We stayed inside the same demand season your history shows: Peak Season (June 10 through August 31)." Seasons are stretches of your year that book differently, read from your own history, and this line is the only place they appear on screen. [Which past nights your rules compare with](@36) has more.
The holiday or the season

- **When the match was loosened.** "Strict matching found too few usable nights, so we relaxed the criteria a step", with a note that this is worth weighing. It means fewer than 4 nights matched on the strict rule (same weekday, same season), so MAYA allowed the same kind of day (a Saturday for a Friday, since both are weekend nights) or a nearby time of year.
When the match was loosened
- **Always last.** "Closed periods and any dates you have told us were not normal are left out of the comparison entirely."
Always last

A night with no similar nights at all is read from momentum instead: how nights near it are filling now, against how the same nights were filling a year ago. The list then opens with two lines that say exactly that, and adds:

- "6 nearby nights could be paired with their counterparts from last year." (or "No nearby night could be paired with a counterpart from last year, so we cannot say whether the pace has changed.")
- "Those nights are filling about 20% faster than they were a year ago." (or "slower", or "at about the same pace as a year ago" when within 5% either way)
- "The starting point was about 4 bookings, taken from how this same night was booking at this point last year (Fri, Nov 14 2025)." (or "taken from the typical pace of nearby nights" when the night itself has no usable history from last year)

Once the second layer is open, and when there are nights to show, **Show me the nights you compared** appears. Click it for one row per night. The nights nearest in time come first, up to 8. For an ordinary night that is usually the same weekday, week after week, from the same season: first any nights of that season that have already passed this year, then the same season last year, then earlier years if there is room.

Three rows from the list for The Harbour Inn's Friday, November 13, 2026:

| Row | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "Fri, Nov 14 2025" then "4 bookings in the same stretch" | That Friday had received 4 bookings over the same stretch, at the same distance before arrival. |
| "Fri, Nov 7 2025" then "1 booking in the same stretch" | The Friday a week before, read the same way. |
| "Fri, Oct 24 2025" then "6 bookings in the same stretch" | The next Friday back. Fri, Oct 31 2025 is not in the list: it is Halloween, and a night near a holiday is never compared with an ordinary night. |

A row can also read "no history for this night". MAYA has no bookings recorded for that night, usually because it falls before your history begins. It adds nothing to the usual number and does not count toward the 5 similar nights a full-strength reading needs.

Under each date, in smaller type, the reasons it was chosen, joined by semicolons: "a Friday; your Shoulder Season; about a year earlier". The season is your own, so its name on your screen can differ. When the match was loosened, the stricter matches are listed first, and a looser row can read "a Saturday, similar to a Friday; your Shoulder Season; about a year earlier" or "a Friday; a nearby time of year; 2 years earlier". The last reason says how long ago the night was: "earlier this year", "recently", "about a year earlier", "2 years earlier" or "3 years earlier".

For a momentum reading the rows are the paired nights, listed on their year-ago date: "3 bookings at this point last year, against 5 bookings now for Fri, Nov 6 2026", with the reason "used to read how the pace has changed since last year". The starting point night reads "4 bookings at this point last year", marked as the starting point for the estimate, with the reason "this same night a year ago".

On the right of each row is **Not a fair comparison?**. Once you have set a night aside, that spot reads "Set aside" with a note that it is not used from the next run onward. [Setting a date aside](@48) walks through the form.

In this example The Harbour Inn's booking history only goes back to September 2025. The third layer lists 8 Saturdays, nearest first. Five have bookings on record, with 1, 4, 5, 5 and 6 bookings in the same stretch. The three oldest fall before the history begins and read "no history for this night", so they add nothing. The usual number is the average of the middle three of the five, about 5, because with five nights the highest and lowest are left off.

The 1-booking night is Sat, Nov 15 2025. Sam recalls the road closure that weekend and clicks **Not a fair comparison?** on it. From the next run that Saturday is left out, and an older Saturday moves up into the list. It too falls before the history begins, so it adds nothing. The usual number stays about 5: the 1-booking night was already left off as the lowest, and the four that remain average 5. But with only four similar Saturdays that have bookings, the reading can now go no further than Faster Than Normal, so "Hot-week surge" (which waits for Much Faster Than Normal) will not fire on this night while that holds. The 25% raise already on the night stays. With a longer history, the Saturday that moved up would have had bookings, and nothing would be capped.

MAYA keeps the detail behind a change for 90 days. Within that time the numbers open for any change still on the change log. Since the log shows the 10 most recent runs, in practice you will always be well inside the 90 days.

**Not yet** · There is no page that lists your seasons, your similar nights or your holidays on their own. They appear only inside this panel, for the night in question. You cannot type an expected number or change the level by hand. The one lever is setting a night aside.

If a past night MAYA compared with was not a normal night (a festival, a buyout, a renovation), set it aside. From the next pricing run it is left out of every comparison. Say it happens every year and, once reports from two different years agree, the whole window around it is skipped every year.

Open the change log, find a change with **How did we know?** under it, and click it. Open **Why did you expect that?**, then **Show me the nights you compared**. Each past night in that list has **Not a fair comparison?** on its right. Click it and a short form opens under that night.

There is no page where you type a date in by hand. You set a night aside from the list of nights MAYA compared with, one night at a time. The change log keeps only the 10 most recent runs, so this works only while the change is still listed there. [The numbers behind a change](@47) walks through the three layers.

The form asks "What made Fri, Nov 14 2025 not a fair comparison?" and offers a dropdown, **Choose a reason…**, with twelve reasons. Pick one, choose how far it should reach where that choice is offered, and click **Set this date aside**. **Never mind** closes the form without saving. While it saves the button reads **Saving…**.

| Reason | Choices it offers |
|---|---|
| The holiday reason (first in the list) | this date, every year, seasons |
| Local Event or Festival | this date, every year, seasons |
| Sporting Event or Tournament | this date, every year, seasons |
| Conference or Convention | this date, every year, seasons |
| Renovation or Rooms Out of Service | this date, seasons |
| Utility or Amenity Outage | this date, seasons |
| Group Buyout | this date only |
| Nearby Competitor Closed or Sold Out | this date, seasons |
| Severe Weather | this date, every year |
| Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption | this date only |
| Booking Data Looks Wrong | this date only |
| Other | this date, every year, seasons |

**Other** needs a few words in the box that appears ("Tell us in a few words what happened"), up to 300 characters. When a reason offers only "this date", no choices are shown and the date is set aside on its own.

When a reason allows more than one, its choices appear (two or three, as the table shows). The first is selected, and each one does everything the one above it does.

**Just set aside this one date (recommended).** This night stops being used in comparisons, and in the reading of your seasons, from the next pricing run. It is never treated as a pattern that repeats.
Just set aside this one date (recommended)

**This happens every year around this time.** The night is set aside now, the same as above. On top of that, MAYA counts it as one report of a yearly pattern. Once it holds reports of the same reason, at about the same time of year, from 2 different years, it leaves a window of 5 days either side of that point out of comparisons every year.
This happens every year around this time

**This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced).** The night is set aside now, and it counts toward the yearly pattern too. On top of that, once it holds reports at this level from 3 different years, the same window is also left out when MAYA reads your seasons (the stretches of your year that book differently). One correction can never change how your seasons are read on its own.

Two things about counting years. A report counts as one year however many nights it covers, so a renovation you flag on three nights is one year of evidence, not three. And reports older than 3 years stop counting.

**Good to know** · Weekends are Friday and Saturday nights. A night you set aside is skipped whatever weekday it falls on, and the yearly window is a stretch of dates, not of weekdays.
This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced)

From the next pricing run (about every five minutes) the night is left out of every comparison and out of the reading of your seasons. Any booking speed rule that fires from then on compares against the nights that remain, so the "usual" number for a night can move.

If setting a night aside leaves fewer than 5 compared nights, the reading is held within one step of Normal, so a rule waiting for Much Faster Than Normal, Surging, Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled will not fire on it. A compared night that shows "no history for this night" does not count toward the 5.

MAYA does not go back and redo prices. A price a rule already set stays until that rule next acts, or its change comes off in the usual way.

For a reading built from momentum (nearby nights compared with the same nights a year earlier), the night you set aside is the year-ago night of each pair, and the starting point night. That is where a night that was not normal usually sits.

**Example: The Harbour Inn sets a Saturday aside**

Sam opens **How did we know?** under a 25% raise to Deluxe on Saturday, November 14, 2026. In the block for the past week, 10 bookings arrived against about 5 usual: Much Faster Than Normal, the level "Hot-week surge" waits for. The compared nights include Sat, Nov 15 2025 with "1 booking in the same stretch". That was the weekend the coast road was closed. Sam clicks **Not a fair comparison?**, picks **Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption** (this date only), and clicks **Set this date aside**.

The row now reads "Set aside". From the next run, that Saturday is left out. The usual number for Saturday, November 14, 2026 stays about 5: the five Saturdays had 1, 4, 5, 5 and 6 bookings, and with five nights the highest and lowest were already left off the average. But only four compared Saturdays remain, so the reading is now held within one step of Normal. The same 10 bookings now read Faster Than Normal, and "Hot-week surge" will not fire on them. The raise it already made stays.

On the **Change Log** tab, under the heading, sits a panel titled **Your corrections**. Click **Show** to open it and **Hide** to close it. Everyone on the property can read it.

Each night you have set aside is one line: the night, then "You told us this date was affected by road, transit, or flight disruption, so we leave it out of comparisons." For **Other**, your own words appear instead of the reason.

Under those, two kinds of note can appear:

- **Still counting.** "We have seen this reported in 1 year of the 2 different years we would want before treating "Local Event or Festival" near June 10 as a pattern that repeats every year." The same shape appears for the seasons choice, ending "as a change to how we read the season around here."
Still counting

- **Now applied every year**, in amber. "Reports across 2 different years flagged "Local Event or Festival" near June 10, so we now leave it out of comparisons every year." For the seasons choice it ends "out of comparisons and out of our seasonal calculations, every year."

When the panel has nothing in it, a short note explains what it is for.
Now applied every year

Each line in **Your corrections** has **Undo**. Click it and the night is compared with again from the next run. Any yearly pattern it counted toward is counted again from the reports that remain, so a window applied every year can go back to "still counting".

If nothing is removed, the panel says "Nothing was removed" and adds that it may already be gone, or that removing it needs manager access.
Setting a night aside, and undoing it, needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Everyone on the property, Viewers included, can open the evidence and read **Your corrections**.

MAYA matches nights around 17 US holidays by their position relative to the holiday rather than by date. It has no other countries' holidays and no local events. When a past night was a holiday or an event MAYA does not have, set it aside with the holiday reason (first in the **Choose a reason…** list) or **Local Event or Festival**, and choose **This happens every year around this time**. After reports from 2 different years, the window is skipped every year. [Which past nights your rules compare with](@36) lists the 17 holidays MAYA has.

A closed period is a stretch you confirmed as closed on the review screen. A card there asks whether you were closed between two dates, or whether your property is normally closed at that time of year. Those nights are left out of comparisons too, and out of the reading of your seasons, without any setting aside. There is no screen to add a closed period by hand, and MAYA does not treat a future closure as closed, so those nights are still priced. [Checking what MAYA found](@26) covers the closure findings.

Click a night on the calendar, type a price in a room type's box and save. That number goes to your property system as typed. Rules that had already moved that night pause for that room type, and rules that fire later stack on top of your price. **Clear** hands the night back to MAYA.

Open the **Calendar** tab and click a day. Under the grid, one card per room type appears. At the bottom of each card sits the price editor: a box with a $ sign, pre-filled with the night's current price (or the price already typed for it), a **through…** link, **Save**, and a **?** that opens a short explanation titled "Setting a price yourself". **Clear** appears only while a typed price is open on that night.

Setting or clearing a price needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Everyone on the property can see the prices that have been set.

1. Click the night on the calendar, then find the room type's card.
2. Type the price in the box. Whole numbers or cents are both fine.
3. For a run of nights, click **through…** and pick the last night the price applies to. The × beside it goes back to a single night.
4. Press Enter or click **Save**. A line under the box confirms what happened (see below).

**Save** stays greyed out while the box is empty, not a number, below 0, or while the last night is before the first.

**A comma or a point?** Type a point for cents, as in 180.50, and no thousands separator, as in 1250. The box is your browser's own number box, so whether it also takes a comma (180,50) depends on your browser and its language. If it cannot read what you typed, it counts as empty and **Save** stays greyed out, so nothing wrong is saved. The amount and threshold boxes in the rule builder work the same way.

Your number becomes the starting point for that night and room type, ahead of the rate in your property system and everything else MAYA might have started from. Three things follow.

- **Changes already on the night are taken off.** A standard rule (occupancy or booking window) that was holding a change on that night keeps its place but stops moving the price. A booking speed or pickup rule's change on that night is taken off. The confirmation line counts them: "Paused 2 rules on this night for this room".
Changes already on the night are taken off

- **Rules that fire later stack on top.** Your price is not a lock. A rule whose condition starts holding after you typed, or a booking speed or pickup rule that fires after its wait, changes the price from your number. The change log then reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00." followed by that rule's sentence.
Rules that fire later stack on top

If you want a night left at your number for good, there is no lock. Type the price, then type it again when a rule moves it, or turn off the rules that would move it. Turning a rule off stops it on every night, not only this one. To stop one rule on this night alone, answer **Stop for this night** when the amber banner asks, which is only after that rule has adjusted the night three times. This works for booking speed and pickup rules only. An occupancy or booking window rule can only be turned off everywhere.
Your price is published as typed

Standard on Friday, November 13, 2026 is at $165: "Warm-date bump" raised it 10% from $150. Priya types $180 and clicks **Save**. The line reads "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now. Paused 1 rule on this night for this room; new rules will apply on top." The night now shows "Manual · $180.00" and the change log reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00."

A week later the night passes 80% full. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) fires and raises it to $198.00, from $180.00. The log reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00." then ""Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $180.00 to $198.00."

**Example: The lines after Save and Clear**

| Line | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." | You are live and MAYA has asked for the price to be sent straight away. |
| "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds on the next cycle (about 5 min)." | You are live and the price goes with the next pricing run. |
| "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." | You are still in simulation. The price shows in MAYA and is not sent. |
| "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 60-day push window." | Every night you saved is more than 59 nights ahead. MAYA sends a night once it enters the window. |
| "Saved. 12 nights sending to Cloudbeds now; 8 more will be sent as they enter the 60-day window." | Your run of nights crosses the edge of the window. |
| "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." | You typed 0, a comp night. See below. |
| "... Paused 2 rules on this night for this room; new rules will apply on top." | Added when your price took a rule's change off. "on these 5 nights" for a run. |
| "... No rule raises a night set to 0." | Added when you typed 0. |
| "Cleared. MAYA is pricing this night again." | **Clear** worked. "Cleared 5 nights. MAYA is pricing them again." for a run. |
| "Couldn't save that price." or "Couldn't clear that price." | MAYA could not do it and gave no reason. Try again. |
| "Couldn't reach MAYA. Try again." | Your browser could not reach MAYA. Check your connection and try again. |
The system's name in these lines (Cloudbeds, Think Reservations, Mews) fills in once you have opened the **PMS** tab in this visit. Before that, the lines and the **?** panel say "your PMS".

**Cloudbeds:** When you are live, MAYA runs your rules on the nights you saved straight away and asks for the price to be sent now. If it cannot ask, the next run sends it within about five minutes. It goes to the room type's base rate in Cloudbeds. A night more than 59 nights ahead is priced now and sent when it enters the 60-night window.

**ThinkReservations:** When you are live, MAYA runs your rules on the nights you saved straight away and asks for the price to be sent now. If it cannot ask, the next run sends it within about five minutes. It goes to the rate type named Best Available, or, if none is, the standard rate type that covers the most room types. ThinkReservations accepts the price and applies it shortly after, and MAYA reads it back within about an hour to confirm it landed. A night more than 59 nights ahead is priced now and sent when it enters the 60-night window.
In simulation the price is saved and shown, and nothing is sent. If you go live later, it goes out with the first live send like every other price.

| Limit | What the screen says |
|---|---|
| Tonight onwards only, on your property's own calendar | "Manual prices apply to tonight onwards; earlier nights have already sold." |
| Up to 364 days ahead | "MAYA prices up to a year ahead." |
| At most 365 nights in one save in practice (tonight to 364 days ahead). The screen's own limit reads 366 | "One change can cover at most 366 nights." You see it only if you pick 367 nights or more. |
| A number of 0 or more | "Price must be a number of zero or more." |
| Not below the floor (except 0) | "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." |
| Not above the ceiling | "Above this room type's ceiling of $300.00." |
| At most 99,999,999.99 | "That price is more than MAYA can store." |
| 30 saves or clears per person per 10 minutes, shared with room type changes | "That's a lot of price changes at once. Give it a minute and try again." |
| Revenue Manager or higher | "This needs Revenue Manager access or higher on this property." |

A price outside the floor or ceiling is refused, not rounded to the limit. Type a number inside the limits, or change the limits first. [Floors and ceilings](@28) explains where they are set.

Prices in these messages show your property's currency sign. The box itself always shows $.

Type 0 and the night becomes a comp night for that room type. It is allowed under the floor. No rule raises it, and no rule can cut it, because it is already at the lowest a price can go.

MAYA does not send a price of 0 to any property system. The confirmation says so, and while the night stays at 0 the change log carries an item headed "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" that reads "MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so Standard rates set to 0 in MAYA weren't changed there", with the action "If the night is meant to be free, set it to 0 in Cloudbeds yourself." Once your system has the night at 0, the item closes on its own. [Make a night free](@68) has the short version.

**A booking speed or pickup rule waits again from your price.** A rule that existed when you typed the price waits its wait from the moment you typed, then reads its whole window afresh, as if nothing had happened on the night before. A rule you add after typing the price is not held by it. [How rules run](@39) explains the wait.
A booking speed or pickup rule waits again from your price

**A standard rule holds its place.** An occupancy or booking window rule whose condition already held when you typed stays quiet on that night. When its condition stops and starts again, or when you clear the price, it moves the price again.
A standard rule holds its place

**The three-times question closes.** If the **Rules that keep adjusting** banner was asking about that night and rule, your price takes its changes off and the question closes for that night. It asks again if the rule adjusts your price three times.
The three-times question closes

After a clear, your rules run on the night again straight away. The starting point is the rate MAYA read from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations for that night, otherwise the rate of the newest booking on it, otherwise the starting point saved on the last run. Mews properties start from the booking or that saved starting point, since MAYA does not read Mews rates.

While your price was open, it was the night's starting point, so that is the one saved. A night with no rate read and no booking on it starts again from the price you typed (when it was above 0). On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations that is usually a night more than 59 nights ahead, because MAYA reads rates for tonight and the next 59 nights. Once the night enters that window, MAYA reads its rate and starts from that instead.
Your typed price is kept as a record of who set what and when. It is not shown once cleared.

A rate you change in your property system, on a night MAYA had sent to, is kept the same way and shows as "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00". [Rates you change in your property system](@50) explains that.

**Not yet** · There is no note field: the price is saved without a comment. You cannot upload prices in bulk. One save covers one room type over a run of nights, so a season across three room types is three saves. You cannot set a price per rate plan: MAYA writes one base rate per room type. You cannot type a price on a night that has passed.

On a night MAYA has already sent a price to and confirmed, a rate you change in your property system an hour or more later is kept as your price and marked "Changed in Cloudbeds". On a night MAYA has never sent to, your rate becomes the starting point, and your rules work from it. Setting a night to 0 in your system closes it.

Which case a night falls into depends on one thing: whether MAYA has already sent a price to that night and confirmed it landed.

**MAYA has sent to the night.** Your change is read as a decision. It becomes a manual price for that night and room type, exactly as if you had typed it in MAYA: rules that had already moved the night are paused for that room type, rules that fire later stack on top of your number, and **Clear** hands the night back. [Setting a price yourself](@49) explains what a manual price does.
MAYA has sent to the night

**MAYA has never sent to the night.** That includes every night before you first go live, and any night beyond the 60-night window. Your rate is read as the property's own rate for that night, the starting point. When a rule fires, it works from your number. When no rule fires, your number is the price.

**Example: The Harbour Inn, one change in each case**

Sam changes two Standard rates in Cloudbeds on the morning of Friday, October 2, 2026.

Friday, November 13, 2026: MAYA sent $165.00 to that night two days ago and Cloudbeds confirmed it. Sam changes it to $175.00. Within the hour MAYA reads the change and keeps it. The night shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $175.00" and the change log reads "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $175.00." When "Busy nights" fires later, it raises the night 10% from $175.00, not from $150.00.
MAYA has never sent to the night

If you change a rate in your system instead, give the night an hour after MAYA last sent to it (an hour or two on ThinkReservations). Change the rate MAYA writes to: the base rate in Cloudbeds, usually the Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. Then, while you are live, your change on a night MAYA has sent to is kept as your price when MAYA next reads it.

**Example: The exact conditions**

On a night MAYA has sent to, your change is kept only when all of these hold:

- You are live. In simulation nothing is sent, so nothing is read as a change (see "Changes made while simulating" below).
- MAYA's last send to that night landed and was confirmed. Cloudbeds reports that the job applied. ThinkReservations only accepts the price, so MAYA counts it as confirmed once its hourly read finds the price there.

- Your change is on the same rate plan MAYA writes to. In Cloudbeds that is the base rate. In ThinkReservations it is the rate type named Best Available, or, if none is, the standard rate type that covers the most room types. A change to another rate plan is not read.
- The new rate differs from MAYA's price by more than half a cent, and is not MAYA's price rounded to a whole unit.
- No newer price typed in MAYA is still on its way to that night.
- The difference is not one shared by nearly every night. That covers tax, a markup, or a raise of one percentage across the board (see "Prices with tax or a markup" below).
- The send landed after you last went live. A rate changed while simulating is a starting point, not a manual price.

MAYA reads your own rates for every night in the 60-night window about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes. It also reads a night again right before sending a new price to it, when the night was last sent to over an hour ago and the hourly read did not run this cycle. So a change on a sent night is read within about an hour, and usually before MAYA sends a new price to that night. The exceptions are a cycle in which MAYA could not read your system, and a change made within an hour of MAYA's send.

A night beyond the window is not read until it enters the window.

On the calendar, the room type's card shows an amber badge reading "Changed in Cloudbeds · $175.00" (or "Changed in Think Reservations · $175.00"). Hover it for "Seen" and the date and time MAYA read the change, in your browser's clock. A price typed in MAYA shows "Manual" instead, with "Set" on hover.

In the change log the entry names no person: "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $175.00." A rule that fires later on that night adds its sentence after it.

**Clear** on the card works the same as for a typed price. Hover it and it reads "Changed in Cloudbeds. Clear hands the night back to MAYA."

Say you meant $150 for a Standard night and typed $15 in Cloudbeds. What happens depends on the same two cases.

**On a night MAYA has sent to**, your $15 is kept as your price, like any change of yours, and the card shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $15.00". The floor does not catch it. A price you set yourself is published as you set it, even under the floor, so $15 stays in your system. Rules that fire later work from $15.
On a night MAYA has sent to

**On a night MAYA has never sent to**, $15 becomes the night's starting point. Your rules work from it and the floor holds the result: with Standard's $80 floor, MAYA publishes $80 (and sends it when you are live). That is not your $150 either. A floor still at $1.00 would let the $15 through.

A rate typed too high works the same way, with the ceiling in place of the floor. To put it right, do one of these:
On a night MAYA has never sent to
- **Press **Clear** in MAYA** on a night marked "Changed in Cloudbeds". The night goes back to your rules, from the starting point MAYA had before your typo, and MAYA's price is sent over the $15.
Press Clear in MAYA
- **Type the right price in MAYA.** It is kept at once and, when you are live, sent straight away.
Type the right price in MAYA

- **Correct the rate in your system.** MAYA reads it within about an hour. On a night MAYA has sent to, it is kept as your price, the same way the typo was. On any other night it becomes the starting point.

Clearing or typing a price in MAYA needs Revenue Manager access or higher. On Mews, MAYA does not read rates, so a rate mistyped in Mews stays as it is until you correct it there.
Correct the rate in your system

If you were live before and went back to simulation, a rate you change in your system on a night MAYA sent to during the live stretch is not read while you simulate. MAYA's prices for that night keep starting from the old starting point. When you go live again, that rate is read as the night's starting point, and your rules work from it.

Set a night's rate to 0 in your system and MAYA reads it as closed.

- On a night MAYA has sent to, the starting point becomes 0, MAYA stops pricing that night and sends nothing to it. Any manual price on that night is cleared, and the rules it paused are released. This needs you to be live and the 0 to be on the rate plan MAYA writes to. MAYA's last send to the night must also have gone through over an hour ago. It does not need to be confirmed, because MAYA never sends 0 itself.
- On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate of 0 is left unpriced from the start. MAYA does not open a closed night at the floor.

Open the night again by loading a rate in your system. The next hourly read takes that rate as the starting point, and your rules work from it.

A 0 in your system does not close a night MAYA has sent to in three cases:

- **A comp night you set in MAYA.** A typed price of 0 makes the night free, so a 0 in your system for that night matches your price rather than closing the night. [Setting a price yourself](@49) covers comp nights.
A comp night you set in MAYA

- **A manual price whose last send was never confirmed.** The night is held rather than closed, since that price may never have reached your system. The manual price stays, and MAYA sends nothing new to the night while your system has 0.
A manual price whose last send was never confirmed
- **A newer price typed in MAYA that is still on its way.** Your typed price is kept and sent as usual.
A newer price typed in MAYA that is still on its way

Some systems report rates through a rule of their own: tax included, or a markup on every night. Those rates all differ from MAYA's price by the same ratio, and reading each one as a change of yours would freeze the window at inflated prices.

So when 80% or more of the sent nights MAYA reads (10 nights at least) differ from its price by one shared ratio, MAYA reads that as your system's rule, not as edits. None of those nights is kept, and nothing shows on the calendar. MAYA's next price for each of them is sent as usual. A night that does not fit the ratio is still read as a change of yours. If your prices in your system look like MAYA's plus tax, that is why, and nothing needs doing.

The same check catches a change you make yourself. Say you are live and you raise every rate by 10% in Cloudbeds. Every sent night now differs from MAYA's price by the same ratio, so MAYA reads your raise as your system's own arithmetic, not as your prices. None of the new rates is kept as a manual price, and nothing shows on the calendar.

Your raised rates stay in your system until MAYA's price for a night next changes. MAYA then sends its new price for that night, worked out from the starting point it had before your raise, so your 10% is gone from that night. Nights change at different times, so for a while some nights carry your raise and some do not. A Standard night MAYA sent at $165.00 reads $181.50 in Cloudbeds after your raise, until MAYA's price for that night next moves.

To move a lot of nights at once, type the prices in MAYA. One save covers one room type and a run of nights at one price, using **through…**. Each night is kept at once as a manual price, and rules that fire later stack on it. [Setting a price yourself](@49) has the detail.

Or change rates in your system only on nights MAYA has not sent to yet, such as nights more than 59 nights ahead. Each of those rates becomes the night's starting point when the night enters the window, and your rules work from it.

|  | In MAYA (the calendar) | In your property system |
|---|---|---|
| Takes effect | At once, and sent straight away when you are live | Within about an hour |
| Which nights | Tonight to 364 days ahead | Only nights MAYA has sent to; any other night becomes a starting point instead |
| Who did it | Named in the change log | "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds", no name |
| A run of nights | One save with **through…** | Night by night, as your system allows |
| Undo | **Clear** | **Clear** in MAYA |

When you mean to set a price, type it in MAYA. Change it in your system when that is where you happen to be, and give MAYA's send an hour first. A change of one percentage to nearly every sent night is not kept (see "Raising every night by the same percentage" above).

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes to the base rate of each room type in Cloudbeds, the rate plan that does not follow another plan. Change that rate and MAYA reads it. A change to a derived plan or a package is not read. Cloudbeds confirms MAYA's sends, so the hour starts when the send goes out.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes to the rate type named Best Available, or, if none is, to the standard rate type that covers the most room types. Change that rate and MAYA reads it. ThinkReservations accepts a price without confirming it applied, so MAYA counts a send as confirmed only once its hourly read finds the price there. A change you make before that read is not kept and is written over by MAYA's next price change. Give a night an hour or two after MAYA's send.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read rates from Mews and does not send prices to Mews. A rate you change in Mews is neither shown in MAYA nor written over. To set a price in MAYA for a Mews property, type it on the calendar. To change the rate guests see, change it in Mews.

A rate the front desk gives one guest lives on that guest's booking, not on your base rate. MAYA does not read it as a change to your rates, and it does not change the price MAYA sends for that night.

The booking counts like any other. It adds to the night's occupancy, booking speed and pickup count. Its rate counts in that night's room revenue and in the ADR (the average rate per room booked) on the calendar, at the rate MAYA read with the booking. Occupancy, booking window and booking speed rules, and pickup rules that count room nights, do not look at what a guest paid. A pickup rule set to measure revenue adds up the rates on the night's bookings, special rates included, so a special rate does move that rule's number.

A booking's rate reaches a price only as a starting point, and only when MAYA has no rate of yours for that night and room type. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, MAYA reads your base rate for every night in the window, so a booking's rate is used only on a night where no rate could be read. On Mews, MAYA does not read rates, so a night starts from the rate on the newest booking MAYA has read for that room type. With no booking yet, it starts from the starting point saved on the last run. A special rate on that newest booking becomes the night's starting point in MAYA until a newer booking arrives. Changing the rate on a booking MAYA has already read does not move the starting point.

The **PMS** tab lists your room types as your property system reports them, with their unit counts. Untick **Counts as a room** for anything nobody sleeps in, and MAYA leaves it out of occupancy and your bill. It is still priced, and sent when you are live, like any other room type. Add **Rooms out of service** for units off sale for a stretch, so occupancy reads against what you can really sell.

Open the **PMS** tab. Under the connection cards sits a section headed **Room types**, with a **?** beside the heading. Everyone on the property can see it. Changing anything here needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

One row per active room type, in name order. Each row shows the room type's name, its unit count ("12 units"), a small "not a room" tag when it is unticked, and the checkbox **Counts as a room**. A room type that does not count is dimmed.

While the list loads you see a grey placeholder. If it cannot load: "Couldn't load room types." with **Try again**. Before the first sync: "No room types have synced yet."

A ticked room type is one guests sleep in. Ticked room types are what MAYA divides by. They make up:

- the sellable count behind sellable occupancy, on the day card and in every occupancy rule,
- the room count behind the calendar's colours (revenue per room),
- the room count you are billed for.

One exception on the bill: a room type nobody has answered for yet, whose name reads like something nobody sleeps in, shows ticked but is left out of your bill until you answer (see "How MAYA proposes the answer" below).

Untick a room type and it leaves all three. Its bookings also leave the history booking speed reads, so a court selling six slots a night cannot read as the hotel filling up. It is still priced, and sent when you are live, like any other room type, and its revenue still counts in the day card's dollar figure.

Tick or untick and the change saves at once. If it does not save you see "That didn't save" with a note to try again, and the box goes back to where it was. Your rules then run again across the 60-night window, since every occupancy figure has moved. Each change is recorded with who made it.

**Example: The Harbour Inn's meeting room**

Cloudbeds lists four room types at The Harbour Inn: Standard (12), Deluxe (6), Suite (2) and Meeting Room (1). With Meeting Room unticked, the property has 20 rooms, not 21. A night with 12 rooms booked reads "12/20 rooms" and 60%. If the meeting room is booked that night, its revenue is in the dollar figure, and the percentage stays 60%. Sam is billed for 20 rooms.

After that, MAYA never unticks a room type on its own. A new room type from your system arrives counted as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it stays unanswered: it shows ticked and counts in occupancy (your existing rules do not include it, see "What a new room type starts with" below), but it is left out of your bill until you answer. To answer, untick it, or, if it is a room, untick it and tick it again. A sync never overwrites an answer you have given. You can change any room type from the **PMS** tab at any time.

Under each room type, click **+ Rooms out of service**. A short form opens:

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| **From** | The first night the rooms are off sale. Required. |
| **To** | The last night. Leave it empty for one night. |
| **Units** | How many rooms, from 1 up to the room type's unit count. |
| **Reason (optional)** | A few words, up to 200 characters. "Renovation" is the hint. |

Click **Save** (it reads **Saving…** while it works) or **Cancel**. The block then lists under the room type as "2 out of service", the first and last night, "· Renovation", and **Clear**.

For those nights only, the units come off the room type's sellable count, for your rules and on the calendar day card. Occupancy then reads against what you can sell, so an occupancy rule does not stay quiet because a renovated wing looks empty. Nothing is sent to your property system. Your rules run again across the 60-night window as soon as you save.

**Example: Two Standard rooms under renovation**

The Harbour Inn takes 2 Standard rooms off sale from November 10 to November 20, 2026. On those nights the property has 18 sellable rooms, so a night with 11 rooms booked reads "11/18 rooms" and 61% instead of 55%. With 15 rooms booked, "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80) fires at 15 of 18, which is 83%. Without the block, 15 of 20 is 75% and the rule would stay quiet.

| Rule | What the screen says |
