| One block covers at most 366 nights | "One block can cover at most 366 nights." |
| Units are whole numbers from 1 | "Units must be a whole number of at least 1." |
| Not more units than the room type has | "Standard has 12 rooms" followed by a note that you cannot block more than that. |
| Blocks stack night by night, never past the count | "Standard already has 8 rooms out of service on some of those nights" followed by how many you can still block. |
| Reason under 200 characters | "Keep the reason under 200 characters." |
| Real dates, last night not before the first | "End date can't be before the start date." |
| Revenue Manager or higher | "This needs Revenue Manager access or higher on this property." |
| 30 changes per person per 10 minutes, shared with typed prices | "That's a lot of changes at once. Give it a minute and try again." |

Click **Clear** beside the block. The rooms are back on sale from the next run, which starts at once. MAYA keeps a record of the block and who cleared it, but it no longer shows. A block already cleared by someone else answers "That block is already cleared."

There is no edit. To change a block's dates or units, clear it and add a new one.

A block changes occupancy only. Booking speed counts the bookings a night has received against what similar past nights had, and a room off sale changes neither count. [Booking speed](@34) explains the count.

MAYA reads bookings and rates from your system, not room blocks, out-of-order rooms or allotments. A wing you close in Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations or Mews still counts as sellable in MAYA until you enter it here. This is also why MAYA's occupancy can differ from your system's headline figure. [Occupancy looks wrong](@98) walks through the differences.

**Cloudbeds:** A new room type appears in MAYA on the next cycle, about five minutes, counted as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it stays unanswered: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you tick or untick it on the **PMS** tab. A changed unit count is picked up on the next cycle, from the count Cloudbeds reports for the room type. A renamed room type shows its new name on the next cycle.

**ThinkReservations:** A new room type appears in MAYA on the next cycle, about five minutes, counted as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it stays unanswered: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you tick or untick it on the **PMS** tab. A room type you remove stays in MAYA with its history. ThinkReservations does not report how many rooms a room type has, so MAYA gives every ThinkReservations room type the same number of units, 100 until we change it. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) your counts. Once we have set the number, occupancy is right from the next run if your room types are all the same size. A renamed room type shows its new name on the next cycle.

**Mews:** A new space category appears in MAYA as a room type on the next cycle, about five minutes, counted as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it stays unanswered: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you tick or untick it on the **PMS** tab. A category you remove stays in MAYA with its history. Mews does not report how many rooms a category has, so MAYA gives every Mews category the same number of units: the number we set with you when we connect Mews, or 100 if it was never set. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) your counts. Once we have set the number, occupancy is right from the next run if your categories are all the same size. A renamed category shows its new name on the next cycle.

Delete a room type in your system and create it again, and your system treats it as a new room type. So does MAYA, even when the name is the same. Nothing carries over from the old one. The old one stays in MAYA as the tabs above describe, so for a while you may see two room types with the same name. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Switch%20off%20a%20room%20type) and we switch the old one off.

A brand new room type, or a rebuilt one, starts like this:

- **Your rules do not cover it.** A rule covers the room types that were selected when you saved it. A room type added later is not in any of your rules, not even one that covered every room type you had. That goes for rules you built and for the starter rules. The **Room Types** column on the **Rules** tab shows what each rule changes.
Your rules do not cover it

- **It has no history.** The old type's past stays remain under the old type, so the new one starts with none. A booking speed rule that measures only the new type has nothing to compare with, so it stays quiet at first. Once the type has bookings of its own, readings with fewer than 5 similar nights are capped at one step.
It has no history

- **Occupancy works at once.** An occupancy rule that measures it reads its bookings against its units from the first cycle. A pickup count rule that measures it waits until MAYA has kept a record of the type for the whole lookback (1, 3 or 7 days).
Occupancy works at once

- **Its floor and ceiling are MAYA's defaults**, $1.00 and $99,999.99, which stop nothing in most currencies (where a room sells above 99,999.99, the default ceiling holds its price down). They stay there until real ones are set for it. A suggestion card is the quickest way (below).
Its floor and ceiling are MAYA's defaults
- **Prices you typed stay with the old type.** A manual price belongs to one room type, so the new type starts without any.
Prices you typed stay with the old type

- **On ThinkReservations and Mews, it gets the same unit count as your other room types**, as the ThinkReservations and Mews tabs above explain.

To bring the new type into your pricing, add a rule for it, or change an existing rule to include it. A saved rule cannot take on a room type, so changing one means deleting it and adding it again with the new type selected. [Change a rule](@71) walks through it.
On ThinkReservations and Mews, it gets the same unit count as your other room types

Twelve rooms, two out of service, nine booked: 90% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.

**Not yet** · You cannot switch a room type off in MAYA or rename it. Names and unit counts come from your property system. The one exception is a duplicate found at import, which the review screen can hide. You cannot edit a block: clear it and add another. Floors and ceilings are not set here. [Floors and ceilings](@28) explains where they are.

The **PMS** tab shows whether your property system is connected, how the last 24 hours of requests to it went, when bookings last synced, and the most recent requests MAYA made. Problems sending prices are not here. They are in the change log. When the connection breaks on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, a General Manager or Hotel Admin sees a **Reconnect** button here (and above the calendar once this tab has been opened in that visit). On Mews, the panel asks you to send us a message.

The **PMS** tab is the last of the five tabs. Everyone on the property can open it. The heading reads "Property System (Cloudbeds)", with your system's name in brackets once connected, and one line under it: "Bookings sync automatically on a schedule. This page shows how that connection is doing."

Before it loads: "Loading connection status…". With no property chosen: "Select a property to view status." With no system connected yet: "No property system is connected for this property yet."

The **Room types** section sits under the connection cards on the same tab. [Room types and rooms out of service](@51) covers it.

A single word, colour-coded. It is the state of the connection as MAYA last recorded it.

| Word | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Connected (green) | Healthy. MAYA reads bookings and, when you are live, sends prices. | Nothing. |
| Pending (amber) | Connected but not yet paid for. Nothing runs. | Finish setting up payment. |
| Degraded (amber) | Still working. MAYA keeps reading bookings and, when you are live, sending prices. Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only. | Usually nothing: it tends to clear by itself on the next read. If it is still there in an hour, click Reconnect. It does no harm. |
| Error (red) | Your system rejected MAYA's saved access. Syncing has stopped. | Reconnect. |
| Disconnected (red) | MAYA's access is gone: the app was uninstalled, its permission removed, or your system refused it. Nothing runs until someone reconnects. | Reconnect. |
| unknown (grey) | MAYA has no status on file for the connection yet. | Open the tab again in a few minutes. If it stays, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Connection%20status%20unknown). |

Degraded looks more worrying than it is. While the card reads Degraded, the amber panel headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system's name) shows anyway, and says your prices aren't updating. For Degraded that line is not true: nothing has stopped and nothing is lost.

The Health card below has a "Degraded" of its own, about failed requests. The two are separate.

How the requests MAYA made to your system in the last 24 hours went. It counts every request, reads and writes alike.

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Healthy | 98% or more of the requests succeeded. |
| Degraded | 80% to under 98% succeeded. |
| Having trouble | Under 80% succeeded. |
| No recent activity | No requests in the last 24 hours. |

Beside the badge: "97% of 412 requests OK".

A short spell of "Degraded" is normal when your system is slow or asks MAYA to wait. "Having trouble" for more than an hour, with a Connection card that is not green, means it is time to reconnect. [Connection lost](@100) walks through the cases.

The last time MAYA read your bookings successfully. It shows as a raw timestamp in UTC, the world reference time, for example 2026-09-22T22:05:12.345+00:00. The +00:00 at the end means UTC, so that one is 3:05 PM in US Pacific time. A dash means it has never read them. On a healthy connection this time is at most a few minutes old, because MAYA reads about every five minutes.

Under the cards is a technical list of MAYA's last 50 requests to Cloudbeds, headed "Recent requests to Cloudbeds". You do not need to read it. If you email us about the connection, it helps us. A request that failed shows its status code, or ERR, in red. Its times show in the same raw UTC form as Last sync. Requests are kept for 7 days. When there are none, it reads "No requests recorded yet".

**Cloudbeds:** The table fills with every request MAYA makes to Cloudbeds, and the Health card is built from the same list.

**ThinkReservations:** Requests to ThinkReservations are not written to this table today. The table stays on "No requests recorded yet" and the Health card reads "No recent activity" even when the connection is working. Read the Connection card and Last sync instead.

Above the cards, what you see depends on the Connection card and on your role. Broken means the card reads Error, Degraded or Disconnected. Any other word counts as not broken.

- **Not broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin:** a quiet link, **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. Use it if you have been asked to, for example after your system's permissions changed.
Not broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin

- **Broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin:** an amber panel headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" with the button **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. One click sends you to your system to confirm and brings you back. Your rules, history and settings are untouched.
Broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin
- **Broken, any system, Revenue Manager or Viewer:** the same heading, with a note to ask the property's General Manager or Hotel Admin, since it takes them one click.
Broken, any system, Revenue Manager or Viewer

- **Broken, Mews, General Manager or Hotel Admin:** a panel headed "Mews needs its keys re-entered", asking you to send us a message. Mews connects with keys from your Mews account rather than a login, so it cannot be repaired from this screen.

The same panel appears as a banner above the calendar while the connection is broken, once you have opened the **PMS** tab in this visit. Until then the change log's "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" item points you here with "Reconnect Cloudbeds on the PMS tab." [Reconnect and disconnect](@16) has the full walk-through.

**Example: The Harbour Inn on a quiet Tuesday**

Sam opens the **PMS** tab. Connection reads Connected. Health reads Healthy, "99% of 412 requests OK". Last sync reads "2026-09-22T22:05:12.345+00:00", which is 3:05 PM that afternoon at The Harbour Inn. Under the cards, the newest request is from a minute ago. Nothing needs doing.

In simulation MAYA does everything it would do for a live property except the last step. About every five minutes it reads your bookings. About once an hour it reads your own rates for the nights ahead (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations). Every cycle it runs every rule over tonight and the next 59 nights and writes the result to the calendar and the change log. Then it stops. No price leaves MAYA.

No. Connecting starts the history import (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) and the first cycles, all in simulation. The rates in your system do not move until someone with General Manager or Hotel Admin access clicks **Turn them on for real** on the review screen and confirms, or we switch the property live at your request. There is no separate demo or test property. Simulation is the look before you send: your own bookings, your own rules, real numbers, and nothing sent.

| Reads your own rates about once an hour (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) | Yes | Yes |

One rule
- **A new rule.** A rule you save from the **Rate Simulator** tab starts switched off, so it moves nothing until you turn it on. A rule you add with **Add Rule** on the **Rules** tab is on at once.

MAYA enforces none of these checks. Each one saves a surprise.

Start with [the checklist for your property system](@20): a base rate of its own for every room type, rates loaded for tonight and the next 59 nights, your time zone confirmed with us, anything nobody sleeps in unticked under **Counts as a room**, blocked rooms recorded, and floors and ceilings set. Load those rates before you go live. Your rules start from your own rate for each night, and a night your system has at 0 is left alone.

Then four checks in MAYA itself.

1. **Floors and ceilings.** Each room type has a floor and a ceiling: the lowest and highest price that can go out for it.
  - **Where to see them.** The **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab shows them for every room type that counts as a room. Your answers to the five questions set some of them, and the import filled others from your own past rates where there was enough history.
  - **A limit still at $1.00 or $99,999.99** stops nothing in most currencies. To set it, answer the floor or ceiling question again at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions (your floor answer goes to every room type at once), or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) the number. Wait until you are live before you press **Get suggestions from my data**: pressing it earlier removes the go-live button from the review.
Floors and ceilings

2. **Starter rules.** They are on, and the prices they set already show on the calendar. Turning a rule **Off** keeps every change it has made to your prices so far, even in simulation, and those prices go out when you go live. To be rid of a starter rule and what it did, **Delete** it and choose **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**. Turn it off only if you are happy for its changes so far to be sent.
Starter rules

3. **Watch for a week.** Open the change log a few times a day (it shows about the last 50 minutes), check the **Fired** column on the **Rules** tab to see which rules act most, and copy any entry you want to keep. If a price would have surprised you, change the rule or the limit before you go live.
Watch for a week

4. **Switch off other pricing tools.** If another tool changes rates in your system, switch it off before you go live. MAYA reads a rate another tool changes the same way as a rate you change by hand. [Rates you change in your property system](@50) says what happens to those.

**Example: Selling in yen, won or rupiah**

The default ceiling is the plain number 99,999.99 in your property's currency. Say a Suite sells at ¥120,000 a night and its ceiling is still the default. On a night where no rule fires, the price that goes out is ¥99,999.99, because every price is kept under the room type's ceiling. Give a room type like this a real ceiling before you go live.
Switch off other pricing tools

You can come back to that screen at any time at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. If it opens on "First: does this match reality?", click **Continue to recommendations**. The card is near the end of the next screen. The dashboard has no go-live button of its own. The blue banner on the dashboard that points to the review appears only while the review still has cards you have not looked at.

There is no way to schedule going live for a later date, such as next Monday morning. Sending starts on the next cycle after a General Manager or Hotel Admin confirms, so click the button when you want sending to start, after switching off any other tool that changes your rates. If we switch you live by email, send the email when you want sending to start.

**Not yet: No card, no button** · The card appears only when setup built starter rules for you. They need at least 60 days of booking history from the history import, which runs for Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations but not yet for Mews. The card also goes once anyone on your team runs **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. Without the card, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) with your property name and we switch the property live for you.

Clicking **Turn them on for real** opens a small dialog. Nothing happens until you click **Go live** inside it. **Not yet**, or the Escape key, closes it and leaves you in simulation. While the switch is being made the button reads "Switching…". The words in the dialog depend on your property system.

**Cloudbeds:** The title is "Send prices to Cloudbeds?", followed by two sentences:

"MAYA starts sending its prices for the next 60 nights to Cloudbeds on the next cycle, in about 5 minutes."

"Each price it sends replaces that night's rate in Cloudbeds, and a night is sent again whenever its price changes."

**ThinkReservations:** The title is "Send prices to Think Reservations?", followed by two sentences:

"MAYA starts sending its prices for the next 60 nights to Think Reservations on the next cycle, in about 5 minutes."

**Mews:** A Mews property has no go-live button, and nothing would be sent to Mews anyway. Your rules run and show their prices either way. There is no history import for Mews yet, so there are no starter rules and no card on the review screen.

We can switch a Mews property to live if you ask. That sends nothing to Mews. It only changes wording in MAYA: the amber banner says "has raised" instead of "would have raised", and a typed price's confirmation says it is sending to Mews although nothing is sent. [Mews: what works today](@14) explains what MAYA does for a Mews property.

Under those lines, above the buttons, one more sentence: "Going live sends these rates to your PMS automatically. You're confirming you've reviewed your rules and limits (Terms 3.3)." The word "Terms" is a link to the Terms of Service.

If the switch fails for a reason other than your role, the dialog stays open and shows the reason above the buttons. It is the reason MAYA sent back, or your browser's own words if the connection dropped. When no reason came back at all, it reads "Couldn't switch to live. Try again." Click **Go live** once more. "Not signed in" means your session has ended: sign in again and come back to the review screen. If it keeps failing, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live%20failed) with the words you see.

For each room type MAYA writes one nightly rate to one rate plan in your system: the base rate in Cloudbeds, the Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. The number that was there is replaced by the price your rules set for that night. That price starts from the rate you had, so on a night where no rule fired the number that goes out is your own rate, kept between that room type's floor and ceiling. If your rate is under the floor or over the ceiling, the floor or ceiling goes out instead, so check the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab first.

Rate plans that follow the base rate (derived plans, and packages built on it) move as your system's own rules move them. MAYA never writes those directly. [How prices reach your property system](@55) has the detail.

Clause 3.3 of the Terms of Service says who can switch a property to live: a General Manager or Hotel Admin, or another role we designate, and you choose who holds those roles. It treats your click on **Go live** as your confirmation of two things. First, that you have reviewed the property's rules and limits: every active rule, whether you wrote it or MAYA built it, and every floor and ceiling. Second, that you accept responsibility for every rate MAYA publishes for the property. It also says that if we switch a property live at your request or with your permission, we act on your instruction. That is why the sentence sits beside the button rather than in Terms accepted weeks earlier, possibly by someone else. [Terms and legal](@109) has the clause.

- Who clicked the button, the version of the Terms shown on the screen, your IP address and your browser. This is kept as the record of the go-live.
- The moment the property went live. It matters later: a rate you changed in your system while simulating is read as your base rate, not as a manual price, and this moment is how MAYA tells the two apart.
- A request to read your own rates again before the first send.

Nothing else changes. Your rules, your floors and ceilings, your history, your manual prices and your team are exactly as they were. Going live flips one switch.
1. **The button becomes a pill**: "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices".
The button becomes a pill

2. **The next cycle reads your rates first.** Cycles run about every five minutes. The first live cycle reads your own rate for every night in the window before it prices. Whatever you had in your system at that moment is the starting point your rules work from.
The next cycle reads your rates first

3. **Then it sends.** Prices for tonight and the next 59 nights go out, nearest nights first, in batches. Nothing has been sent before, so every priced night goes out on this first send: nights where a rule fired at the rule's price, nights where none fired at your own rate (kept between the room type's floor and ceiling), and a price you typed while simulating as typed. A change made while simulating by a rule you have since turned off goes out too.
Then it sends

4. **After that, changes only.** A night is sent again when its price changes. A cycle where nothing changed sends nothing.

Everything about what is sent, held back, confirmed and retried is on [How prices reach your property system](@55).
After that, changes only

Usually on the next cycle, so about five minutes. Cloudbeds applies each price a few seconds after receiving it. ThinkReservations accepts each send and applies it shortly after.

It takes longer when the first read of your rates fails or runs out of time (the first send waits for the next cycle that reads them), when your property is large (a big first send continues on the next cycle), or when your system asks MAYA to slow down. If nothing has changed in your system after 15 minutes, open the change log. A problem that needs you appears there as "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds". [Prices are not reaching your property system](@99) walks through what to check.
Yes. A property on its free trial is treated as paid for everything MAYA does, sending included. The only gate on going live is your role.

Not yet. The switch is for the whole property. What you can do instead: a rule only changes the room types you tick under **Apply to room types**, so a room type no rule names is sent at your own rate, kept between its floor and ceiling. Its number in your system does not move unless your rate sits under its floor or over its ceiling, and then the floor or ceiling goes out instead. There is no way to keep a room type out of sending altogether.

**Careful: One-way in the app** · There is no switch to put a property back into simulation. To pause, turn your rules off (the prices they set stay). To go back to simulation, email us. [Pausing, or going back to simulation](@57) covers both.

At about 3:10 PM the next cycle reads the Harbour Inn's Cloudbeds rates for the 60 nights, then runs the rules. "Busy nights" has fired on two Friday nights in November, so on those two Fridays Standard goes out at $165, Deluxe at $220 and Suite at $330. Every other night goes out at the rates Sam already had: Standard $150, Deluxe $200, Suite $300. Cloudbeds' derived plans follow their base rates by Cloudbeds' own rules.

At about 3:15 PM the next cycle finds nothing changed and sends nothing. On Thursday a booking takes another night over 80% full. "Busy nights" fires, and only that night's three room types are sent.

Every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA sends the prices that changed since the last successful send, for nights from today to 59 days out, one nightly rate per room type. Cloudbeds applies each price a few seconds after receiving it and tells MAYA when it is done. ThinkReservations accepts each price and applies it shortly after, and MAYA's hourly read then finds it there. If a price never appears in your system, MAYA does not send it again until the night's price changes, so compare the night in both places and email us. Mews receives nothing.

About every five minutes MAYA runs one cycle for your property. It reads your bookings. If an hour has passed, or your hotel day has changed, it reads your own rates for the window too. It runs every rule over tonight and the next 59 nights. Then, if the property is live, it sends the prices that changed. A cycle where nothing changed sends nothing. About once a day MAYA reads every booking again, so anything missed is picked up within the day. [How rules run](@39) covers what happens inside the rules step.

A price you type is the one thing that does not wait for the cycle. On a live property the save runs the rules for those nights at once and asks MAYA to send them now. The confirmation says "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." If that nudge cannot be made, it says "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds on the next cycle (about 5 min)."
- **Every cycle**, changed prices only, live properties only.
Every cycle
- **Now**, after you save a typed price. If another run is busy with your property, the nudge waits up to a minute and then leaves the price to the next cycle.
Now
- **Not on a cycle where the read of your bookings failed.** Nothing is priced or sent on stale bookings. The next cycle reads again.
Not on a cycle where the read of your bookings failed

- **Not until a read of your bookings has finished.** Your rules run on what has arrived, but MAYA sends nothing until a read of your bookings has finished. On a large property that read can take more than one cycle.
Not until a read of your bookings has finished

Nights beyond the window are not sent, and the cycle does not price them. Each morning, at your property's day change, one more night enters the window and is priced and sent from then on. Your own base rate is read only inside the window too. So going live sends the 60 nights of the window, and nothing beyond them until each night's turn comes.

A price you type can reach further: up to 364 days ahead. It is saved, shown on the calendar and sent on the cycle after its night enters the window. The confirmation says "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 60-day push window." For a range that crosses the edge it says how many nights go now and how many wait: "Saved. 12 nights sending to Cloudbeds now; 8 more will be sent as they enter the 60-day window."

When you save or clear a price further ahead, MAYA runs your rules past the window. It runs them over every night from tonight to the last night you chose. That is the only time rules run beyond the window.

Out there MAYA has none of your own rates to start from. A night is priced only when it has another starting point, such as a booking for that room type or a price you typed. Those nights show a Current price on the calendar. None of them is sent until it enters the window, where the cycle prices it again.

Nights before your property's today are never sent. Tonight stays in the window, priced and sent like any other night, until midnight at the property. After that it leaves the window.

A night is sent again only when MAYA's price for it changes. If the last successful send to that night was at the same price, to the same rate plan, the night is skipped. That is why a quiet property can go hours with nothing sent, and why the change log's runs often read "Prices checked" with no change.

One exception: a night is sent again at the same price when the rate plan behind its room type changes in your system, for example after a base rate is replaced or the rate catalogue is rebuilt. MAYA re-reads which plan each room type maps to and sends the night to the new one. If you have renamed or rebuilt your rate plans and prices have stopped landing, [Prices are not reaching your property system](@99) has the steps.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type, to that room type's **base rate**: the rate plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name of its own. Every other plan for the room type is left alone. A package, a long-stay plan or any other independent plan is never written, even when the room type has no base rate. A room type with no base rate is left out, and the change log tells you (see "MAYA can't find a base rate" on [When your property system does not accept a price](@56)).

Plans that follow the base rate (derived plans) move by Cloudbeds' own rules when the base rate moves. Booking channels take their rates from Cloudbeds as before. MAYA does not talk to channels.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type, to the property's **Best Available** rate type. ThinkReservations marks a rate type as standard or derived, and a non-refundable rate or a package is standard too, so the rate type MAYA writes to is set by its name. MAYA writes to the standard rate types whose name includes "Best Available". If none has that name, it writes to the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. If two cover the same number, it writes to neither, and nothing is sent until you name one Best Available.

A room type that no base rate type covers is left out, and the change log tells you. Derived rate types reprice themselves from their parent, so writing the parent is the whole job.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews. MAYA reads Mews bookings and room categories, runs your rules and shows the prices it would send, and stops there. It does not read Mews rates either, so a Mews night's starting price comes from your bookings rather than from a rate calendar.

A price you type on a Mews property is saved and shown but not sent. On a live Mews property the confirmation still says it is sending, for example "Saved. Sending to Mews now." That is wrong: nothing is sent. Ignore it. [Mews: what works today](@14) has the full picture.

Whatever your system, it is one price per room type per night. MAYA cannot send a different price to each rate plan, and it never creates a rate plan, a restriction, a minimum stay or a close-out.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds applies each price a few seconds after receiving it and tells MAYA when it is done. Right after sending, MAYA asks Cloudbeds how each send went, waits a few seconds for any still being applied, and keeps asking on later cycles for up to 60 minutes.

- A send Cloudbeds reports as applied cleanly counts as landed.
- A send Cloudbeds reports as failed, or applied with a complaint, counts as refused. A cause that clears on its own is retried. A cause that needs you is held. [When your property system does not accept a price](@56) lists each cause and when you are told.
- A send still listed as unfinished 45 minutes after it went out is treated as not applied and the night is sent again.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations answers each send with "accepted" and applies it shortly after. It tells MAYA nothing more after that. MAYA's check that the price is there comes with its next hourly read of your rates. If a price never appears, MAYA does not send it again until the night's price changes, so compare the night in both places and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Price%20not%20in%20ThinkReservations).

Until that read, MAYA cannot tell whether the rate is there yet. Two things follow. MAYA does not promise the write is instant, only that it is accepted and then checked within about an hour. And a rate you change in ThinkReservations on that night before MAYA has read its own price back is not kept: the next price change writes over it. [Rates you change in your property system](@50) has the rule.

MAYA's part ends at your property system. A price that changes is sent on that cycle, to the room type's base rate there, and to nothing else. Your booking engine, your channel manager, Booking.com, Expedia and every other channel take their rates from your system, on their own timing, as they did before MAYA. MAYA does not talk to any of them, so it cannot hurry them and cannot tell you how long they take.

So when MAYA shows a new price and a channel still shows the old one, check your property system first. Look at the room type's base rate for that night.

- **Your system still has the old rate.** The price has not reached it yet. A price that changed in the last few minutes may not have gone out. If it is older than that, read [Prices are not reaching your property system](@99).
Your system still has the old rate
- **Your system has MAYA's price.** MAYA's part is done, and the wait is on the channel's side. Ask your channel manager, or your system's support, how often that channel picks up a rate change.
Your system has MAYA's price

- **The channel sells a rate plan MAYA does not write.** A plan that follows your base rate moves by your system's own rules. A plan that does not follow it, such as a package, keeps its own price whatever MAYA sends.

**Cloudbeds:** Compare the room type's base rate in Cloudbeds with the night's Current price in MAYA. Cloudbeds applies a send a few seconds after it goes out, so the two should match within a minute of it.

**ThinkReservations:** Compare the rate on the rate type MAYA writes to (Best Available, as above) with the night's Current price in MAYA. ThinkReservations applies a send shortly after accepting it, so allow a little longer than you would for Cloudbeds.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so MAYA never changes what a channel shows. Your channels show your Mews rates, as they always have.
The channel sells a rate plan MAYA does not write

Before every send MAYA checks each room type and night once more, against the room type as it is now. A night that fails a check is held back and recorded, and never sent. The checks:

| Held back when | Why |
|---|---|
| The night is outside the window | Only nights the cycle priced go out. |
| The room type is switched off in MAYA | A duplicate room type hidden at import, or one you confirmed as a duplicate on the review screen. A room type your system has removed is not switched off. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations it is reported in the change log instead (see the next section). |
| The price is 0 | A comp night. No property system is confirmed to take a 0 from MAYA, so you set 0 in your system yourself. You are told in the change log. |
| Your system has the night at 0 and nobody typed a price | The night is closed there, or its rates are not loaded that far out. MAYA leaves it alone. |
| The price is under the floor or over the ceiling as they are now | A limit you changed after the night was priced. The next cycle re-prices and the hold clears. A typed price widens the limits to include itself. |
| No pricing run has backed the price within the last 30 minutes | If runs have been failing for half an hour, MAYA stops sending until one succeeds, rather than send an old number. |
| The room type has no base rate in your system | Nothing to send to. You are told in the change log. |

Only two of these are shown to you: the price of 0 and the missing base rate, because those need you. The rest are MAYA's own checks, and most clear on a later cycle without you. A room type switched off as a duplicate is never meant to be sent, and a night your system has at 0 waits until you load a rate there.

**Good to know: A price of 0 is never sent** · Type 0 for a night and the confirmation reads "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." The change log then carries the same reminder until your system has the night at 0. No rule raises a night set to 0.

**Counts as a room** on the PMS tab changes what MAYA divides by for occupancy and what you are billed for, not what is sent. A room type you untick there is still priced and sent whenever it has a starting price, such as your rate in your system, a booking or a price you typed. To keep MAYA off a room type, leave it out of every rule's **Apply to room types**: it is then sent at your own rate, kept between its floor and ceiling. If your rate is outside them, the floor or ceiling is sent instead. There is no switch that takes a room type out of sending, with one exception.

The exception is a duplicate. A room type the review screen hides as a duplicate is switched off in MAYA, and nothing is sent for it. MAYA hides one at import, or you confirm one there later.

A room type your system has removed is not switched off in MAYA. On Cloudbeds its prices cannot land. Once you are live, the change log reports its nights as "Cloudbeds can't find the rate MAYA changes for" that room type. On ThinkReservations its prices cannot land either, and once MAYA's hourly read finds it gone, the change log reports it as "MAYA can't find a base rate for" that room type. [Room types and rooms out of service](@51) says how to have it switched off.

The first time MAYA sends to a night, it writes over the rate you had there. So MAYA makes sure the price it sends was built on a rate it has read recently. A night MAYA has never sent to is held until the cycle's read of your rates has succeeded, or a read within the last hour did. That is why the first send after going live, and the first send to each new night entering the window, can take one cycle longer than you expect.

Before a new price goes to a night last sent to over an hour ago, MAYA reads your rate there once more if its hourly read did not run this cycle. A night whose rate moved waits for the next pricing run instead of being written over. [Rates you change in your property system](@50) has every condition.

Nothing is priced or sent on that cycle. MAYA tries again, waiting longer after each failed read: about ten minutes, then twenty, then forty, up to an hour between tries. The first read that works puts the property back on the normal cycle, prices it and sends what changed.

While reads are failing, the rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. MAYA never sends a rate to undo an earlier one.

If only the hourly read of your rates fails, rules still run and changed prices still go out. Only nights MAYA has never sent to wait for the next successful read.

On a large property the daily re-read of your bookings can take more than one cycle too. Until it finishes, rules still run but nothing is sent. Sending resumes on the cycle it completes.

When your system is busy it can ask MAYA to slow down, and MAYA waits and tries again. A busy hour at your system can make a large send take a few minutes longer. You do not need to do anything. If it lasts, the change log says so, for example "Cloudbeds asked MAYA to slow down, so Standard rates are taking longer than usual to update". [When your property system does not accept a price](@56) explains that message.

To check a night, compare its Current price in MAYA with the rate in your system. On Cloudbeds they should match within a minute of a send. On ThinkReservations, allow a little longer. For "is it working right now?", start at [Start here: the four questions people ask first](@94).

**Not yet** · MAYA cannot show you what it sent next to what your system has, and there is no per-night "landed" mark. Compare the night in both places, or read the change log for problems.

**Inside my system, how can I tell which rate changes MAYA made and which a colleague made?** MAYA writes through the connection your property approved. On Cloudbeds that is the MAYA app connected from the Marketplace, and on ThinkReservations the ThinkReservations login used to connect it. It sends only the rate for each night, with no note or tag. How your system's own rate history or audit log labels those changes (by the app's name, or by the person who connected it) is up to your system, so look there for which name appears beside them. MAYA's change log is the record of what MAYA set: each change with its night, room type, price and reason. A rate that matches the change log's latest price for that night came from MAYA. On Mews, MAYA writes nothing, so every rate change there is someone else's.

**Does MAYA pick up new bookings instantly?** No. A booking made in your system is read on the next cycle, within about five minutes. The rules run on that cycle, and any price that changes is sent on the same cycle.
Does MAYA pick up new bookings instantly?
**Why did MAYA send a night again at the same price?** The rate plan behind that room type changed in your system, so MAYA sent the night to the new plan.
Why did MAYA send a night again at the same price?

**What does "Last sync" mean?** The time of the last successful read of your bookings. It says nothing about sending. [The PMS tab: connection health](@52) explains the rest of that tab.

**Example: One cycle at the Harbour Inn**

Tuesday, 3:05 PM cycle (your browser's clock). MAYA reads the Harbour Inn's bookings and finds one new booking for Friday, November 13, 2026. That night is now 17 of 20 rooms, 85% full. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) fires on every room type: Standard's $150 becomes $165, Deluxe's $200 becomes $220 and Suite's $300 becomes $330.

The send has three changes, all for November 13: Standard $165, Deluxe $220, Suite $330. Each goes to its room type's base rate in Cloudbeds. MAYA asks Cloudbeds what became of the send a few seconds later and records the prices as landed. The other 59 nights are unchanged and are not sent.
What does "Last sync" mean?

If a price does not land for a reason that usually clears on its own, MAYA sends it again every cycle, up to 10 times at one price, then once a day. If the reason needs you, such as a rate rule, the night is held and tried again after a day, when its price changes, or (for a connection or permission problem) after a reconnect. A missing base rate is different: MAYA looks for one again every cycle, so the night usually goes out on the cycle after you add it. You are told in the change log, in an item headed "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds", straight away for a cause that needs you, otherwise after 2 hours and 5 tries. Each item names the cause and, when there is something for you to do, says what.

Sending problems live in one place: the **Change Log** tab. There is no email and no badge for them, and no banner except the connection banner when Cloudbeds stops accepting MAYA's connection. While a problem is ongoing its item sits at the top of the log, above every pricing run, with an amber border. Once it is over it drops into the timeline at the point it ended, and only while the log still shows runs from that time.

Only a live property has these items. In simulation nothing is sent, so nothing can fail to land. Anyone on the team who can open the change log can read them.

An item has four parts, and a fifth you can open.

1. **The header**: "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds", then the date it opened and, in brackets, how long ago. The name is your system's: "Rates not reaching Think Reservations" for ThinkReservations.
The header
2. **The cause**, one sentence, for example "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate."
The cause
3. **The size and the state**: "6 nights, 2 room types · Still happening", or "· Resolved <when>" once the prices landed, or "· Ended <when>" when something else closed it.
The size and the state
4. **What to do**, one line, shown only while the problem is ongoing and only for causes where there is something for you to do: "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."
What to do

5. **Show 12 tries** opens the list of tries behind it, oldest first, one line per group that went the same way: "12 tries, Sep 17, 10:05 AM to 10:50 AM, 6 nights: Cloudbeds refused them". Hover a line to read your system's own words. When every line is a check MAYA made without reaching your system, the button reads **Show 12 checks**. A footer such as "3 other tries not shown" means more tries were counted than listed.

The words at the end of a try line say how it went: "Cloudbeds refused them", "Cloudbeds accepted them, then rejected them", "Cloudbeds never confirmed them", "Nothing to send to in Cloudbeds", "Couldn't read the rates in Cloudbeds", "MAYA held them back", or "Went through".

Room types are named in the cause: "Deluxe rates", "Deluxe and Suite rates", or "rates for 3 room types". When MAYA could not name them it says "some rates" or "some room types".
Show 12 tries

The sentences below are exactly what the change log says, with Cloudbeds and the Deluxe room type as the example. For ThinkReservations the name changes and nothing else.

| The item says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudbeds stopped accepting MAYA's connection, so Deluxe rates can't be changed. | Your system no longer accepts MAYA's connection, so nothing can be written. The connection banner appears at the same time. | "Reconnect Cloudbeds on the PMS tab." A General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. Held prices go out on the next cycle after. |
| Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates. | Your system lets MAYA read but refuses the write. Someone changed MAYA's permissions there. | "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Cloudbeds, then reconnect on the PMS tab." |

**Good to know: How a refusal gets its cause** · When your system refuses a price, MAYA matches its words against a fixed list of phrases and answer codes. A message on the list gets its cause. Anything else is filed as "couldn't tell why". Your system's own words are behind the hover on the try line, so you can check the match yourself.

There is no screen for changing one room type's floor or ceiling in MAYA. So when your system's minimum sits above MAYA's floor (or its maximum below MAYA's ceiling), you have three ways to line them up. They differ in what else they change.

1. **Change your system to match MAYA.** Lower the minimum, or raise the maximum, for that room type in your system. Only that room type is touched. MAYA's floor and ceiling for each room type are in the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab.
Change your system to match MAYA

2. **Answer the floor question again.** Your answer becomes the floor of every room type at once, not only this one. Use it when one floor suits them all. A new ceiling answer goes only to room types that have never sold above it. [Set or change a floor or ceiling](@80) has the steps and the catches.
Answer the floor question again

3. **Email us for one room type.** [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) with the room type and the numbers.

The night that was refused waits. MAYA is not told about a change you make in your system, so the night goes again within a day, or sooner if its price changes. To send it now, type a price on it that sits inside both your system's limits and MAYA's.
Email us for one room type

MAYA counts days on your property's own calendar, using the time zone it read from your system when you connected. If the time zone in your system has since changed, or was wrong then, the two can disagree about when tonight ends. If midnight comes first in your system's time zone, your system counts tonight as over until midnight comes in MAYA's. It refuses any new price MAYA sends for tonight in those hours.

Don't wait for the change log to tell you, because it will usually not show this cause at all. A refused night is held rather than sent every cycle, and at midnight in MAYA's time zone it leaves the 60-night window. An item appears only once one night has had at least 5 tries over 2 hours or more. A held night rarely gets there before midnight.

Look at your rates instead. The sign is a new price for tonight, set in those hours, that shows as the **Current price** in MAYA but never reaches your system. Prices for later nights go through as normal. If you see it, check the property's time zone in your system first. To change the time zone MAYA uses, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone). [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@105) explains how MAYA counts days.

**Example: Eastern in Cloudbeds, Pacific in MAYA** · Say Cloudbeds is set to US Eastern and MAYA has US Pacific. From 9:00 PM to midnight Pacific time, Cloudbeds already counts tonight as over and refuses any new price for tonight. Later nights go through as normal.

- A price that fails for a cause that clears on its own (slowing down, not responding, never confirmed, cause unrecognised) is sent again every cycle, up to 10 tries at that price, then once a day.
- A price that fails for a cause that needs a person (connection, permission, a rate rule, a night already begun) is held. It is not sent again until the price changes, the rate plan behind it changes, a day has passed, or, for a connection or permission problem, the connection has been reconnected. MAYA is not told about a change you make in your system. So after you do what the item asks there, the held night goes again within a day, or sooner if its price or rate plan changes. You do not have to touch the price, but a price you type goes out now.

- A price of 0 is never sent. MAYA checks each cycle whether your system now has the night at 0, and closes the item when it does.
- A night is never given up on for good. Every held or exhausted night gets one more try each day, so a fix nobody told MAYA about, such as a rate rule loosened in your system, is picked up within a day.

- **At once** for a cause that needs you: a connection or permission problem, a derived-only rate, a missing base rate, a rate rule, a price of 0. And for a rate MAYA cannot find, once its second try has failed.
At once

- **After 2 hours and at least 5 tries** for the causes that usually clear on their own. A price that lands on a retry before then is never mentioned. That is deliberate: an item you cannot act on is noise.
After 2 hours and at least 5 tries

- **Usually not at all** for a night that had already begun. Such a night leaves the window at midnight, nearly always before it reaches 5 tries. [The time zone case](#the-time-zone-case) says what to look for instead.

An item that closed within the last hour and then fails again is reopened rather than duplicated.
Usually not at all

An item is over when no night is still failing for that cause. The second line then says how it ended:

- **Resolved** when your system took the prices (for ThinkReservations, when it accepted them).
Resolved

- **Ended** when something else closed it: a new price replaced the failing one, the night left the 60-night window, the night is no longer priced, or the property stopped sending (it went back to simulation, or its subscription lapsed).

A resolved or ended item is not deleted. It sits in the timeline at the point it ended, for as long as the log shows runs from that time.
Ended

The cause sentence names which system did what: "Cloudbeds refused", "Cloudbeds isn't responding", "MAYA doesn't send". The hover shows your system's own words. As a rule:

- A refusal that names a setting (a rate rule, a permission, a plan that follows another) is settled in your system. For Cloudbeds, Cloudbeds Support can see those settings; we cannot.
- Slowing down, not responding and never confirmed are your system being busy or down. Wait.
- "MAYA couldn't tell why" and anything you cannot place: email us with the sentence, the hover text and your property name.

[Contact support](@110) has our address and the link to Cloudbeds Support.

Only when the item has an action line. An item with no action line is MAYA keeping you informed while it retries. If the action line asks you to add a base rate, the nights usually go out on the next cycle after you do. If it asks for another change in your system, such as a rate limit, make the change, and the held nights go again within a day, or sooner if their price changes. If it asks for a reconnect, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects on the PMS tab, and the held prices go out on the cycle after. [Reconnect your property system](@91) has the clicks.

**Cloudbeds:** Everything on this page applies as written. A refused write for a gone connection also marks the connection disconnected, so the reconnect banner appears at the same time.

**ThinkReservations:** The sentences read "Think Reservations" in place of "Cloudbeds". Three differences:

- A refused write never disconnects ThinkReservations. It is held as a permission problem and the connection stays up for reading. So the cause "stopped accepting MAYA's connection" is never filed for ThinkReservations; you see "won't let MAYA change ... because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates" instead.

- If ThinkReservations quietly drops an accepted batch, the night keeps showing MAYA's price in MAYA while ThinkReservations keeps the old rate, until the price next changes and is sent again. Compare a night in both places if you suspect this.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so a Mews property never has a "Rates not reaching" item.

Before every send MAYA checks each night against the room type as it is now: inside the window, room type still active, price above 0, inside the floor and ceiling, backed by a recent pricing run, and your system not holding the night at 0 with no typed price. A night held by one of those checks is recorded but not shown to you, except a price of 0, which needs you. Most of the others clear on a later cycle without you. A room type switched off as a duplicate is never meant to be sent, and a night your system has at 0 waits until you load a rate there. [How prices reach your property system](@55) lists the checks.

Sam sets a minimum rate of $120 on Deluxe in Cloudbeds. MAYA's floor for Deluxe is $110, lower than that minimum. On Monday, "Last minute" (booking window Less than 3 and occupancy Less than 50, Decrease 15%) cuts Deluxe for a quiet Wednesday night from $140 to $119. That is above MAYA's floor, so it goes out, and Cloudbeds refuses it.

Because a rate rule is a cause that needs a person, the change log shows at once: "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds", then "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate." and "1 night, 1 room type · Still happening", with "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."

To pause, turn your rules off: the prices they set stay where they are. To undo what a rule did, delete it. To hold a price on some nights, type it. To put the whole property back into simulation, email us; only we can switch it. Turning rules off, typing a price or going back to simulation never puts back a rate MAYA has replaced. Deleting a rule is the one route that does: its changes come off and the new prices are sent.

| You want to | Do this | Prices already in your system |
|---|---|---|
| Stop every rule acting from now on | Turn each rule **Off** on the **Rules** tab | Stay as they are |
| Undo everything one rule did | **Delete** the rule | Go back to what they would be without it, and are sent |
| Stop one rule on certain nights | Answer **Stop for this night** on the amber banner | Stay as they are, unless enough of the bookings behind a raise cancel |
| Hold a price on a night or a stretch | Type the price on the **Calendar** tab, with **through…** for a range | Become the price you typed |
| Stop sending altogether, keep everything else | Email us to go back to simulation | Stay as they are |

Every rule on the **Rules** tab has an **On** / **Off** switch. Click it and the rule is off from the next pricing run. There is no confirmation.

Off freezes. The rule stops acting, and every change it has already made stays on the price: a raise stays raised, a cut stays cut. Those prices are already in your system and MAYA does not send them again or send anything to undo them. Turn the rule **On** again and it resumes from the next run, starting from the prices as they are.

To pause everything, turn every rule off. Nothing else happens: MAYA keeps reading your bookings and your rates, and sends a price only when one changes. With every rule off, a price changes when you type or clear one, or when a floor or ceiling you change moves it. And each morning one new night enters the window. It goes out at your own rate, kept between your floor and ceiling. [Pause everything for a while](@70) is the short version.

**Careful: Off does not undo** · Turning a rule off keeps every price it set. If a rule has set prices you do not want, delete it, or type the prices you want. Off alone leaves them in place.

The red **Delete** button on a rule opens a dialog headed "Delete "Busy nights"?". It says: "Deleting this rule also undoes the price changes it has already made. Any night it adjusted goes back to what the price would be if this rule had never run." It then offers the other choice, turning the rule off instead, with the prices it set staying exactly as they are. And it warns: "Deleting cannot be undone."

Three buttons: **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**, **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes** (which does the same as the switch and closes the dialog), and **Cancel**.

Once a booking speed or pickup rule has adjusted the same night three times, the amber Rules that keep adjusting banner asks you what to do. **Stop for this night** stops that rule on that night. What it already cut stays. A raise it already made stays, unless enough of the bookings behind it cancel. Your other rules keep working there. The rule then shows a "Stopped on 3 nights" chip on the **Rules** tab, and **Let it run again** puts it back. [Rules that keep adjusting](@42) explains the banner. There is no way to stop a rule on one night before the banner asks, other than turning the rule off everywhere. A typed price takes off what the rule already did on that night, but the rule can fire on it again.

Click a night on the **Calendar** tab, type a price for a room type, click **through…** to pick the last night if you want a range, and click **Save**. On a live property, nights inside the 60-night window go to your system as typed, now. Nights further ahead are sent as they enter the window. In simulation nothing is sent. Rules that had already moved those nights pause for that room type. Rules that fire later still apply on top of your price, so a typed price is a starting point, not a lock. A range can run from tonight up to 364 days ahead (365 nights at most).

**Clear** takes your price off the night, and your rules set its price again. [Setting a price yourself](@49) has every detail, and [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@67) is the short version.

There is no switch in MAYA to put a property back into simulation. Going live is one-way in the app. To go back, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Back%20to%20simulation) from your MAYA sign-in address with your property name. We switch it for you.

What happens once we do:
- **Sending stops on the next cycle.** Everything else carries on: bookings are read, rules run, the change log fills, the calendar shows what MAYA would send.
Sending stops on the next cycle

- **The prices already in your system stay.** MAYA never sends a rate to undo an earlier one. If you want different rates, set them in your system, or wait until you are live again and type them in MAYA.
The prices already in your system stay

- **On a night MAYA never sent to, a rate you change in your system becomes the base.** For example, a night that entered the window after we switched you back. MAYA reads your rate again within the hour (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) and uses it as the night's starting price. It is not kept as a manual price.
On a night MAYA never sent to, a rate you change in your system becomes the base

- **On a night MAYA sent to while you were live, a rate you change in your system waits.** While you simulate, your rules keep working from the base that night already had. When you go live again, MAYA reads your rate as that night's base (next point).
On a night MAYA sent to while you were live, a rate you change in your system waits

- **When you go live again**, from the button on the review screen if it is still there (otherwise email us and we switch you live again), MAYA reads your rates once more before its first send, and your rules work on top of them. A night whose rate you changed while simulating starts from that rate. A rate you changed in your system on a night MAYA had sent to, and that MAYA had already kept as a manual price ("Changed in Cloudbeds"), stays a manual price.
When you go live again

- **Your rules, limits, history, manual prices and team are untouched.**

[Simulation mode](@53) describes the state you go back to.
Your rules, limits, history, manual prices and team are untouched

Cancelling your subscription is a different thing from pausing. It is done in the billing portal or by email, takes effect at the end of the paid period, and MAYA keeps working until then. After that, reading, pricing and sending stop, and the rates in your system stay as they are. Your rules and history stay too, and **Restart your subscription** brings MAYA back. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@61) has the steps.

MAYA does not read future closures from your system, and there is no screen to enter one. Nights you are closed are priced and sent like any others while they are inside the 60-night window. Three ways to handle a closed stretch, from simplest:

1. **Close the nights in your system.** Set the rate to 0 there (or close the night the way your system does, if that reports as a rate of 0). On a night MAYA has already sent to, MAYA reads the 0 on its next hourly read, your rules stop running on that night, and any manual price there is cleared. On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate of 0 means the night is not priced at all. Either way nothing more is sent for it. When you reopen and load a rate, MAYA reads it as the night's base and your rules work on top of it. This works for Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations. Nothing is sent to Mews in any case.
Close the nights in your system
2. **Turn your rules off** for the closed stretch and back on afterwards. Simple to do, but it pauses every night, open or closed.
Turn your rules off

3. **Type a price** for the closed nights as a range. A typed price is sent as typed, so this only helps if a placeholder rate is what you want in your system.

A closure in the past is a separate matter: it should not skew comparisons. MAYA finds long stretches of zero occupancy in your history and asks on the review, "Were you closed ...?". Confirming keeps those nights out of comparisons. [Checking what MAYA found](@26) explains that card.
Type a price

Click **Billing** at the top right of the dashboard. General Managers and Hotel Admins see it. Everyone else sees a line saying who to ask. The top card says where you stand in one sentence. **Your plan** lists status, price and next charge. **Update card, receipts & cancellation** opens Stripe's billing portal, where your card, invoices and cancellation live. Your room count is changed on this page, never in Stripe.

**Billing** is a button at the top right of the dashboard, beside **Team** and **Sign Out**. The page is headed "Billing" with three links: **Help**, **Your team** and **← Back to MAYA**.

Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can see the plan and act on it. A Revenue Manager or Viewer who opens the page sees one line instead: "Billing is handled by this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. Ask one of them for access if you need to change it." Everyone on the property, Viewers included, still sees the dashboard banner when something needs attention, so nobody is left wondering why prices stopped. [Roles: who can do what](@63) has the full table.

One sentence at the top of the page says where you stand. MAYA shows the sentence that matters most, in this order, and colours the card to match: plain, amber for a warning, red when work has stopped.

| Title | Colour | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|---|
| "MAYA has paused work on this property" | red | Prices are no longer worked out or sent. If the status is "Unpaid", the card says to update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off. For any other status it says the subscription was cancelled and starting again means a new one, and a green **Restart your subscription** button sits under it. If the status is "Paused", email us before you restart ([Your plan](#your-plan) explains). |
| "Your last payment did not go through" | amber | The bank is retrying the payment, and your rules keep running while it does. Update your card to avoid an interruption. |
| "Your saved card stopped working" | amber | A card check failed. "Nothing has failed yet, but the next charge will. Update it before your renewal to keep pricing running." |
| "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 24" | amber | Your system shows more rooms than you pay for. The card says how many are not paid for and how many days you have to set the count yourself. [Your room count and what you pay](@59) explains. |
| "This subscription is set to cancel" | amber | "MAYA keeps working until" the date "then stops." |
| "Your trial ends in 5 days" (or "today") | plain | "Your first charge of $110 lands on" the date. Days are whole days, rounded down. |
| "Your subscription is active" | plain | "Next charge of $110 on" the date. |

The amount in the last two rows is Stripe's own total for your whole next invoice. It includes any code. After a room count change it also includes the part-period difference: more after a raise, less (down to nothing) after a credit from lowering the count. So for one invoice it can differ from your usual price. If Stripe cannot be reached within a moment, the bracket price for your room count shows instead, which can be higher or lower than the invoice. That is also why the number can differ from the calculator on get-maya.com.

Four rows at most.

- **Status.** One of "On trial", "Active", "Payment overdue", "Unpaid" (the row goes on to say stopped), "Cancelled", "Never completed" (a checkout that was never finished) or "Paused" (explained under this list).
Status

- **Price**, or **Was** whenever work has stopped (the status reads "Unpaid", "Cancelled", "Never completed" or "Paused"). Under **Price** it is the same number as the top card, Stripe's total for your next invoice, followed by "per month" or "per year". After a room count change that total includes the part-period difference, so it may not be your monthly (or yearly) price. The hint reads, for example, "20 rooms at MAYA's monthly rate." and adds "with your code applied" whenever that total differs from the bracket price, whether or not you used a code. Under **Was** the row shows the bracket price for your room count.
Price
- **Trial ends.** The date, only during a trial.
Trial ends

- **Next charge**, or one of its three other names: **Access ends** (set to cancel: MAYA works until this date, then stops), **Retrying payment until** (a payment failed and the bank is retrying) or **Ended** (work has stopped: "Unpaid", "Cancelled", "Never completed" or "Paused"). Under every name the date is the end of the current billing period. So while a payment is being retried, the date is not when the retries stop: they usually stop well before it, after about two weeks. An "Unpaid" subscription reads **Ended** too, but it is not over. Update your card in the portal and it restarts where it left off. Its **Ended** date can even be one still to come.
Next charge

**What "Paused" means.** The subscription is on hold in Stripe. No invoices are made, and work on the property stops, as it does for "Unpaid". You cannot pause a subscription from MAYA or from the billing portal, so this status is rare. If you see it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Paused%20subscription) and we sort it out with you. The top card will say the subscription was cancelled and offer **Restart your subscription**, but a paused subscription still exists in Stripe. Email us before you restart, or you may end up with two subscriptions.
What "Paused" means

This amber section appears only after a card check has failed: "We checked it on" the date "and your bank declined it", with the bank's short reason in brackets, then "Nothing has failed yet" and a note that updating the card now avoids an interruption. Nothing has been charged and nothing has stopped. [Cards, payments and invoices](@60) explains the check and how the warning clears.

The button **Update card, receipts & cancellation** (it reads "Opening…" while the link is made) opens Stripe's billing portal, and the line under it says why: "Opens Stripe, where your card, invoices and cancellation all live." When you are done, Stripe returns you to this page.

What you can do there:

- See and download every invoice and receipt.
- Change the billing email address, the billing address and a business tax ID.
- Update the card.
- Cancel, giving a reason (MAYA keeps the reason category, never any comment you type).
- Switch between monthly and yearly. A switch starts a new billing period that day and is charged at once, less a credit for the unused part of the old period. [Switching between monthly and yearly](@60#switching-between-monthly-and-yearly) has the details, including what happens during a free trial.

The code you used at checkout does not show on this page today. If you need to check which one was applied, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Which%20code).

If the portal does not open: "Could not open the billing portal." or "Could not reach the billing portal." Try again in a moment. "Billing for a shared group is still being set up. Ask the account owner, or try again later." appears when you manage one property of a group whose billing account you do not own. The owner can act from their own **Billing** page.

**Careful: The billing email is separate from your login** · Receipts and Stripe's own emails go to the email address on the billing account, which you change in the portal. Changing it does not change the address you sign in with, and changing your login is not possible in the app yet.

This section appears while the subscription is running: "Your plan covers 20 rooms. We check this against your property management system.", then what MAYA measured, then a **Rooms billed** box and a **Change** button with a quote of the new price before you save. [Your room count and what you pay](@59) walks through every line.

Shown only when you have set a property aside with **Not now** during a Cloudbeds Marketplace group setup: each one with "Set aside" and the date, and a **Set up** button that reopens the payment screen for it. [Paying for a group of properties](@10) covers groups.

When the subscription has been cancelled, was never completed or is "Paused", a green **Restart your subscription** button under the top card opens a screen of the same name, with your room count and period pre-filled. For "Paused", email us first, as [Your plan](#your-plan) explains. An "Unpaid" subscription has no restart button, because it is still alive in Stripe and comes back when you update the card in the portal. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@61) has the steps.

While everything is fine there is no banner. When something needs attention, a strip appears above the dashboard with the same title and sentence as the top card, and one button: **Fix it** on an amber warning, **Restart MAYA** on a red stop. Both open the **Billing** page. Everyone on the property sees the banner, Viewers included. Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can act on it.

A property that has paid but has not connected its system yet cannot be shown on the **Billing** page. The payment or connect screen shows **Manage billing or cancel** instead (with the property's name in a group). It opens Stripe straight onto cancelling that one subscription and brings you back. Once set to cancel it reads "Cancels at the end of the period". Three messages:
- **"There is no subscription waiting on setup to manage."** Nothing is waiting. Open the **Billing** page instead.
"There is no subscription waiting on setup to manage."
- **"This property's billing has changed. Reload the page."** Reload, then try again.
"This property's billing has changed. Reload the page."
- **"This subscription is already set to cancel at the end of the period."** Nothing more to do.
"This subscription is already set to cancel at the end of the period."

Each property has its own **Billing** page showing its own subscription. A group from the Cloudbeds Marketplace bills on the owner's one account in Stripe. A General Manager or Hotel Admin of one property who does not also manage every other property on that account does not get the full portal. For them, **Update card, receipts & cancellation** opens only Stripe's screen for changing that property's plan: no card, no invoices, no cancelling. For those, ask the owner, who opens the full portal from their own **Billing** page, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20billing). [Paying for a group of properties](@10) explains why.

**Not yet** · No invoices, receipts or billing history inside the app. They live in the Stripe portal. No pause. No way to see a property's billing until its system is connected. The code you used at checkout is not shown. The page shows US dollars whatever your property's currency.

MAYA charges per room and counts your rooms from your property system on every sync, leaving out room types you have unticked as rooms. Up to 500 rooms, if it finds more rooms than you pay for, you get a banner, an email and 7 days to set the count yourself before MAYA raises it and adjusts your next invoice. It never lowers the count for you: if you run fewer rooms, lower it on the **Billing** page and your next invoice drops. On ThinkReservations every room type counts as 100 rooms until we set your property's number, so [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) as soon as you connect.

About every five minutes, when MAYA reads your bookings, it also adds up the rooms in your active room types. Two kinds of type are left out:

- **Types you have unticked as rooms.** On the **PMS** tab, each room type has a **Counts as a room** box. Untick it for anything nobody sleeps in, such as a meeting room, a spa slot or a court. An unticked type is left out of the count whatever its name. A ticked one is counted whatever its name. Your answer is final in both directions.
Types you have unticked as rooms

- **Types you have not answered for, whose name reads like something nobody sleeps in.** Until you tick or untick a type, MAYA reads its name, as set out below. This is only a reading of the name, and one tick from you overrides it.

Some words leave a type out whatever else its name says, such as meeting, conference, boardroom, banquet, parking, massage, treatment, storage and day use. Others leave a type out only when its name has no bedroom word in it (room, suite, king, queen, villa or cabin, for example). Spa, pool, cabana, court, event, hall, package and fee are words of this second kind. So "Spa Suite" is counted, while "Meeting Room", "Garden Cabana" and "Pool House" are left out.

If the **Billing** page lists a type as not counted and guests do sleep there, tick it on the **PMS** tab. If its box already shows ticked, untick it and tick it again: your tick then counts.
Types you have not answered for, whose name reads like something nobody sleeps in

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds reports how many rooms each room type has, so the count MAYA measures is the count Cloudbeds holds.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations does not report how many rooms each room type has. So MAYA gives every room type the same number of rooms, from one rooms-per-type number for the whole property, and uses it for occupancy and for this count alike. Until we set that number for your property, it is 100: each room type ticked as a room counts as 100 rooms. We can change that one number, not set a separate count for each type, and there is no field in MAYA for you to set it yourself.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) as soon as you connect, so we can sort out your billed count with you by hand before the 7 days run out. If nobody steps in, MAYA raises your billed count to the measured number 7 days after the email: for The Harbour Inn, to 300 rooms at $750 a month.
