**1. The bank retries and MAYA keeps working**

Stripe retries the card over a period (about two weeks). During the retries the status on the **Billing** page reads "Payment overdue" and the date row is renamed **Retrying payment until**. The top card reads "Your last payment did not go through", and says your rules keep running while the bank retries and that updating your card now avoids an interruption. The date on it is the end of the current billing period, not the last retry: the retries usually stop well before it (about two weeks). The dashboard shows the amber **Fix it** banner. Your rules keep running as normal, and a live Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations property keeps sending prices. Nothing is sent to Mews yet, or while a property is in simulation, whether or not a payment has failed.

**2. If the retries run out, work stops**

The status becomes "Unpaid" (the row goes on to say stopped). The top card turns red: "MAYA has paused work on this property" with "Prices are no longer being calculated or sent to your PMS. Update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off." The dashboard shows the red **Restart MAYA** banner. There is no **Restart your subscription** button in this state, because the subscription is still alive in Stripe. Update the card in the portal, and read [Moving to another card](#moving-to-another-card) to be sure the subscription is charged on it. Once the payment goes through, work picks up again.

One difference: managing Hotel Admins. A General Manager can hand out any role up to General Manager, change or remove anyone up to that level (other General Managers included), and cannot touch a Hotel Admin. A Hotel Admin can do all of that and also make, demote or remove other Hotel Admins. Both can go live, reconnect, see billing and manage the team. Two rank rules hold for everyone: you can give a role at your own level or below, never above ("You can't give someone a role above your own."), and you cannot change or remove someone above you ("That's above your own access level.").

Can a General Manager remove another General Manager? Yes. A General Manager can change another General Manager's role or remove them, as they can for anyone up to their own level, even though the role's one-line description in the app says otherwise.

Open the **Change Log** tab. Each pricing run lists the nights whose price moved, one bold line per room type and night, followed by a sentence that names the rule and the reason. **1. Go to the Change Log tab**

It opens on changes only. Each entry is headed **Pricing run** with the time of the run in your browser's local time, such as "Sat, Nov 14, 2026, 3:05 PM PST", and how long ago it was, such as "(12 min ago)". Inside a run, each change starts with a bold line in the shape "Standard · stay 2026-11-14: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%)". Look for the stay date. Down moves read "down to" with a minus percentage.

**3. Read the sentence under it**

The first sentence names the rule and the move: "Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. The next sentence gives the reason in your own numbers: It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.

When a booking speed rule acted, a **How did we know?** link sits under the entry. It shows how many bookings the night received, how many a night like it usually has by that point, and the level that reads as. **Why did you expect that?** lists which past nights were compared and why, and **Show me the nights you compared** lists them one by one.

A rule cannot be edited, so to change its name, condition, amount or room types, delete it and add it again. Deleting undoes every price change the rule made, so the new rule starts from clean prices. To keep the gap between the two short, build the new rule in the **Rate Simulator** first: it arrives switched **Off**, ready to switch on the moment you delete the old one. The one change made in place is a **Tune** suggestion after **Get suggestions from my data**, which moves an occupancy rule's threshold. Nothing is undone when you accept, but from the next run nights that no longer meet the new threshold lose the change.

**1. Write down the settings you are keeping**

On the **Rules** tab the row shows the rule's **Conditions** (for example "Occupancy above 80%"), its **Room Types** and its **Price Change**. A booking speed rule's row also shows the window and the wait, such as "booking speed at least Faster Than Normal (past week), then waits 3 days".

**2. Delete the old rule**

Click **Delete** at the end of the row, then **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes** in the dialog. Every night the rule adjusted goes back to the price it would have without it, from the next run.

**3. Add the new rule**

Click **+ Add a rule**, enter the new settings and click **Add Rule**. The new rule is **On** at once. To look before it acts, build it in the **Rate Simulator** tab instead: a rule saved from there arrives on the Rules tab switched **Off**.

Rules need Revenue Manager access or higher.

**Safer: build the new rule first.** In the **Rate Simulator** tab, build the new rule and click **Save This Rule**. It arrives on the **Rules** tab switched **Off**. Then delete the old rule and switch the new one **On** straight away. The simulator's form has no **Measured over**, **Then waits (advanced)** or **Change prices on different room types** controls, so a booking speed rule built there measures the past week and waits 1 week. For any other settings, use the steps above.

**Careful** · Whichever way you do it, add or switch on the new rule straight after deleting the old one: the next cycle then drops the old rule's changes and applies the new rule together. If a cycle runs in between, the nights the old rule was holding lose its change until the new rule's first cycle. On a live Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations property, that in-between price is sent to your system.

The new rule is a new rule. Its **Fired** count starts at a dash. Any nights you had answered **Stop for this night** for the old rule are no longer stopped, because those answers belonged to the old rule. A booking speed rule made after a typed price is not held by that price's wait. Its old entries stay in the change log under the name "Pricing rule".

When you click **Get suggestions from my data** on the Rules tab, MAYA reads your history again and may offer a card headed "Tune "Busy nights"?" that proposes moving an occupancy threshold, for example from 80% to 95%. Click **Make that change** and the threshold changes in place. The rule keeps its name, its fire count and its place in the list. Only occupancy thresholds are offered this way, and only when yours is more than 10 percentage points away from what your own history supports.

Accepting does not undo anything by itself. But a Tune only ever moves a standard rule (one with only occupancy or booking window conditions). A standard rule holds its change only while a night meets its condition. So from the next run, any night that no longer meets the new threshold loses the change.

**Not yet** · There is no edit control, no rename, and no way to change a rule's room types, amount, window or wait in place. Deleting and adding again is the way, and the three-button dialog makes the choice between undoing and keeping the old changes explicit.

A rule cannot be limited to a season, so for a stretch of dates, type the new price for each room type on the **Calendar** tab with **through…**, or change your rates in your property system on nights MAYA has not sent a price to yet.

A season here is any stretch of dates you choose, such as your summer or the winter holidays.

| A season, at one price per room type | Type the price on the calendar with **through…** | One amount for every night in the run. You work out the new price. |
| A season, keeping each night's own rate | Change the rates in your property system | Only on nights MAYA has never sent to: every night before you first go live, then nights more than 59 nights ahead. Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only. |

The change comes in on the next pricing run, about every five minutes.

Change rates in your property system only on nights MAYA has never sent a price to. Before you first go live, that is every night. Once you are live, it is every night more than 59 nights ahead.

MAYA reads your rate for each night in the window about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes. On a night it has never sent to, your rate is the starting point, so a night you raised 10% starts 10% higher and your rules work on top. Each night keeps its own rate, so weekends stay above weekdays.

On a night MAYA has already sent to, a change in your system is kept as your own price once MAYA's last send there has landed and is an hour old ("Changed in Cloudbeds" on the calendar). That works for part of the window, not for nearly all of it. [Rates you change in your property system](@50) has every condition.

**Careful: Changing the whole window in your system once you are live** · If you are live and change 80% or more of the nights MAYA has sent to (10 at least) by one percentage in your system, MAYA reads it as your system's own arithmetic, like prices shown with tax, and keeps none of it. Your new rates stay in your system only until MAYA's price for each night next changes. For the whole window, use the rule above.

**Cloudbeds:** Change each room type's base rate, the rate plan that does not follow another plan. MAYA reads and writes that rate. A change to a derived plan or a package is not read.

**ThinkReservations:** Change the Best Available rate type. MAYA reads and writes that rate. A change to another rate type is not read.

The rule works on top of whatever starting point a night has, a rate you raised in your system included. With a price you typed (or one MAYA kept from your system as yours), it depends on timing:

- If the rule was already acting on the night when you typed, your price stands and the rule stays off that night until you click **Clear**.
- A price typed for a night more than 59 nights ahead gets the rule's change on top once the night comes into the window.
- A rule added after you typed a price applies on top of that price.

**Example: The Harbour Inn, all nights up 10% and the winter holidays**

On Friday, October 2, 2026, Sam adds "All nights up 10%". On the next run every night from October 2 to November 30 moves: Standard from $150 to $165, Deluxe from $200 to $220, Suite from $300 to $330.

Sam wants the winter holidays higher still, Friday, December 18, 2026 through Sunday, January 3, 2027. Those nights are 77 to 93 nights away, so MAYA has never sent to them, and Sam raises each one's base rate 10% in Cloudbeds. On October 20, December 18 comes into the window. MAYA reads $165 as the Standard starting point, and the rule adds its 10%: $181.50, which is 21% above the old $150.

**Not yet** · A rule cannot be limited to a date range or a season, and a booking window counts days from today, so it cannot pick out fixed dates. The calendar takes an amount, not a percentage, and there is no bulk upload.

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**, leave **Metric** on **Sellable occupancy (%)**, set **Greater than** 85, choose **Increase the rate** by 10%, keep every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**. From the next run, any night in the next 60 with more than 85% of its sellable rooms booked is raised 10%. When the night drops back to 85% or under, the raise comes off.

**1. Open the builder**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Nearly full.

**2. Set the condition**

The first condition row is already **Sellable occupancy (%)**. Leave **Compare** on **Greater than** and change **Threshold** from 80 to 85.

**3. Set the change**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Increase the rate** in **Direction (required)**. **Adjust by percent (%)** is ticked with 10 already. For a fixed amount instead, untick it and tick **Adjust by fixed amount ($)**. Pick one or the other: when both are ticked only the percent is saved.

**4. Pick the room types and add it**

Under **Apply to room types** every room type that counts as a room is ticked. Leave them, and click **Add Rule**. The rule appears in the list switched **On**.

The row reads "Occupancy above 85%" under **Conditions** and "+10%" under **Price Change**. When a night crosses the mark, the change log shows a line such as "Standard · stay 2026-11-14: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%)" with the sentences "Nearly full" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. It was 90% full, past the 85% mark you set.

This is a standard rule: it switches on when the condition starts holding, holds one raise while it holds, and switches off when it stops. A cancellation that takes the night to 85% or under reverts the raise on the next run. It never stacks on itself.

**Example** · The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms that count. On Saturday, November 14, 2026, 18 are booked: 90%, so the rule fires and Standard goes from $150 to $165. A cancellation leaves 17 booked: 85% exactly, which is not more than 85, so the raise comes off and Standard returns to $150.

**Good to know** · Occupancy is measured over the rule's own room types, and only over rooms that count as rooms, with rooms out of service taken off first. A rule on Suite alone measures Suite: 2 rooms, so 2 booked is 100% and 1 booked is 50%. The threshold cannot be set above 100.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with **Metric** set to **Booking speed (recommended)**, **Speed** **Slower Than Normal**, **Measured over** **Past month**, **Then waits (advanced)** **1 week**, and **Decrease the rate** by 7%. A night whose bookings over the past month are slower than similar past nights had by the same point is cut 7%. After a week the rule counts only the bookings made since that cut, and cuts again if those are still slow. This rule is not a copy of the starter rule "Slow-date trim", which cuts only nights that read exactly Slower Than Normal.

**1. Open the builder and name it**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Slow nights.

**2. Choose booking speed**

In the condition row, change **Metric** to **Booking speed (recommended)**. The row changes to a **Speed** dropdown: pick **Slower Than Normal**.

**3. Set the window and the wait**

Under the row, set **Measured over** to **Past month** and **Then waits (advanced)** to **1 week**. The **?** beside each explains what it does in the app's own words.

**4. Set the cut, pick the room types, add it**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Decrease the rate** and type 7 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. Leave every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**.

How a wedding block counts depends on how it was booked. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, one reservation that holds several rooms counts as one booking. When guests book their own rooms from the block, each of their reservations counts as a booking. On Mews every room is its own reservation, so a group counts once per room. For occupancy, every booked room counts either way.

**Slower Than Normal** means that slow or slower: the rule fires on Slower Than Normal, Much Slower Than Normal and Stalled. With an expected count of 5, a night with 1 booking reads as Much Slower Than Normal and fires. With 5 or 6 it reads Normal and does not. When the difference is small, or there are fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, MAYA keeps the call close to Normal, so the rule fires less often rather than wrongly.

The cut stays on the price, and cancelled bookings never take it off. For 1 week the rule leaves that night alone for that room type. When the wait is over it counts only the bookings made since the night was last cut by a booking speed or pickup rule, this one or another. A cut from a standard rule, such as "Last minute", does not restart the count. It compares those bookings with the same days on the similar nights, and if they read slow on their own, it cuts another 7%, and the change log reads: Then "Slow nights" lowered it another 7%. Once it has cut the same night three times, the amber banner asks whether to keep adjusting or stop.

**Good to know** · The five starter rules include "Slow-date trim" (Slower Than Normal only, past month, cut 7%, waits 1 week) and "Slow-date rescue" (Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled, past month, cut 15%, waits 1 week). This rule is not a copy of either: it cuts 7% on all three slow levels. If both starter rules are on, you do not need this one: together they already cover every slow level. To keep a nearly full night from ever being cut, click **+ Add condition** and add **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 60: the rule then needs both to be true.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with **Metric** **Booking speed (recommended)**, **Speed** **Surging**, **Measured over** **Past day**, **Then waits (advanced)** **1 day**, and **Increase the rate** by 25%. A night that received far more bookings today than similar nights had on the same day of their run-up is raised 25%. The next day the rule counts only the bookings made since that raise, and raises again if those still read Surging. This is the starter rule "Sudden-spike catcher", so check your list first.

**1. Open the builder and name it**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Sudden rush.

**2. Choose Surging over the past day**

Change **Metric** to **Booking speed (recommended)** and pick **Surging** in **Speed**. Set **Measured over** to **Past day** and **Then waits (advanced)** to **1 day**.

**3. Set the raise, pick the room types, add it**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Increase the rate** and type 25 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. Leave every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**.

**Past day** counts the bookings dated today, on your property's own calendar, so a reading soon after midnight has almost nothing in it yet. MAYA compares that count with what similar past nights received on the same single day of their own run-up. Surging is the top of seven levels: the night needs at least 3.5 times the usual count, and at least 4 more bookings than usual, to read as Surging. With an expected count of 5, that is 18 bookings or more in one day. With fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, the call is capped at one step from Normal and Surging cannot be reached.

Picking **Surging** means the rule fires on Surging only. To fire on a broader rush, pick **Much Faster Than Normal** (at least twice the usual count) or **Faster Than Normal**, which fire on that level and everything above it.

The raise stays on the price, up to the room type's ceiling. For 1 day the rule leaves that night alone. Then it counts only the bookings made since the night was last raised by a booking speed or pickup rule (this one or another). If those alone read Surging, it raises another 25%.

A raise by an occupancy or booking window rule does not restart that count. One burst of bookings raises a night once, not once per rule. After three raises on the same night, the amber banner asks whether to keep adjusting or stop.

A raise comes off by itself when enough of the bookings behind it cancel: when the bookings still on the books from the day it counted are back to what a night like it usually has. The change log then reads: "Sudden rush" stopped applying an earlier 25% raise here: enough of the bookings behind it cancelled.

**Good to know** · The five starter rules include "Sudden-spike catcher" (Surging, past day, raise 25%, waits 1 day), "Hot-week surge" (Much Faster Than Normal, past week, raise 25%, waits 2 days) and "Warm-date bump" (Faster Than Normal, past month, raise 10%, waits 3 days). Together they step up as the pace climbs.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with two conditions: **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 3, and **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50, then **Decrease the rate** by 15%. Tonight, tomorrow night and the night after are cut 15% while fewer than half their sellable rooms are booked. When a night fills to 50% or more, the cut comes off.

**1. Open the builder and name it**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Last minute.

**2. Set the booking window condition**

In the first row, change **Metric** to **Booking window (days to stay)**. Set **Compare** to **Less than** and **Threshold** to 3.

**3. Add the occupancy condition**

Click **+ Add condition**. The new row is **Sellable occupancy (%)**. Set **Compare** to **Less than** and **Threshold** to 50. The line under **Conditions** says it: the rule matches when all of its conditions are true.

**4. Set the cut, pick the room types, add it**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Decrease the rate** and type 15 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. Leave every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**.

Booking window is the number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar: tonight is 0, tomorrow night is 1. **Less than** 3 covers 0, 1 and 2, so tonight and the next two nights. The count moves every day, so each night slides into the rule's range as it gets closer, and out again once it has passed.

The occupancy condition is what keeps this from cutting a night that is already selling. A night at 50% or more is left alone. Both conditions must hold at the same time.

The row on the Rules tab reads "Occupancy below 50% · Booking window below 3 days" with "-15%". In the change log a change reads: "Last minute" lowered this night 15%, from $150.00 to $127.50. It was 40% full with 1 day to go, under the 50% mark and past the 3-day mark you set.

This is a standard rule. It holds one cut while both conditions hold and takes it off when either stops: when the night fills to 50% or more, or when the night passes. It never cuts the same night twice.

**Example** · It is Tuesday at The Harbour Inn. Wednesday night has 8 of 20 rooms booked (40%) and is 1 day away, so Standard drops from $150 to $127.50, Deluxe from $200 to $170 and Suite from $300 to $255. Two more bookings on Wednesday morning take it to 10 of 20 (50%), which is not less than 50, so on the next run the cut comes off.

**Not yet** · A rule cannot be limited to certain weekdays or dates, so this rule runs every night of the year. To keep a weekend or event out of it, type those nights' prices and switch this rule off (which stops it on every night) until the nights have passed. A typed price alone does not stop a rule that starts to hold later. Read [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@67).

In the rule builder, tick **Change prices on different room types**. The room type list splits in two: **Measure**, the room types whose occupancy or bookings the rule reads, and **Change**, the room types whose prices it moves. Tick Standard under **Measure** and Suite under **Change**. When Standard is more than 80% full, the Suite price rises.

**1. Open the builder and set the condition**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. Name it Suites follow Standard. Leave the condition on **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** 80, and under **Rate adjustment** choose **Increase the rate** by 10%.

**2. Split the room type lists**

Under the room types, tick **Change prices on different room types**. The single **Apply to room types** list becomes two lists, **Measure** and **Change**. The **?** beside the box explains: you watch occupancy, pickup and booking speed on the Measure room types, and when the rule fires you change prices on the Change room types.

**3. Pick Measure and Change**

Under **Measure**, click **Clear** and then tick Standard only. Under **Change**, click **Clear** and tick Suite only.

**4. Add it**

Click **Add Rule**. The row's **Room Types** column reads "Watches Standard · Changes Suite".

Occupancy is measured over the **Measure** list alone. The Harbour Inn's Standard has 12 rooms, so 10 booked reads as 83% and the rule fires: Suite goes from $300 to $330, while Standard's own price is untouched. Booking speed and pickup conditions work the same way, counting only bookings in the measured room types.

Only room types that count as rooms are offered under **Measure**. A Meeting Room, unticked as a room on the **PMS** tab, can be changed by a rule but never measured. Under **Change**, every room type is offered, rooms or not.

The change log names both sides: Standard was 83% full, past the 80% mark you set, on a line for Suite.

In the rule builder, the chips under **Apply to room types** are the room types the rule covers. Every type that counts as a room starts ticked. Click a chip to untick it and the rule leaves that room type alone, in what it measures and in what it changes. A saved rule cannot be changed, so for an existing rule delete it and add it again with the right chips.

**1. Open the builder**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule** and fill in the name, condition and rate adjustment as usual.

**2. Untick the chips you want left out**

Under **Apply to room types**, each room type is a chip. A ticked chip is highlighted. Click Suite to untick it. The summary beside the label counts what is left, for example "2 of 4 room types". **Select all** ticks every chip and **Clear** unticks them all.

**3. Add the rule**

Click **Add Rule**. The row's **Room Types** column lists the types it covers: "Standard, Deluxe".

At least one room type must be ticked. Leaving none gives "Select at least one room type."

With the single list, the rule measures and changes the same room types. It measures the ticked types that count as rooms, and it changes every ticked type. So a rule ticked on Suite alone measures Suite's occupancy on its own (The Harbour Inn has 2 Suites, so 1 booked is 50%) and moves Suite's price only.

A chip tagged "not a room" is a type you have unticked as a room on the **PMS** tab, such as a Meeting Room. It starts unticked in the builder. Tick it and the rule changes its price, but never measures it: a court or meeting room has no occupancy to read.

If you tick only "not a room" types, the rule has nothing to measure. An occupancy, booking speed or pickup condition then can never be true, so a rule with any of them never fires. Only a rule whose single condition is booking window (the number of days until the stay) still fires, because it counts days, not bookings.

**Good to know** · To measure one set of room types and change another, tick **Change prices on different room types** under the chips. For example, measure Standard and change only the Meeting Room. Read [Let suites follow your standard rooms](@77).

A rule's room types cannot be changed after it is saved. Delete it with **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes** and add it again with the chips you want. The starter rules MAYA built from your history cover every room type that counts as a room, so to keep one of them off your suites, delete that starter rule and rebuild it. Its settings are in the row: the condition, the window and wait, and the percentage.

Open the **Rate Simulator** tab, set up a made-up night, click **+ Build a test rule** and fill it in. The **What would happen** table shows what each room type would become. Nothing is saved and no price reaches your property system until you click **Save This Rule**, and even then the rule arrives on the **Rules** tab switched **Off**. Turn it **On** when you are ready.

**1. Set up the night**

On the **Rate Simulator** tab, under **The night**, pick a **Stay date** (it starts 30 days ahead) and a **Booking speed** level. Leave it on **Not enough history** and booking speed rules stay quiet, which is what happens on a night MAYA cannot measure.

**2. Set up the rooms**

Under **Your rooms**, each room type that counts as a room has a **Base price** (starting at the nearest price MAYA has published), an **Occupancy** percentage (starting at 70%) and a **Picked up** count. Its floor and ceiling show under **Guardrails**. Change the numbers to the night you want to test.

The **What would happen** table shows each room type's **Base**, what it **Becomes**, the **Change**, and **Because**, which names the rules that fired. A price held at a limit is tagged "held at your floor" or "held at your ceiling". The **Didn't fire** list says why a rule stayed quiet, for example "Conditions not met" with what it saw.

**5. Save it, switched off**

Click **Save This Rule**. A green line reads "Rule Added to Rules Tab and Initialized as Disabled". Until you press it, the rule exists only on this screen. On the **Rules** tab, switch it **On** when you are ready.

Saving a rule needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

The maths is the same as a real run's, so the numbers are what a real run would produce for the night you typed. Your existing rules are all ticked under **Rules in play**, switched-off ones included, so you can see what turning one on would do. Untick any to leave it out of the test.

Three things it simplifies, as the note at the foot of the page says:

- A standard rule (occupancy or booking window) fires on the way into its condition and holds, so the table shows where the night settles rather than each step.
- When several booking speed or pickup rules match, a real run lets only one of them act on each night and room type, while the simulator adds them all.
- A booking speed or pickup rule that is still true once its wait is over adjusts the night again, which the simulator shows only once.

It is one run, not where a night ends up over a week.

There is no floor and ceiling editor yet. Setup sets them from your answers and your own past rates: check them in the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab. A limit still at $1.00 or $99,999.99 can be set from a **Get suggestions from my data** card. To change one already set, answer the floor and ceiling questions again, or email us the numbers.

Before you set anything, look at what you already have. Setup fills in floors and ceilings for you, so do not assume yours are still at $1.00 and $99,999.99.

Your answers to the floor and ceiling questions go on first. The floor goes to every room type, and the ceiling to each room type whose highest sold rate is at or below it, unless the two clash (see below).

Then the history import fills any floor still at $1.00, or ceiling still at $99,999.99, from that room type's own past rates. There is no card to accept. The floor is 40% of what the room type typically sells for, rounded to the nearest $5 and never under $10, and needs at least 30 room nights sold for that room type (a room night is one room for one night). The ceiling is 1.5 times the rate it rarely sells above, rounded to the nearest $10, and needs at least 200 room nights sold.

A limit stays at the default when the room type had sold too few room nights, or looked like it might not be a room. A ceiling needs far more room nights than a floor, and a room type with few rooms gets there more slowly. At The Harbour Inn, Standard has 12 rooms and reaches 200 room nights after about 17 full nights. Suite has 2 rooms and needs at least 100. So a room type can have a floor and still carry the $99,999.99 ceiling. To see yours, open the **Rate Simulator** tab and read the **Guardrails** column. It shows the floor and ceiling of every room type that counts as a room.

**1. Ask for suggestions**

On the **Rules** tab, click **Get suggestions from my data** beside the **Pricing Rules** heading. A panel headed "Here's exactly what happens" says that nothing changes by itself. Click **Sounds good**. The button shows a waiting message while MAYA reads your history again.

**2. Open the review**

When it is done, the button reads "3 suggestions ready →". Click it to open the review page, under the heading "Recommendations from your data".

**3. Edit the amount and set it**

A card reads "Set a floor for "Standard"?" with the reason under it, for example: Standard has typically sold for $150 a night, so MAYA suggests a floor of $60. The amount sits in a box labelled **Amount to set**. Leave it, or type your own number. The button reads **Set it to 60** and follows what you typed. Click it. **No thanks** leaves the room type as it is.

Cards only fill gaps: a floor still at $1.00 or a ceiling still at $99,999.99. A limit that is already set, by your answers, the import or an earlier card, gets no card, whatever its number. So if setup filled every limit, you will see no floor or ceiling cards. The amount on a card is your own answer where it fits, and otherwise a number from the room type's past rates, worked out the same way as during the import.

Accepting a suggestion needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Reading your history again is limited to 5 runs in 15 minutes, needs a paid property with a connected system, and can take a while on a large property.

The floor and ceiling questions from setup can be answered again at any time, at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions once your property is connected. They are the same five cards, all skippable. Skip to the floor card, answer it, then the ceiling card, then skip the rest.
- **The floor** you type replaces the floor of every active room type, except where it clashes.
The floor

- **The ceiling** you type goes only to room types whose highest sold rate is at or below it, so a property-wide ceiling never pins a suite below what it already sells for. Other room types keep their ceiling.
The ceiling

- **A clash is skipped without a message.** A room type takes the new numbers only if its floor still ends up at or below its ceiling. If your floor is above a room type's ceiling, or your ceiling is below its floor, that room type keeps the floor and ceiling it had.
A clash is skipped without a message

- **Your saved answers go on again each time.** Saving the floor card, the ceiling card or the fifth card writes both of your saved answers again, by the same rules. So answering only the ceiling card still puts your saved floor answer, if you gave one, back on every room type. Skipping a card changes nothing.

Nothing on screen tells you when a room type was skipped. Check the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab afterwards.

To give one room type a floor of its own, or to lower a ceiling under a room type's past rates, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) with the room type and the numbers.
Your saved answers go on again each time

Every price your rules produce is held inside the room type's floor and ceiling. So is your system's own rate on a night where no rule has fired: under the floor, the floor is published, and over the ceiling, the ceiling. The change log says so when a limit stops a rule: "That would have gone past your $300.00 ceiling for Standard, so it stopped there." A booking speed or pickup rule that cannot move the price in its own direction against a limit does not fire.

**Good to know** · When the amber banner says a rule keeps adjusting a night and your limit is still the default, it offers **Ask MAYA for a ceiling** or **Ask MAYA for a floor**. The link takes you to the **Rules** tab, where **Get suggestions from my data** is the next click.

**Not yet** · No per-room-type editor, no floor or ceiling per night or per season, and no way to lower a ceiling under a room type's past rates yourself. The floor cannot be 0: use a comp night for a free night.

Open the **PMS** tab, scroll to **Room types**, and untick **Counts as a room** on the meeting room's row. It saves at once. From then on that type is left out of sellable occupancy, the calendar's room counts, booking speed and the room count you are billed for. It can still be priced if a rule changes it.

**1. Open the room types**

Go to the **PMS** tab. Under the connection cards is a section headed **Room types**, one row per active room type with its unit count and a **Counts as a room** checkbox.

**2. Untick Counts as a room**

On the Meeting Room's row, untick the box. It saves straight away, with no confirmation. The row dims and gains a "not a room" tag. If it did not save, the box snaps back and a short error shows.

Changing it needs Revenue Manager access or higher. The change queues a re-price of the next 60 nights, so occupancy rules read the new figure within a few minutes.

- **Sellable occupancy.** Only ticked types are divided by. The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms plus a Meeting Room. With it ticked, 18 booked rooms read as 18 of 21 (86%). Unticked, they read as 18 of 20 (90%).
Sellable occupancy
- **The calendar.** The day card's "18/20 rooms" and its percentage count ticked types only. Revenue on the card still sums every type.
The calendar
- **Booking speed.** Bookings for an unticked type are not counted, and it is never measured by a rule.
Booking speed

- **Rules.** In the rule builder the type is tagged "not a room" and starts unticked. A rule that ticks it can still change its price. A rule that measures only unticked types (the Meeting Room alone, say) never fires on occupancy, pickup or booking speed. A booking window condition counts days, not bookings. So a rule whose only condition is booking window still fires and changes the room types it is set to change.
Rules

- **Your bill.** The room count MAYA measures from your system leaves out unticked types. Lowering the count never lowers your bill on its own: set it on the **Billing** page. Read [Change the room count you pay for](@88).

**Good to know** · During setup MAYA unticks types whose names are plainly not bedrooms (parking, meeting, conference, spa treatment and the like) and asks about softer cases on the review page with a card headed "Is "Pool Cabana" actually a room?". Your answer is final either way, and you can change it here any time.
Your bill

Go to the **PMS** tab, find the room type under **Room types**, click **+ Rooms out of service**, enter the dates and the number of rooms, and **Save**. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, so occupancy reads against what you can sell. Nothing is sent to your property system, and rooms you block there are not read by MAYA, so enter them here.

**1. Find the room type**

On the **PMS** tab, scroll to **Room types** and find the row. Under it, click **+ Rooms out of service**.

**2. Fill in the block**

**From** is the first night. **To** is the last night and defaults to the same night. **Units** is how many rooms of that type are off sale, from 1 up to the type's count. **Reason (optional)** takes a few words, such as Renovation.

**3. Save**

Click **Save**. The block lists under the row as "3 out of service", the dates, and the reason, with a **Clear** link. MAYA re-prices the next 60 nights at once.

Adding or clearing a block needs Revenue Manager access or higher. One block can cover at most 366 nights. Blocks on the same nights add up, and the total cannot exceed the type's units: MAYA tells you how many you can still block.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. A rule reads it over the room types it measures, and a new rule measures every type that counts as a room. At The Harbour Inn that is Standard, Deluxe and Suite: 20 rooms, or 17 with 3 Standard rooms out of service.

Take a night with 8 Standard, 5 Deluxe and 1 Suite booked. A rule that measures all three reads 14 of 17, or 82%, instead of 14 of 20, or 70%. A rule that measures Standard alone (only Standard ticked) reads 8 of 9, or 89%, instead of 8 of 12, or 67%. Either way, an occupancy rule set at **Greater than** 80 fires with the block and not without it.

The calendar shows the same reduced counts. On this night the day card reads "14/17 rooms", and the day detail reads "Booked 8/9" for Standard.

**Good to know** · A block held in your system for a wedding or a group, with no bookings behind it, is invisible to MAYA in the same way. Entering those rooms as out of service keeps the night from reading as empty. Read [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@67).

Click **Clear** beside the block. The rooms come back into the sellable count from the next run. Cleared blocks are kept for the record but no longer shown. A block whose last night has passed needs no clearing: it only ever counted for its own nights.

**Not yet** · Blocks are per room type, not per room, and MAYA does not read blocks, allotments or out-of-order rooms from any property system. A whole-property closure that is still to come is not a closed period either: those nights are still priced. Closed periods only come from your setup review.

Find the change in the **Change Log** tab, click **How did we know?**, then **Why did you expect that?** and **Show me the nights you compared**. On the night that was not normal, click **Not a fair comparison?**, choose a reason such as **Local Event or Festival**, keep **Just set aside this one date (recommended)** and click **Set this date aside**. From the next run that date is left out of comparisons for 3 years. **Undo** under **Your corrections** puts it back.

**2. Show the nights it compared**

Click **Why did you expect that?**, then **Show me the nights you compared**. One row per past night appears, such as "Fri, Jul 18 2025" with "12 bookings in the same stretch" and why it was picked.

**3. Flag the odd one**

On the row that was not normal, click **Not a fair comparison?**. Under "What made Fri, Jul 18 2025 not a fair comparison?", choose a reason from the list: **Local Event or Festival**, **Sporting Event or Tournament**, **Conference or Convention**, **Renovation or Rooms Out of Service**, **Utility or Amenity Outage**, **Group Buyout**, **Nearby Competitor Closed or Sold Out**, **Severe Weather**, **Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption**, **Booking Data Looks Wrong**, **Other** (which asks for a few words), or the holiday reason covered in [Handle a holiday MAYA does not have](@84).

Leave **Just set aside this one date (recommended)** selected and click **Set this date aside**. The row now reads "Set aside" with a note that it is not used from the next run onward.

Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Anyone on the property can open the panel and read the nights.

From the next pricing run the date is left out of every comparison and out of the reading of your seasons. The expected count for the night you started from is worked out again from the nights that remain, and any booking speed rule reads the new figure on its next check. Nothing about the past is changed and no price is moved by the correction itself.

Some reasons offer two more scopes. **This happens every year around this time** starts a yearly pattern: once the same reason is reported near the same time of year from 2 different years, a window of about 5 days either side is left out every year. **This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced)** needs reports from 3 different years before it changes anything about seasons. Until those counts are reached, only the single date is set aside.

**Example** · Priya opens a cut on Fri, Nov 13 2026 at The Harbour Inn. One of the eight nights compared is Fri, Nov 15 2024, with 14 bookings in the same stretch, the weekend of a food festival that has since moved. She sets it aside with **Local Event or Festival**. On the next run the usual count for a night like this drops from 6 to 5, and the cut rule reads the night as Normal.

At the top of the **Change Log** tab, **Your corrections** lists every date you have set aside, each with **Undo**. Undo makes the date comparable again from the next run. A flagged date can also be seen on the row itself the next time you open that night's comparisons.

**Not yet** · Dates can only be set aside from a change's comparisons, so you cannot flag a date before it has been used. Closed periods (a stretch when the whole property was shut) are confirmed on the setup review, not here.

MAYA uses 17 US holidays for every property, wherever it is, and has no screen to add another or switch one off. The workaround: when a change's comparisons include a past night that fell on your holiday, click **Not a fair comparison?** on it, choose the holiday reason (the first in the list), pick **This happens every year around this time** and click **Set this date aside**. The date is left out at once. After the same report from 2 different years, the days around it are left out of comparisons every year, for as long as those reports are under 3 years old. If your holiday never shows up in a comparison, email us its dates and we can set them aside for you, or type prices for the holiday nights yourself.

The same 17 holidays, each covering a short stretch of nights around the day itself, apply to every property, wherever it is. For a property in Canada, the UK or anywhere else, a night in the stretch around US Thanksgiving or Memorial Day is still compared with the same position around that US holiday in earlier years. An ordinary night is never compared with a night in one of those stretches.

There is no setting to switch a US holiday off yet. Setting its past nights aside takes them out of comparisons. It does not make them ordinary nights.

Your own holidays are different. A night on one that falls outside every US stretch is compared with ordinary nights of the same weekday and time of year. A past night on it can also turn up as a comparison for an ordinary night and make it read slow.

**Good to know: Some of your holidays already line up** · A few holidays outside the US fall inside a US stretch every year, so they are already compared by their position around it: Good Friday and Easter Monday (Easter), Boxing Day (Christmas), the UK's late May bank holiday (Memorial Day), and Canada's Labour Day, Thanksgiving and Remembrance Day (Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day and Veterans Day). Under **Why did you expect that?** the line names the US holiday.

**1. Find a comparison that used your holiday**

On the **Change Log** tab, open a booking speed change with **How did we know?**, then **Why did you expect that?** and **Show me the nights you compared**. Look for a past date that fell on your holiday.

**2. Flag it with the holiday reason**

Click **Not a fair comparison?** on that row and choose **Holiday We Don't Have Modeled**.

**3. Choose the yearly scope**

Select **This happens every year around this time**. The hint under it says the date is set aside now, and that treating it as a yearly pattern needs reports like this one from 2 different years.

**4. Set it aside**

Click **Set this date aside**. Repeat when a comparison uses the same holiday from another year.

Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

- **At once:** that date is left out of comparisons and out of the reading of your seasons, from the next run.

Once a booking speed or pickup rule has adjusted the same night three times, an amber banner at the top of every tab asks what to do, and the rule keeps adjusting until you answer. **Keep adjusting** lets it carry on and stops the question for that night. **Stop for this night** means no more changes there, while what it already did stays. A stopped night shows under the rule on the **Rules** tab, where **Let it run again** puts the rule back on it.

The banner is headed with the rule and the count, for example "Hot-week surge" has raised Sat, Nov 14 2026 3 times, and the line under it: It keeps raising these nights until you stop it. For several nights it reads "Hot-week surge" has raised 4 nights, 3 times each.

Each night has a card: the date, how many times on which room types ("3 times on Standard, once on Deluxe"), what the rule read (In the 7 days it measured, 9 bookings came in. A night like this usually has about 4 by then.) and where the price can go: If it keeps raising, the price can climb to your $300.00 ceiling for Standard. If the limit is still MAYA's default, the card says so and offers **Ask MAYA for a ceiling** or **Ask MAYA for a floor**, which takes you to the **Rules** tab.

While your property is simulating the wording is "would have raised" and "would climb", because nothing has been sent.

**1. Choose for one night or for all of them**

With several nights, two buttons come first: **Keep adjusting on all 4 nights** and **Stop on all 4 nights**. Under them the nights are listed. Click **Answer night by night** to open a card per night, each with **Keep adjusting** and **Stop for this night**.

**2. Keep adjusting**

The rule carries on as it is, and MAYA stops asking about that night. Other rules are unaffected.

**3. Stop for this night**

The rule makes no more changes on that night. For a rule that raises, the raises it already made stay, unless enough of the bookings behind them cancel. For a rule that cuts, what it cut stays. Your other rules keep working on the night.

Answering needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Anyone else sees the banner with "Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer this." The **?** beside the buttons repeats what each answer does.

A rule you stopped on nights still to come shows an amber chip under its switch on the **Rules** tab: "Stopped on 4 nights", with a **?** that names them and a **Let it run again** link. One click clears the stop on every stopped night of that rule. The rule can adjust them again from the next run, starting from the price it left, and MAYA asks again after three more adjustments.

**Good to know** · The question is per rule and per night. It can arrive a few minutes after the third adjustment. A price you type on the night, or deleting the rule, closes the question without an answer. Deleting and re-adding a rule starts its count at zero.

| The Billing page says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Your saved card stopped working | MAYA checks the card with a zero-amount check that moves no money, once after checkout and again about 48 hours later. This one was declined. Nothing has failed yet. | Before the next charge, update the card, then email us so we move your subscription onto it. The warning clears by itself the next time a payment succeeds. |

The banner is checked only when the page loads, so reload after switching if it has not appeared. The review is also always at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. The property starts in simulation like the first, and a General Manager or Hotel Admin takes it live from the review.

The button for that, **Turn them on for real**, is there only if MAYA built starter rules for the property (about 60 days of history). It also goes once anyone runs **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab for that property. Without the button, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) with the property's name and we switch it live.

If you chose **Hold My Hand** or **Let Me Drive** for your first property, that choice carries over. Your choice is saved with your login, so you are asked once, not again for each property. The five setup questions are not asked for the new property either. To answer them, pick it in the **Property** dropdown and open maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions. If your login has never made the choice (you joined your first property by invitation, say), it appears after payment.

If one Cloudbeds login covers several properties, one **Connect App** connects them all. They line up for payment one at a time, headed "Property 2 of 3", with a **Not now** link to set one aside. Set-aside properties wait under "Properties not set up yet" on the **Billing** page with a **Set up** button.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA signs one ThinkReservations property up at a time, and a ThinkReservations login that covers several properties is refused at the connect step. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Add%20a%20property) with the property's name and we set it up.

**Mews:** Mews properties are connected by us. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Add%20a%20property) and we walk through the keys with you.
- **Shared:** your login. One email and password reach every property you belong to. Your role can differ per property. The **Hold My Hand** or **Let Me Drive** choice is made once per login too.
Shared

- **Per property:** the subscription and its bracket (brackets are never pooled), the trial, the code, the rules, floors and ceilings, room type answers, manual prices, simulation or live state, and the team. Invite a colleague from each property's **Team** page.
Per property

- **Switching:** the **Property** dropdown to the right of the tabs lists your active properties by name. The dropdown opens on the property you used last in that browser. After you sign out, it opens on the first property in alphabetical order.

**Good to know** · Rules are not copied between properties. Each property gets its own copy of the five starter rules, made only if that property has about 60 days of history. Any rule you build belongs to the property you built it on.

**Not yet** · No group view across properties, no shared rules, no one-click invite to every property, and no pooled billing. Each property is billed at its own room count.
Switching

Open the **Change Log** tab: each change a rule makes names the rule and the reason. To fix a night now, type the price you want. To undo a rule's changes everywhere, delete the rule. Most runs change nothing, and nothing is sent until you go live.

One of your rules may have. Open the **Change Log** tab and find the night. Each change names the rule that acted and the reason, in one or two sentences. The change log only reaches back about 50 minutes. For an older change, check the night's **Current price** and any **Manual** badge on the calendar, and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) the night and room type: the detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you. If a booking speed rule cut the night, the sentence reads something like "Bookings came in much slower than normal this past month: 1, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now."

That reading can be right and still feel wrong, for two reasons.

First, a wedding booked as one reservation is one booking. For booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. A 20-room wedding on your Saturday is 20 booked rooms for occupancy and one booking for booking speed. If similar Saturdays had received 5 bookings by this point, one booking reads as much slower, and a cut rule that measures only booking speed fires. It does not look at how full the night is unless you gave it an occupancy condition.

Second, MAYA reads bookings, not blocks or allotments, from Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations and Mews. A wedding held as a block in your property system, with no booking behind it, adds nothing to the count and nothing to occupancy.

**Fix it now.** On the **Calendar** tab, open the night, and on the room type card type the price you want. Use **through…** to cover the whole weekend in one save. On a live Cloudbeds property that price goes to your system now, and ThinkReservations applies it shortly after. With Mews a typed price is never sent, although the confirmation says "Sending to Mews now". Rules that had already moved the night are paused for that room type. Read [Setting a price yourself](@49).
Fix it now

**Keep the rules off those nights.** Your typed price is not a lock. Once its wait is over, a booking speed rule reads the night again and can cut on top of your price. To keep your number, switch off the cut rules on the **Rules** tab until the weekend has passed. Off stops a rule on every night, and what it already did stays. Read [Hold a price for an event](@67).
Keep the rules off those nights

**Prevent it next time.** Give your cut rules an occupancy condition, so a full night can never read as one to cut. A rule cannot be edited. Switch the old rule **Off** (its cuts stay) and add a new one with **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50 as a second condition. Deleting the old rule instead undoes every cut it made, on every night.

For a block held in your system without bookings, enter those rooms as out of service on the **PMS** tab so occupancy reads against what you can sell.

**Careful** · A cut made by a booking speed rule never comes off by itself. A raise comes off when enough of the bookings behind it cancel. A cut stays until you type a price or delete the rule. Other rules stack on top of it.

Read [A price looks wrong](@95) for the other surprises, and [Booking speed](@34) for how the count works.
Prevent it next time

Most pricing runs change nothing, and the change log hides them by default. Press **Show All Cycles** and you will see a run about every five minutes reading "Prices checked" and nothing needed to change. A quiet property is a property whose rules were checked and found no reason to act.

The usual reasons a rule stays quiet:
- **A standard rule holds.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions changes the price once when its condition starts to hold, then holds it. It does not fire again every day.
A standard rule holds

- **A booking speed rule is waiting.** After it acts on a night it leaves that night alone for its wait, from 1 day to 2 weeks. When the wait is over it counts only bookings made since the night was last raised (or last cut), so a burst it already acted on cannot make it act again.
A booking speed rule is waiting

- **Not enough history.** A booking speed rule stays quiet only when there are neither similar past nights nor enough nearby nights to read momentum from (how nearby nights are filling now). Then **How did we know?** under a change says no booking speed call was made. Occupancy and booking window rules work from day one.
Not enough history

- **A read failed.** A run whose booking read failed prices nothing and sends nothing. **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab shows the last read that worked. On Cloudbeds, **Health (last 24 hours)** also counts the requests that failed. On ThinkReservations and Mews that card always reads "No recent activity", so check **Last sync**.
A read failed

- **The subscription lapsed.** A red banner at the top of the app reads "MAYA has paused work on this property". Nothing runs until the subscription restarts. After failed payments, update your card. After a cancellation, start a new subscription. The banner says which, and its **Restart MAYA** button opens the **Billing** page.
The subscription lapsed

- **The connection is lost.** Open the **PMS** tab to check. The amber banner above the calendar, "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system's name), appears only once that tab has been opened in your session. Nothing runs until someone reconnects.
The connection is lost

- **Rules are switched Off.** The **Rules** tab shows each rule's **Status**.

In simulation the log still fills. Every run happens, every change is written down, and nothing is sent. So a quiet log is quiet for one of the reasons above, not because you are simulating.

Read [A rule did not fire](@96) for the full checklist.
Rules are switched Off

Yes, three ways, and one that does not work.

1. **Type the price you want.** On the **Calendar** tab, open the night, type the price on the room type card and press **Save**. On a live Cloudbeds property it is sent now, and ThinkReservations applies it shortly after. With Mews it is never sent. This is the fastest fix for one night or a range.
Type the price you want

2. **Delete the rule.** On the **Rules** tab, **Delete** undoes every price change the rule made, on every night. The dialog offers **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**. Deleting cannot be undone, and the rule's history stays in the change log under the name "Pricing rule".
Delete the rule

3. **Stop it on that night.** When the amber banner asks, **Stop for this night** means the rule makes no more changes there. What it already did stays.

Switching a rule **Off** does not undo anything. Its changes stay exactly where they are, which is the point: you can pause a rule without prices jumping. The delete dialog's other button, **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes**, does exactly that.

Read [Undo a price change](@66) for the steps, and [When a change comes off](@40) for what comes off on its own.
Stop it on that night

MAYA sends prices only when you have gone live, and only for nights whose price changed since the last send. There is no "sending" light on the dashboard, and no badge that says live or simulation. The word live beside the time at the top right of the calendar ("Updated 3:05:12 PM · live") only means the calendar refreshes by itself. It shows in simulation too. Here is how to tell.

- **The go-live card.** Open the review screen at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. The card headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules" shows "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices" once you are live, and the button **Turn them on for real** while you are simulating. The card appears only when MAYA built starter rules for you during setup, which needs about 60 days of history, and it goes once someone clicks **Get suggestions from my data**. Without it, read [Going live](@54).
The go-live card

- **A price you typed.** If you typed a price for a real reason lately, its confirmation read "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." on a live property and "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." while simulating. Do not type a price only to test this: on a live property it sends the price, and it takes any booking speed or pickup change off that night for good.
A price you typed
- **The alert banner.** In simulation the amber banner says a rule "would have raised" a night. Live, it says "has raised".
The alert banner

- **Compare a night.** Open a night in your property system and in MAYA. Live, the rate there matches MAYA's **Current price** within a few minutes of a change.

Sending problems show in the **Change Log** tab as an item headed "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" (or your system's name). Success is silent. **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is the last time bookings were read, not the last time a price was sent.

Mews: nothing is ever sent, live or not. MAYA reads Mews bookings and shows prices, and sending to Mews is not built yet.

Read [Simulation mode](@53) and [How prices reach your property system](@55).
Compare a night

The wedding was booked as one reservation for 12 rooms. That is 12 rooms for occupancy (100% of Standard) and one booking for booking speed. Sam opens the Friday, types $150 with **through…** set to the Saturday, and presses **Save**. The confirmation reads "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now. Paused 1 rule on these 2 nights for this room; new rules will apply on top."

- [A price looks wrong](@95): jumped 50%, $1, $99,999, stuck at the floor, changed with no rule named, back to the base rate, an unpriced night.
- [A rule did not fire](@96): the day card says 85% but the rule did not act, fired on Deluxe but not Standard, 59 days out but not 61.
- [Booking speed reads oddly](@97): faster from two bookings, compared with a festival, a group counted once, a holiday MAYA does not have.
- [Occupancy looks wrong](@98): differs from Cloudbeds, over 100%, tiny on ThinkReservations, a room type with 100 rooms.
- [Prices are not reaching your property system](@99): went live and nothing is sent, the old price is still in Cloudbeds, a rate you changed there was written over.

- [Account and billing problems](@102): cannot sign in, "Payment received" is stuck, billed for 20 rooms but running 24.
- [Messages you might see, explained](@103): every on-screen message, A to Z, with what to do.

Start in the **Change Log** tab: every change names the rule and the reason. A big jump is usually two rules stacked (percentages compound). A $1 or $99,999 price is the default floor or ceiling, which stop nothing in most currencies, so set real ones. A change with no rule named is your own rate changing in your property system, or a price someone typed. A night with no price is past the 60-night window (tonight and the next 59), closed in your system, or not run yet.

The change log shows the chain with running prices, each step followed by its own reason:

"Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $200.00 to $220.00.
It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.
Then "Hot-week surge" raised it 25%, from $220.00 to $275.00.
Bookings came in much faster than normal this past week: 12, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now.

Once one booking speed rule has adjusted the same night three times, the amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner asks you whether to carry on or stop. Until you answer, it keeps going. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@42).

If the jump is bigger than you want, set a ceiling. The default ceiling is $99,999.99, which stops nothing in most currencies. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

Deluxe is $200. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) takes it to $220. "Hot-week surge" (Much Faster Than Normal, Increase 25%) takes it to $275. The Deluxe ceiling is $400, so $275 is published. Had the ceiling been $250, the log would add "That would have gone past your $250.00 ceiling for Deluxe, so it stopped there."

Because booking speed compares a night with what similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival, not with how full it is. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out. If those nights had received none at all by then, 2 or 3 bookings in a week read Much Faster Than Normal, or Faster Than Normal when there are fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with. If they had averaged a fraction of a booking, 0.4 say, it takes 3, because a difference of less than 2 bookings always reads Normal.

To keep raises off empty nights, add **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** as a second condition to your raise rules. A rule needs every condition true at once. You cannot edit a rule. Switch the old one **Off** to keep the raises it made, or delete it to undo them on every night, then add a new rule with the extra condition. A starter rule added again ranks with the rules you build, no longer above them.

A cut rule with only a booking speed condition does not look at occupancy. It counts bookings made in its window (past day, week or month) and compares them with similar nights over the same stretch. A night that filled up months ago and received one booking this month reads slower than a night like it usually books, and the cut fires.

A wedding or group booked as one reservation makes this more likely: for booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. Twenty rooms in one reservation are 20 rooms for occupancy and one booking for booking speed.

Fix the night by typing a price on the **Calendar** tab. Read [Start here](@94) for the wedding weekend case in full.

MAYA does not read how many rooms your system still has for sale. A full night is priced like any other: your rules run on it every cycle, and once you are live its price is sent whenever it changes (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations). That is on purpose. A cancellation puts a room back on sale, and it sells at the rate your system has at that moment, which is MAYA's latest price once you are live.

On a sold-out night:

- **An occupancy raise stays.** A rule such as "Busy nights" keeps its one raise while the night stays above its mark, and takes it off if cancellations bring the night back down to the mark or under.
An occupancy raise stays
- **A booking speed cut can still fire.** A full night takes no new bookings, so its recent count can read slow against similar nights that were still selling at the same point (the question above).
A booking speed cut can still fire

- **Raises already made stay on the price**, as they do on any night.

To keep cuts off full nights, add a **Sellable occupancy (%)** row set to **Less than** (70, say) to each cut rule. Rules cannot be edited, so switch each cut rule **Off** (its cuts stay) or delete it (its cuts are undone), then add a new one with the extra row in the rule builder. For an exact price on a sold-out night, type it on the **Calendar** tab.

Re-adding a starter rule is not an exact copy. It no longer ranks above rules you built, and "Slow-date trim" cannot be rebuilt as it was: choosing **Slower Than Normal** in the builder also covers **Much Slower Than Normal** and **Stalled**. To add a row to a starter rule and keep the rest exactly as it is, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Add%20a%20condition%20to%20a%20starter%20rule).
Raises already made stay on the price

That is the default floor, $1.00, and it stops nothing in practice. A cut rule that fires again after each wait, on a night that keeps reading slow, walks the price down until the floor catches it. With no floor set, the floor is $1.

Set a floor for each room type. On the **Rules** tab press **Get suggestions from my data**. MAYA offers a floor only for a room type whose floor is still the $1.00 default. It also needs your answer to the floor question during setup, or at least 30 sold nights for that room type. Accept the amount, or type your own, then press **Set it to**. On the amber banner, **Ask MAYA for a floor** takes you to the **Rules** tab for the same button.

Once a floor is set, a cut rule stops firing on a night that is already at the floor, because it cannot move the price in its own direction. The price stays at the floor until you type a price, delete the rule, or bookings change what the rules read.

That is the default ceiling, $99,999.99. In most currencies it has the same effect as no ceiling at all. Raise rules that keep firing on a night that keeps reading fast climb until the ceiling stops them.

In a currency where rooms sell for more than 99,999.99 (yen, won, rupiah or dong, for example), a price stuck at 99,999.99 is the default ceiling holding it down, even below your own rate. Set a real ceiling for that room type before you go live. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28#when-your-rates-are-above-the-default-ceiling).

**Good to know: The banner tells you when a limit is still the default** · When a rule has adjusted a night three times and the limit is still the default, the banner's night card says so: "Your ceiling for Suite is still MAYA's $99,999.99 default, so the price can climb that far."

Every published price is held between the room type's floor and ceiling. When the rules ask for less than the floor, the floor is published and the change log says "That would have dropped under your $80.00 floor for Standard, so it stopped there."

While the price sits at the floor, a cut rule does not fire again (it cannot move the price down), and a standard rule's cut holds while its condition holds. The price stays at the floor until something changes what the rules read, or until you act.

To lift it: type the price you want on the **Calendar** tab, or delete the cutting rule (which undoes its changes). Turning the rule **Off** keeps its changes, so the price stays at the floor. A typed price below the floor is refused rather than moved: "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." The one exception is 0, which is a comp night.

Three shapes of entry have no rule name.

**"The rate moved from $200.00 to $210.00."** MAYA had nothing else to say: no rule fired, no rule came off, no limit stepped in. Nearly always your own rate changed in your property system. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes, and prices from that base. On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate you change in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations becomes the new starting point. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@50).

Mews: MAYA reads no rates from Mews, so a night's starting price is the rate of its newest booking (or the last one saved). On a Mews property this line usually means a new booking came in at a different rate.
"The rate moved from $200.00 to $210.00."
**"Sam set the base rate to $180.00."** A person typed a price on the **Calendar** tab. The entry is labelled "Manual price". "A manager" appears when the name is not on file.
"Sam set the base rate to $180.00."

**"The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $180.00."** On a live property, a rate you changed in your system on a night MAYA had already sent to, an hour or more after the send, is kept as a manual price. The day card shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00". No name is attached.

A fourth shape names a rule you cannot find: **"Pricing rule"**. That is a rule someone has deleted. The history stays; the name does not.
"The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $180.00."

Four reasons, and the change log names each.

- **A standard rule switched off.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions holds its change while the condition holds. A cancellation drops occupancy under the mark, the condition stops holding, and the change comes off on the next run.
A standard rule switched off

- **A raise came off after cancellations.** ""Warm-date bump" stopped applying an earlier 10% raise here: enough of the bookings behind it cancelled." A raise from booking speed at **Faster Than Normal** or above comes off when the bookings still on the books from the days it counted fall back to what a night like it usually gets over those days. A raise from pickup count **Greater than** comes off when the rooms booked in the room types it measures fall back to where they were when its window opened. A cut never comes off this way, and nor does any other raise.
A raise came off after cancellations
- **A rule was deleted.** Deleting undoes every change the rule made, from the next run.
A rule was deleted

- **A manual price was cleared.** **Clear** on the room type card hands the night back to your rules. Standard rules (occupancy and booking window) that the typed price had paused apply again at once, if their condition still holds. Booking speed and pickup changes it took off stay off. Those rules change the night again only by firing anew, which they are free to do from the next run.

Read [When a change comes off](@40).
A manual price was cleared

The room type card shows "Current price" followed by a dash when no price has been published for that night and room type. Reasons, most common first:

1. **Beyond 60 nights.** Regular runs price tonight and the next 59 nights, so on those runs a night further out gets no price. One exception: when you save or clear a price further out, MAYA runs your rules once over every night from tonight to the last night you chose. Nights past the window can get a price then, and a night you typed a price for does. Those prices are sent once the nights enter the window.
Beyond 60 nights

2. **Closed in your system.** A night whose rate is 0 in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, with no price typed in MAYA, is left unpriced. MAYA does not open a closed night at the floor. Type a price if you want the night priced.
Closed in your system
3. **Not run yet.** A property that connected minutes ago has no runs until its first cycle. Give it about five minutes.
Not run yet
4. **A past night.** Past nights are never priced or changed.
A past night

5. **A room type switched off in MAYA.** A room type hidden during the review (an empty duplicate), or one we switched off after you removed it from your system, is not priced and has no card on the **Calendar** tab. A room type you only removed in your system stays priced until we switch it off, but nights that enter the 60-night window after you removed it have no rate to start from and show a dash. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Switch%20off%20a%20room%20type) its name and we switch it off. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@51).

Mews: a Mews property has no rate read, so a night's starting price comes from its bookings or from the last saved starting price, and a night with neither stays unpriced.
A room type switched off in MAYA

Because it keeps going until you answer. Once a booking speed or pickup rule has adjusted the same night three times, the amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner appears at the top of every tab: ""Hot-week surge" has raised Fri, Nov 13 2026 3 times." and "It keeps raising these nights until you stop it."

Answer **Keep adjusting** and MAYA stops asking about that night. Answer **Stop for this night** and the rule makes no more changes there. Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@42).

Stop means no more changes from that rule on that night. What it already did stays. For a cut, "What it already cut stays." For a raise, "A raise it already made stays, unless enough of the bookings behind it cancel."

To put the price where you want it, type it on the **Calendar** tab. To undo everything the rule did on every night, delete the rule. Read [Undo a price change](@66).

""Slow-date trim" lowered this night 7%, from $200.00 to $186.00." and, after its reason, "Then "Slow-date trim" lowered it another 7%, from $186.00 to $172.98." is one rule that fired, waited its wait, and fired again. A booking speed rule can act on the same night more than once. After the first change it counts only bookings made since the night was last cut (or raised), compared with similar nights over the same days, and if those still read slow it cuts again. Three times on one night brings the amber banner.

Three things clear a manual price.

- **Someone pressed **Clear**.** The confirmation reads "Cleared. MAYA is pricing this night again." Any Revenue Manager or above on the property can do it.
Someone pressed Clear

- **Your system reported the night at 0.** On a live property, a night MAYA has sent to that your system now has at 0 is read as you closing it. The night is left unpriced and the manual price there is cleared. When you load a rate again, MAYA reads it as the starting point.
Your system reported the night at 0
- **The night passed.** Manual prices apply to tonight onwards.
The night passed

A rule fires only when every one of its conditions is true on the room types it measures, and only where nothing holds it back: a wait, a stronger rule, a ceiling or floor already reached, or history it does not have. The day card shows the whole property, while a rule reads only its own room types, and **Greater than** 80 means more than 80, not 80 exactly. The **Fired** column on the **Rules** tab tells you whether it has ever acted.

Two things to check.

**Which room types the rule measures.** The day card's big percentage is sellable occupancy over every room type ticked as a room. A rule reads occupancy over the room types in its own list. If a rule such as "Busy Standard" measures only Standard, and Standard is 75% full while Deluxe and Suite are full, the property reads 85% and the rule reads 75%. The **Room Types** column on the **Rules** tab shows the list, and "Watches Standard · Changes Suite" when the rule measures one set and changes another.
Which room types the rule measures

**The comparison is strict.** **Greater than** 80 fires at 80.01% and not at 80.00%. **Less than** 50 fires at 49.9% and not at 50.00%. To fire at exactly 80% as well, set the threshold to 79.99 (the box takes decimals).

Also check the rule's other conditions. A rule with occupancy and a booking window needs both true at once. "Busy nights" with a booking window **Less than** 7 added does nothing on a night 20 days out, however full it is.
The comparison is strict

Work down this list. Most are visible on screen.

1. **The rule is Off.** The **Status** switch on the **Rules** tab. An Off rule is skipped on every night.
The rule is Off
