2. **It measures nothing.** Only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** are measured. A rule whose measured list holds only a meeting room, a court or a spa slot reads nothing, so its conditions can never be true. A room type switched off in MAYA (an empty duplicate hidden during the review, or one we switched off after you removed it from your system) is dropped from the list too.
It measures nothing

3. **It changes nothing.** A rule needs at least one room type to change, and the builder refuses to save without one. A room type switched off in MAYA is never priced, so a rule that changes only that type does nothing. A room type you only removed in your system stays priced until we switch it off, but nights that enter the 60-night window after you removed it have no rate to start from, so nothing fires on them (item 10).
It changes nothing

4. **It is waiting.** A booking speed or pickup rule leaves a night alone for its wait after acting on it, from 1 day to 2 weeks, per night and room type. A price you type on the night restarts the wait from that moment for every rule that existed when you typed it.
It is waiting

5. **It counts only what came in after the last raise.** Once a night has been raised, a booking speed rule that raises counts from that raise, whichever booking speed or pickup rule made it. On the day of the raise, only the bookings that arrived after it count. The similar past nights it is compared with are read over the same days. The same holds for cuts after a cut. A raise by a rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions never moves where counting starts. After a price you type, the rule reads its whole window again.
It counts only what came in after the last raise

6. **A stronger rule holds the night.** Only one booking speed or pickup rule fires on a night and room type in a run. A waiting rule whose condition still holds keeps the night, so nothing weaker fires under it. When two are ready at once, higher priority wins first (starter rules before yours, and every rule you build has the same priority). Then the one with more conditions wins, then, for two pickup rules with the same **Compare**, the stricter threshold, then the larger money move, then the older rule. Read [which one fires when several match](@39#which-one-fires-when-several-match).
A stronger rule holds the night
7. **The price is already at the limit.** A raise does not fire on a night already at its ceiling. A cut does not fire on a night at its floor. Neither counts as a fire.
The price is already at the limit

8. **Not enough history.** A booking speed rule needs similar past nights, or failing those enough nearby nights to read momentum from. Momentum is how nearby nights are booking now compared with the same nights a year earlier. With neither it stays quiet. The change log's **How did we know?** says "No booking-speed call was made, and rules that watch booking speed were not allowed to act on this night."
Not enough history

9. **No pickup reading from the window's start.** A pickup count rule compares booked rooms now with booked rooms when its lookback window opened (1, 3 or 7 days ago). MAYA needs a reading from that moment for every room type the rule measures. A property that connected two days ago has no reading from 3 days ago, so a 3-day pickup rule stays quiet until it does, and a room type ticked as a room today has none either. A reading more than 12 hours older than the window's start does not count.
No pickup reading from the window's start

10. **The night has no starting price.** A night your system has at 0, with no price typed in MAYA, is not priced, so nothing can fire on it. Neither is a night with no rate at all and no booking or earlier price to start from.
The night has no starting price

11. **A standard rule is already holding.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions fires once when its condition starts to hold, then holds. It does not fire again while the condition stays true, and the **Fired** count does not climb.
A standard rule is already holding

12. **The night is outside the window.** Regular runs price tonight and the next 59 nights. Past nights are never touched.

**Good to know: The Fired column** · **Fired** shows how many times a rule has acted, once per night and room type, including changes that later came off. A dash means never. Its **?** explains the count.
The night is outside the window

Rules act per room type, so every hold in the list above applies room type by room type.

- **Different ceilings and floors.** Standard's $300 ceiling may already be reached while Deluxe has room under its $400.
Different ceilings and floors
- **Different waits.** Each room type waits on its own. Standard may still be inside its wait from an earlier fire while Deluxe is free.
Different waits

- **Different counts.** One rule reads the same count for every room type it changes, taken over the room types it measures. A booking speed rule's count differs between two room types only when the night was last raised (or cut) at a different time on each, or you typed a price on one of them after that, which sends the rule back to its whole window there. To read each room type on its own, make one rule per room type, each measuring and changing only itself.
Different counts

- **A stronger rule holds Standard.** Another rule may be waiting on Standard with its condition still true, which keeps weaker rules off that room type.

The change log lists each room type's change separately, so you can read the reason for the one that fired and look for the hold on the one that did not.
A stronger rule holds Standard

Each regular run prices a window of 60 nights: tonight and the next 59, counted on your property's own calendar. On those runs, a night 61 days out is not priced or sent, and no rule reads it. It enters the window the day after tomorrow, and rules act on it then.

One exception: when you save or clear a price further out, MAYA runs your rules once over every night from tonight to the last night you chose. Nights past the window can get a price then. Those prices are sent once the nights enter the window. You can type a price up to 364 days ahead.

Only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** are measured. Occupancy is rooms booked over rooms you can sell, and booking speed counts bookings, and neither is worked out for a court, a meeting room or a spa slot. A rule whose measured list holds only such types measures nothing and never fires.

It can still price the court. Tick **Change prices on different room types** in the builder, put a real room type under **Measure** and the court under **Change**. The rule then reads the room type's occupancy or booking speed and changes the court's price. Read [Measure one set of room types, change another](@38).

When a rule measures a mix, MAYA drops the non-rooms from the figure and says so in the change log: "That 95% leaves out Pickleball Court."

The **Rate Simulator** tab lists every rule that did not fire under "Didn't fire", with one of these reasons:

| Reason | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Conditions not met" | The rule's conditions were false for the numbers you typed. The line adds what it saw: "(it saw 70% occupancy, 30 days out)". |
| "No occupancy for its signal room types" | None of the room types the rule measures counts as a room, or you gave them no rooms. |
| "Rule has no room types attached" | The rule has nothing to change. |
| "Outside the rule's date window" | The rule has a date range. Rules you make in the app have none, so you should not see this. |
| "This day of the week is excluded" | The rule excludes weekdays. Rules you make in the app run every day, so you should not see this. |

The simulator's **Booking speed** select starts on "Not enough history", which keeps booking speed rules quiet, exactly as your booking speed rules do on a real night when there is not enough history. Pick a level to see what they would do.

The simulator differs from a real run in three ways it states on screen: a standard rule shows where the night settles rather than each step, every matching booking speed rule is added rather than one winner chosen, and a rule that would fire again after its wait is shown once. Read [The Rate Simulator](@43).

The room type list in the builder does two jobs. Unticked, **Apply to room types** is both the set the rule measures and the set it changes. Ticked, **Change prices on different room types** splits it into **Measure** and **Change**. The rule card reads "Watches Standard, Deluxe · Changes Suite" when the two differ.

If a rule changed a room type you did not expect, it is in that rule's **Change** list. A rule cannot be edited: delete it (which undoes its changes) and add it again with the list you want.

Viewers can look but not change. A Viewer who presses **Add Rule** sees an error in red under the form. A Viewer who flips a switch or presses **Delete** sees nothing change. Rules need Revenue Manager access or higher. Ask a General Manager or Hotel Admin to change your role on the **Team** page. Read [Roles](@63).

Turning a rule **Off** freezes what it has done: its changes stay on the price. A booking speed or pickup rule that is Off also still marks where your active booking speed rules start counting, because the bookings behind its raises (and cuts) were already acted on. A booking speed rule that raises counts only bookings made since the night was last raised, whichever booking speed or pickup rule raised it, paused ones included. Delete the rule if you want its changes and its marks gone.

Booking speed compares how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month with how many similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. A booking counts once, however many rooms it holds. Small numbers read the way small numbers do: 2 bookings on a far-out night can be Much Faster Than Normal, and a big count can still read Normal when the difference is within the ordinary ups and downs. The **How did we know?** panel under a change shows the count, the expected count and the nights compared.

MAYA compares the bookings a night received with the bookings a night like it usually has by now, and reads the gap as one of seven levels. The smaller the numbers, the bigger the gap has to be before a night reads anything but Normal. With 5 expected you need 9 to read Faster Than Normal. With 20 expected you need 27. The outer levels, Stalled and Surging, need a bigger gap still. With fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, the level stays within one step of Normal.
Expected 5, received 9, with 5 similar nights: Faster Than Normal.

Because the nights it was compared with had received almost none by that point. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out, which is often close to nothing. When the similar nights had received none at all, 2 or 3 bookings read Much Faster Than Normal and 4 or more read Surging, provided there are at least 5 similar nights. Against an expectation of 0.4, 2 bookings still read Normal: it takes 3 to read Much Faster and 5 to read Surging. One booking stays Normal against either, because a difference of one is inside the first check.

With fewer than 5 similar nights, or a momentum reading, the call stops at Faster Than Normal. That is how 2 bookings against none end up reading Faster Than Normal.
If you would rather raise rules stayed off far-out nights, add a **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** condition, or a **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** condition, to the rule.

- "The raw numbers pointed at an even stronger call, but not by enough evidence to justify it, so we softened it one step." A Surging or Stalled reading without enough difference behind it.
- "We found only a few genuinely comparable nights, so we kept the call within one step of Normal no matter how strong the numbers looked." Fewer than 5 similar nights. A momentum reading (below) always counts as one, so it is always capped.

**Example: Expected 5 at The Harbour Inn**

Similar Saturdays had received about 5 bookings by this point. This Saturday received: 1, which reads Much Slower Than Normal. 5 or 6: Normal. 7 or 8: still Normal, because the gap is too small at this size. 9: Faster Than Normal. 10 to 17: Much Faster Than Normal. 18 or more: Surging.

Because strict matching found too few nights. MAYA looks for similar nights in three widening steps: first the same weekday in the same stretch of the year, going back up to 3 years, wanting at least 4 and taking up to 8. When that finds too few, it widens to the same weekend or weekday class, day by day. Friday and Saturday nights form the weekend class, so a Friday can be matched with a Saturday. When that is still too few, it takes the same weekday within 45 days of the date, ignoring the season.

Under **How did we know?**, **Why did you expect that?** says when it widened: "Strict matching found too few usable nights, so we relaxed the criteria a step" and each compared night carries its reason, for example "a Saturday, similar to a Friday". As your history grows, widening happens less.

Because nobody had told MAYA that weekend was unusual. Open the change, press **How did we know?**, then **Why did you expect that?**, then **Show me the nights you compared**. Beside the festival night press **Not a fair comparison?**, choose a reason such as **Local Event or Festival**, and press **Set this date aside**.

From the next run that night is left out of every comparison. Choosing "This happens every year around this time" also counts toward a yearly pattern: once the same reason has been reported from 2 different years, a window of 5 days either side is set aside every year. Read [Not a fair comparison](@48). Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

MAYA has 17 US holidays and no others, and there is no screen to add one. A night near one of those holidays is compared with the same position around the same holiday in earlier years. A night near any other holiday is compared like an ordinary night.

**Not yet** · You cannot add a holiday. The workaround is to set the night aside from the **How did we know?** panel with the reason **Holiday We Don't Have Modeled** and the scope "This happens every year around this time". After reports from 2 different years, MAYA leaves that stretch out of comparisons every year.

Read [Handle a holiday MAYA does not have](@84).

No. For booking speed a booking counts once, however many rooms it holds, on the night it is made and on every past night it is compared with. A 10-room group booked as one reservation is one booking. For occupancy it is 10 booked rooms. For a pickup count rule it is 10 room nights.

A room added to a group later is not a new booking. The group is counted at the earliest booking date across its rooms on that night.

**Cloudbeds:** Each room of a Cloudbeds reservation is stored as its own room-night, and MAYA groups them back into their reservation for booking speed. A group made as separate reservations counts as separate bookings.

**ThinkReservations:** Each room of a ThinkReservations reservation is stored as its own room-night, and MAYA groups them back into their reservation for booking speed. A group made as separate reservations counts as separate bookings.

On Cloudbeds, a booking with the status Confirmation Pending (Cloudbeds calls it not confirmed) holds a room, and Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts it as sold. MAYA counts it the same way, for occupancy and for booking speed. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not count, and a booking that cancels disappears from the count on the next read.

On Mews, every reservation counts except a cancelled one. Optional, Enquired and Requested reservations count as booked, for occupancy and for booking speed, exactly like a Confirmed one. On ThinkReservations every booking counts except cancelled bookings and no-shows.

Because it is an average. Expected is the trimmed average of what the similar nights had received over the same stretch: a plain average with fewer than 5 nights, and with 5 or more the single highest and lowest are dropped first. An expected count of 0.4 is a true statement about a quiet far-out night: most similar nights had none, one or two had one. On screen it reads "almost none" when it is under 1, and "about 3" otherwise. A similar night with no bookings at all in your history is left out of the average, not counted as zero.

Yes, but the count never goes below zero. It counts the bookings for the night that were made during the window and are still on the books. A booking that cancels drops out on the next read, so cancellations lower the count, down to none at the lowest. A booking made before the window that cancels during it was never in the count, so it changes nothing.

The nights it is compared with are counted the same way: a past booking that cancelled is not in their counts either. When the bookings behind a raise cancel, the raise can come off. Read [When a change comes off](@40).

When a night has no usable similar nights at all, MAYA falls back to momentum: how the 10 nights either side of it are booking now compared with the same nights a year earlier. The **How did we know?** panel opens like any other reading, with the count, the expected count and the level.

Under **Why did you expect that?** it explains "This night had no usable comparable nights in your history" and says it read your recent booking momentum instead. Then comes "Momentum means: how nights near this one are filling right now, compared to how the same nights were filling at this time last year." After that it says how many nearby nights could be paired, whether they are filling faster or slower than a year ago, where the starting point came from, and that a momentum reading is a best effort.

After a night has been raised, a rule that raises counts only the bookings made from that raise on, whichever booking speed or pickup rule made it, a paused one included. A raise by a standard rule, one with only occupancy or booking window conditions, does not change where counting starts.

On the day of the raise, only the bookings that reached MAYA after it count, so a burst later that day is not lost. The nights it is compared with are read over the same days (the raise's own day in full). A rule that cuts counts from the night's last cut the same way. So one burst of bookings raises a night once, and a stronger rule steps in on top only when the bookings since that raise read faster on their own.

The change log sentence names the shorter stretch: "Bookings came in faster than normal in the 4 days since this night was last raised: 6, against the 2 a night like this usually gets in those days." The **How did we know?** panel opens with "This night was last raised on Fri, Nov 13 2026. In the 4 days from that raise on, 6 bookings arrived for it, with 20 days still to go before arrival." Under **Why did you expect that?** it adds "Once a night has been raised, rules that raise count only the bookings made after that raise, whichever rule made it". That raise is always one made by a booking speed or pickup rule.

When the raise was made today, the stretch is that one day: the change log says "later on the day this night was last raised" and the panel starts "Later that day,".

A rule reads bookings across every room type it measures, then changes every room type in its change list. "Hot-week surge" measuring Standard, Deluxe and Suite reads one count for all three. Six bookings on Standard and Deluxe against an expectation of 2 read Much Faster, and the rule raises Suite too, with no Suite booking in sight.

If you want each room type read on its own, make one rule per room type, each measuring and changing only itself. Each such rule also has its own expected count, worked out from that room type's own history. A small set has a small expected count, and a difference of fewer than 2 bookings always reads Normal, so it stays at Normal more often. When it does leave Normal, a few bookings can be enough.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms and taking rooms out of service off first. It differs from Cloudbeds' headline number because Cloudbeds keeps blocked rooms in its count while MAYA removes only rooms you enter as out of service. It can read over 100%. On ThinkReservations, and on Mews where Mews gives no count, a room type is counted as 100 rooms until we change that number, so email us your counts.

Two reasons. Both can make MAYA's number higher than Cloudbeds', and the second can also make it lower.

**Blocked rooms.** Cloudbeds' own headline occupancy keeps blocked rooms in the count it divides by. MAYA does not read room blocks, allotments or out-of-order rooms from Cloudbeds. It divides by the room type's room count minus any rooms you have entered as out of service in MAYA. So a block you enter in MAYA can only make MAYA's number higher than Cloudbeds', and a block you hold only in Cloudbeds does not make them differ.
Blocked rooms

**Which room types count.** MAYA counts only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** on the **PMS** tab. If Cloudbeds lists a meeting room or a parking space as a room type and MAYA has it unticked, the two numbers divide by different room counts. MAYA's number reads higher when those types are emptier than your rooms, and lower when they are fuller.

Which bookings count is the same in both: bookings with the status confirmed, checked in, checked out or Confirmation Pending count as booked. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not.

Read [Sellable occupancy](@32) for the definition.
Which room types count

Because nobody has told MAYA. Rooms out of order in your property system are not read. Enter them in MAYA: on the **PMS** tab, under the room type, press **+ Rooms out of service**, fill in **From**, **To**, **Units** and an optional **Reason (optional)**, and press **Save**. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, and your rules run on those nights again straight away if they fall within the next 60 nights. Nothing is sent to your property system about the block.

Standard has 12 rooms, 3 are out of service, 8 are booked: 8 of 9, which is 89%. Without the block it reads 8 of 12, which is 67%.

Read [Tell MAYA rooms are out of service](@82).

Because more rooms are booked than MAYA reads as sellable. It happens when you mark rooms out of service after they were already sold (12 rooms, 3 out of service, 10 booked reads 111%), or when your property system has overbooked the night. MAYA does not cap the number.

A rule's threshold cannot go above 100, so a rule set to **Greater than** 100 fires on any overbooked night.

ThinkReservations does not report how many rooms a room type has. On Mews, the same goes for any room category Mews sends no room count for. Every room type without a count gets the same number of rooms, one number for your whole property, 100 until we change it. A room type with 6 rooms and 5 booked reads 5% instead of 83%, and occupancy rules that need a full night never fire.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Room%20counts) your room types and their room counts. We can change that one number for you, not set a count for each type. Once we have set it, occupancy is right from the next run if the room types without a count are all the same size. If they differ, it reads wrong for at least one of them. Read [ThinkReservations](@13) or [Mews](@14).

The **PMS** tab's **Room types** list shows "100 units" for a room type whose room count MAYA does not have. On Cloudbeds the count is read from your system on every cycle, so this is rare and means Cloudbeds reported none. On ThinkReservations it is every room type, and on Mews every room category Mews sends no room count for, until we set the one number for your property. Either way, email us the real count.

They are reading different room types. The day card's percentage is the whole property: every room type ticked as a room. A change log sentence such as "It was 92% full, past the 80% mark you set." is the occupancy over the room types that rule measures. A rule measuring only Standard reports Standard's occupancy.

When a rule's measured list includes a type that is not a room, MAYA leaves it out of the figure and says so: "That 92% leaves out Meeting Room." Read [A rule did not fire](@96) for how a rule reads its own room types.

Yes, for occupancy. A booking that holds 10 rooms is 10 booked rooms on each of its nights. That is different from booking speed, where a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. Read [Booking speed reads oddly](@97).

The day card's revenue figure sums every room type, including ones you have unticked as rooms. Occupancy and the "12/20 rooms" line use only the ticked ones. So a meeting room booking adds to revenue and not to occupancy.

They value a booked night differently. The day card values each booked night at the booking's rate as it was imported, falling back to its current rate, and to a placeholder of $150 when neither is on file (which is also why an empty room type shows "ADR $150.00"). A pickup count rule set to **Revenue (currency)** sums each booked night's current rate as your system reports it. The two can differ for the same night. Neither figure is sent anywhere.

MAYA adds up the nightly rates your system reports for booked nights. It never adds tax or takes off a booking site's commission, and what the rate includes depends on your system: in Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations it is the room rate on the same basis as your own rates, and in Mews it is the booking total, taxes included, split across its nights. A report that adds taxes, fees or extras, or takes off commission, will differ. [The calendar](@45#one-day-line-by-line) has the detail for each system.

**Not yet** · Booked revenue is shown per night on the calendar and used by revenue pickup rules. There is no revenue report and no export. The day card shows occupancy and room revenue for each night, not the bookings behind them.

Give a new price two cycles, about ten minutes, then open the **Change Log** tab. A problem that needs you, such as a lost connection or a rate rule in your system, sits at the top at once as "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds", with the cause and what to do. One that clears on its own is shown only if it lasts 2 hours, and a time zone mismatch usually not at all. Nothing is sent while you are simulating, nothing is ever sent to Mews, a price of 0 is never sent, and a night past the 60-night window (tonight and the next 59) waits until it enters it.

Check these in order.

1. **Wait two cycles.** Prices go out about every five minutes, and only prices that changed since the last send. The first send to a night MAYA has never sent to also waits until a fresh read of your own rates has succeeded, within the last hour, so that MAYA writes over a rate it has freshly read. The first live cycle reads your rates before it sends.
Wait two cycles

2. **Check that you are live.** There is no badge on the dashboard. Open the review page and find the card headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules". The green pill "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices" in it means you are live, and the button **Turn them on for real** means you are simulating. The card appears only when MAYA built starter rules for you at setup, which needs at least 60 days of booking history. If your review page has no such card, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Am%20I%20live) and we check. [Going live](@54#where-the-button-is) says how to go live without the card, and [Tell whether you are live or in simulation](@86) has the other clues.
Check that you are live

3. **Look for a problem item.** On the **Change Log** tab, an ongoing problem sits above every run, headed "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" (or "Rates not reaching Think Reservations"), with the cause and what to do. [When your property system does not accept a price](@56) explains each.
Look for a problem item

4. **Check the connection.** Open the **PMS** tab and read the **Connection** card. Error or Disconnected means your system stopped accepting MAYA's connection. Nothing is read from it or sent to it until a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. Do not wait for the amber banner above the calendar, "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds": it shows only once the **PMS** tab has been opened in your visit. [Connection lost](@100) explains each status, and what an old **Last sync** means.
Check the connection

5. **Check the subscription.** A red banner reading "MAYA has paused work on this property" means prices are not worked out or sent until the subscription is running again. Read [Account and billing problems](@102).

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type to that room type's base rate: the rate plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Cloudbeds takes the write as a job, and MAYA asks Cloudbeds whether the job applied. Packages and derived plans are never written; derived plans follow the base rate by Cloudbeds' own rules.
Check the subscription

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, live or not. MAYA reads Mews bookings and shows prices on the calendar and in the change log. The go-live dialog says so: "MAYA doesn't send rates to Mews yet, so nothing is sent. The hotel only shows as live." A manual price saved on a Mews property is not sent either, whatever the confirmation says.

Five reasons, most common first.

- **It has not gone yet.** A price changed in the last few minutes goes on the next cycle. The first send to a night waits for a fresh read of your rates.
It has not gone yet
- **You are simulating.** Prices are worked out and shown, and never sent. See the check above.
You are simulating
- **A problem is holding it.** Look for "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" at the top of the change log. The item says what is wrong and what to do.
A problem is holding it

- **Cloudbeds took it and never finished.** Cloudbeds applies a rate write as a job. If a job is still unfinished 45 minutes later, MAYA treats it as not applied and sends the night again. You are told only if it keeps happening.
Cloudbeds took it and never finished
- **ThinkReservations applies it later.** ThinkReservations accepts a write and applies it afterwards. MAYA confirms it on the next hourly read.
ThinkReservations applies it later

MAYA writes one rate per room type and no other: the base rate in Cloudbeds, the Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. Your non-refundable rate, like every other plan, moves only by your system's own rules. MAYA never writes to it.

Check three things in your system.

1. **The base rate itself.** Open the night. If the base rate still shows the old price, the new one has not landed yet. Read [the five reasons above](#maya-shows-a-new-price-but-cloudbeds-still-has-the-old-one).
The base rate itself

2. **Whether the non-refundable rate follows the base.** A plan set to follow another is what both systems call derived. Only a derived plan moves when the rate it follows moves. A plan with prices of its own stays where you set it, whatever MAYA sends.
Whether the non-refundable rate follows the base

3. **What it follows, and by how much.** A derived plan follows one rate, by the amount set in its own settings. If it follows a different plan, or the amount is not what you expect, change that in your system.

At The Harbour Inn, "Non-refundable" follows Standard Rate at 10% off. On Fri, Nov 13 2026, "Busy nights" raises Standard from $150 to $165, and MAYA sends $165 to Standard Rate. Cloudbeds moves Non-refundable from $135 to $148.50 on its own. MAYA wrote only the $165.

To make your non-refundable rate move with MAYA's price, set it in your system to follow the rate MAYA writes to. Your system then works it out from each new base rate.
What it follows, and by how much

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations marks each rate type as standard or derived. A non-refundable rate type can be standard, with prices of its own. MAYA never writes to it, so it does not move with Best Available. A derived one moves once ThinkReservations has applied the new price to the rate type it follows. Check that it follows the rate type MAYA writes to, which the ThinkReservations tab near the top of this page describes.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so no rate moves there, base or derived.

On a live property, a rate you change in your system is kept as a manual price when all of these hold: the night is one MAYA had already sent to, MAYA's send there was confirmed, the send is at least 60 minutes old, and your rate differs from MAYA's price by more than rounding. The day card then reads "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00", rules that had already moved the night are paused, and MAYA does not write over it. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@50).

Your change was written over for one of these reasons:

- **Within the hour.** You changed it less than 60 minutes after MAYA's send. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour, and again before re-sending a night it last sent to over an hour ago, so a change made inside that hour can be written over when MAYA's own price for the night changes.
Within the hour

- **A night MAYA had never sent to.** Your rate there is read as the night's starting point, not as a manual price. Your rules work from it, and MAYA sends the result. This is also what happens to every rate you change while simulating.
A night MAYA had never sent to

- **A ThinkReservations night MAYA had not read back yet.** A send to ThinkReservations counts as confirmed only once MAYA's hourly read finds it. Until then a different rate there is not read as your change.
A ThinkReservations night MAYA had not read back yet

- **Nearly every night differs by the same ratio.** When 80% or more of the nights MAYA sent to (10 at least) differ from MAYA's price by one shared ratio (a system reporting prices with tax included, or a markup), MAYA reads that as your system's own arithmetic, not as edits, and keeps sending its own prices.

**Good to know: Change prices in MAYA when you can** · A price typed on the **Calendar** tab is sent now, shows who set it, and pauses the rules already on that night at once. A change made in your system is picked up within the hour, and only on nights MAYA has already sent to.
Nearly every night differs by the same ratio

A night whose rate is 0 in your system, with no price typed in MAYA, is left unpriced. MAYA never opens a closed night at the floor.

The timing matters. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour and when your property's date changes. A night you close after MAYA has sent to it is read within the hour: its starting price becomes 0, the night is left unpriced, and any manual price on it is cleared. Between your change and that read, MAYA's price may still be there. A night closed before MAYA ever sent to it is left unpriced from the first run.

MAYA does not send a price of 0 to any property system. A manual price of 0 is a comp night: no rule raises it, and the save confirmation says "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." The change log carries an item that says the same until your system has the night at 0. Set it there yourself. Read [Make a night free](@68).

Each cycle prices and sends tonight and the next 59 nights, on your property's own calendar. A night 70 days out is not priced, refreshed or sent until it enters the window. A manual price you type further out is saved now and sent when the night enters the window, and the confirmation says so: "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 60-day push window."

The item's second line names the cause, and the item itself says what to do. [When your property system does not accept a price](@56) lists every one of those sentences with its meaning, the fix, and how MAYA retries.

A new price for tonight that never lands, while later nights go through, usually means your system and MAYA hold different time zones for your property. This one rarely shows in the change log. [The time zone case](@56#the-time-zone-case) has what to check.

**Not yet** · There is no per-night "sent" or "confirmed" mark on the calendar, and no email or notification for a sending problem. Problems live in the change log only. To confirm a price landed, open the night in your system.

**Example: A minimum rate at The Harbour Inn**

Sam sets a minimum of $120 on Deluxe in Cloudbeds. MAYA's floor for Deluxe is $110. On a slow Tuesday, "Last minute" cuts Deluxe from $140 to $119. The floor lets that through, and Cloudbeds refuses it. The change log shows at once: "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds", "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate.", "1 night, 1 room type · Still happening", and "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."

Priya types $120 on that night on the **Calendar** tab, and it is sent. Cloudbeds takes it. The item then reads "Ended" with the time, because a new price replaced the refused one.

An amber banner reading "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" means your system stopped accepting MAYA's connection: a General Manager or Hotel Admin presses **Reconnect Cloudbeds** and signs in at Cloudbeds again. The same banner can show while the **PMS** tab reads Degraded, when MAYA is still reading and sending (reconnect if it is still there in an hour). While the connection is down nothing is read, priced or sent, and the rates already in your system, your rules, history and settings stay as they are. Mews connects with keys rather than a login, so email us and we re-enter them with you.

When the connection reads Error or Disconnected, here is what stops: reading bookings, running rules and sending prices, all of it, until someone reconnects. What stays: the rates already in your system (MAYA reverts nothing), your rules, your history, your room type answers and your manual prices.

What to do: a General Manager or Hotel Admin presses **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the banner or on the **PMS** tab. It sends you to Cloudbeds to sign in and confirm, then back to MAYA. The banner text says the same: "Reconnecting takes one click and sends you to Cloudbeds to confirm. Your rules, history and settings are all untouched." Read [Reconnect your property system](@91).

After you reconnect, the next cycle reads your bookings again and sends any prices that were held back.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds tells MAYA when you uninstall or disable the app, usually within seconds. Otherwise MAYA reads the refusal on its next call, within about five minutes. Either way the banner appears and the property leaves the schedule until someone reconnects. You can also reconnect from the Cloudbeds Marketplace by pressing **Connect App** again.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA when access is revoked. MAYA finds out when its calls fail, and shows the banner once the connection's status changes. Until then the **PMS** tab may still read "Connected" while **Last sync** falls behind. A refused rate write does not disconnect ThinkReservations; it appears in the change log as a permission problem instead.

**Mews:** Mews connects with keys rather than a login, and we enter them for you. MAYA does not mark a Mews connection as lost when its reads fail, so the **PMS** tab can keep reading "Connected" with no banner. **Health (last 24 hours)** always reads "No recent activity" on Mews, so **Last sync** is the one sign. If **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is more than an hour old, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys).

The status changes to Disconnected only when we remove the keys. Then a General Manager or Hotel Admin sees "Mews needs its keys re-entered", with no button. Email us and we walk through it with you. Read [When the keys stop working](@14#when-the-keys-stop-working).

Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can reconnect. Everyone else sees the same banner with "Ask this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin to reconnect it" and no button, so they can tell the right person. Read [Roles](@63).

Go back to the Cloudbeds Marketplace and press **Connect App** for MAYA again. You land on MAYA's sign-in page with "Your Cloudbeds connection is active again. Sign in to pick up where you left off." Sign in, and the property is back on the schedule. Nothing was deleted by the uninstall. The **Reconnect Cloudbeds** button in MAYA works too.

Reading still works, so no connection banner appears. Instead the change log shows "Rates not reaching Cloudbeds" with "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates" and the action "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Cloudbeds, then reconnect on the PMS tab." Restore the permission in your system, then press **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the **PMS** tab. Held prices go out on the next cycle. Read [Prices are not reaching your property system](@99).

When Cloudbeds answers MAYA's calls with a refusal, or with its wording for an app that is no longer connected, MAYA marks the connection disconnected and shows the banner. A change to your Cloudbeds subscription or apps can cause that. Reconnect as above. If a change to your Cloudbeds login stops the connection, the same banner appears and **Reconnect Cloudbeds** fixes it.

MAYA shows the banner and the **Reconnect Think Reservations** button when the connection stops working and its status changes. Because ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA, that can lag: MAYA's reads fail first and are retried with a growing gap of up to an hour, and the banner follows once the status is marked. If **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is hours old and no banner shows, press **Reconnect Think Reservations** there anyway, with a login for this hotel only. It is harmless on a working connection.

Mews uses keys rather than a sign-in, and only we can enter them. The banner has no button. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys), and it takes a couple of minutes together.

This banner shows only after we remove the keys. If the keys stop working on their own, MAYA does not mark the connection as lost, so no banner appears and the **PMS** tab can keep reading "Connected". Watch **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab instead. If it is more than an hour old, email us.

The **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab shows one of these.

| Status | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Connected | Healthy. Bookings are read every cycle. | Nothing. |
| Pending | Connected but not yet paid for. Nothing is read or priced until the subscription starts. | Finish setting up payment. |
| Degraded | MAYA is still reading and sending. The lost-connection banner may show. | If it is still there in an hour, reconnect with a login for this property only. It does no harm. |
| Error | Your system rejected MAYA's saved sign-in. A person must reconnect. | Press **Reconnect**. |
| Disconnected | The connection is gone. The property is off the schedule. | Press **Reconnect**. |
| unknown | MAYA has no status on file. | Open the tab again in a moment, then reconnect if it stays. |

The banner appears for Degraded, Error and Disconnected. A Mews connection never reads Degraded or Error. It keeps reading Connected even while its reads fail, so on Mews watch **Last sync**.

**Last sync** is the last time bookings were read successfully. On a healthy connection it is a few minutes old. After a failed read MAYA waits longer before each retry, doubling each time up to an hour, so a system that is down for a while leaves **Last sync** up to an hour behind before it catches up. A disconnected property stops reading altogether until someone reconnects. A paused subscription stops it too.

**Health (last 24 hours)** counts MAYA's requests to your system over the last day: "Healthy" when 98% or more succeeded, "Degraded" from 80%, "Having trouble" below that, with the figure beside it, for example "76% of 412 requests OK". "Having trouble" usually means your system was down or refusing for part of the day. If the connection card reads Connected and **Last sync** is recent, the trouble has passed. If not, reconnect.

"No recent activity" means no requests were recorded. For ThinkReservations and Mews it always reads that, because only Cloudbeds requests are recorded on this tab. Read [Calendar and change log questions](@101).
The banner above the calendar appears once the **PMS** tab has been opened in your session. Open the **PMS** tab: the connection panel and the **Reconnect** button are always there.

That is normal. A successful reconnect brings you back to the dashboard, and the banner stops showing once the connection reads Connected. Open the **PMS** tab to see the status and, a few minutes later, a fresh **Last sync**.

**Careful: Reconnect with a login for this property only** · There is no screen for moving a MAYA property to a different Cloudbeds property. But on a property you connected from inside MAYA, and on ThinkReservations, reconnecting with a login that reaches one other property moves MAYA onto it, and nothing on screen warns you. Always reconnect with a login for this property only.
There is no disconnect button in MAYA. To disconnect, remove the app in Cloudbeds. Disconnecting does not cancel your subscription and deletes nothing.

Nothing is read, priced or sent. The rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. After you reconnect, the next cycle reads your bookings, prices again and sends what changed. Any price held back by a permission problem goes out then too.

The calendar colours compare each night's room revenue per room with your own other nights, so a busy night can be red, and every day is amber when there are fewer than 10 nights to compare. The calendar and the bold line of each change in the change log show $ whatever your currency. Only the sentences under each change use your currency's symbol. The change log holds the 10 most recent runs (roughly the last 50 minutes) and 40 changes per run, in your browser's time zone, and hides quiet runs unless you press **Show All Cycles**.

Colours need something to compare with. Each night's room revenue is divided by the property's room count to give revenue per room, and past nights are ranked against your other past nights, future nights against your other future nights. With fewer than 10 nights on a side, MAYA borrows both sides together, and with fewer than 10 in total there is no scale and every night is amber. A new property, or a property whose history is still importing, is amber until it has enough nights. The legend under the grid says "measured by revenue per room, relative to this property's own results".

Because the colour is revenue per room, not occupancy. A full night at low rates can earn less per room than a half-full night at high rates. Red is the bottom third of your nights, amber the middle third, green the top third, each side (past, future) ranked on its own. The colour tells you how the night's revenue ranks against your own nights, and nothing else.

The booked counts and revenue on the visible month are always fresh, but the ranking they are coloured against is kept for up to 5 minutes. A colour can lag a new booking by that long. The calendar also refreshes itself every 5 minutes on the **Calendar** tab and when you return to the browser tab.

The sentences under each change, the amber alert banner and the manual price error messages use your currency's symbol: $ for US dollars, € for euros, £ for pounds, and the three-letter code in front of the amount for any other currency. So a property in euros sees "$150.00 up to $165.00" in a change's bold line and "€150.00" in the sentence under it, for the same price. Your currency comes from your property system when you connect and cannot be changed in the app.

**Not yet** · The calendar and the change log's bold lines cannot show your currency's symbol yet, and the currency cannot be changed on a screen. If MAYA has the wrong currency for your property, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Currency).

The room type card's ADR (average daily rate: that night's room revenue divided by the rooms booked) needs at least one booking. When **Booked** reads 0, ignore the ADR line: the $150.00 there is a placeholder, whatever your rates are. It is not a price and it is not sent anywhere. Look at **Current price** for the price your rules have set.

The day detail reads "revenue on the books" for today and later, and "revenue" for past days. At properties in the Americas, today's heading can switch from "revenue on the books" to "revenue" in the evening. It is only a label and changes no price. Pricing always uses your property's own date.
The month grid has none. Click a day and its heading names the weekday: "Friday, November 13, 2026". The grid starts on Sunday.
Nights before your property's imported history have nothing to show. The year picker runs from the first month with a booking or a price to the last.

Pressing **Show All Cycles** shows every run, and a run happens about every five minutes whenever bookings were read. A run that changed nothing reads "Prices checked" and nothing needed to change. That is MAYA checking your rules and finding no reason to act. Press **Show Changes Only** to go back to the default view, which keeps only runs that changed something, sending problems and your answers.
- **Nothing has changed yet.** The default view hides quiet runs. Press **Show All Cycles** to see them. A new property with rules that have not fired shows only quiet runs.
Nothing has changed yet
- **No run has happened yet.** A property that connected minutes ago runs its first cycle within about five minutes.
No run has happened yet
- **The subscription lapsed.** A red banner reads "MAYA has paused work on this property". No runs happen until it is fixed.
The subscription lapsed
- **Reads are failing.** A run whose booking read failed prices nothing and writes nothing. Check **Health (last 24 hours)** and **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab, and look for the connection banner.
Reads are failing

- **It could not load.** "Couldn't load your price history." with a **Try again** link means the page could not fetch the log. Press **Try again**.

Simulation is not a reason: while simulating, every run happens and is written down.
It could not load

The change log holds the 10 most recent runs, quiet ones included: roughly the last 50 minutes. **Show Changes Only** hides the quiet ones among those 10, so it can look empty when nothing changed recently. An older run drops off the bottom as new ones arrive.

A sending problem that is still going on stays at the top of the log until it ends, however long ago it started. Once it has ended, it shows only while it ended within the time those 10 runs cover. Your answers to the amber banner work the same way: each one shows only while it falls within that time.

For an older change, check the night's **Current price** and any **Manual** badge on the calendar, and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) the night and room type. The detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you.

A run lists its 40 biggest moves, largest percentage first. A run that changed more nights than that shows 40 and does not say how many more there were.

**Not yet** · There is no export, no search and no filter by night or room type in the change log, and no way to see runs older than the 10 shown. For a change older than about 50 minutes, email us the night and room type and we read it for you.

Under those changes the reading is background, not the reason the price moved. The sentence under the change names what moved it. The button shows how the night was booking at the time of that run.

The button is missing when that run took no booking speed reading for the night. That happens when none of the rules you have switched on uses booking speed, and on the occasional night no booking speed rule was checking in that run. A booking speed rule that measures only some room types leaves its reading on the room types it adjusts, and nowhere else.

Your browser's. "Pricing run · Fri, Sep 18, 2026, 3:05 PM PDT" is the time on your computer's clock, with its zone abbreviation. Hover the time for the exact timestamp. Pricing itself works in your property's own time zone, and the "Updated 3:05:12 PM · live" time on the calendar is also your browser's clock.

The **Health (last 24 hours)** card and the **Recent requests** table are filled from a request log that only Cloudbeds writes to today. On a ThinkReservations or Mews property the card reads "No recent activity" and the table reads "No requests recorded yet" however healthy the connection is. Use **Connection** and **Last sync** on those properties instead.

The amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner loads when the page opens and when you switch property, and not on a timer. A night you answered in another tab, or a night that has since passed, stays on screen until you reload the page.

The billing banner loads only when the page opens. It does not reload when you switch property, so after a switch it can still show the last property's billing message, or show nothing when the new property has one. Reload the page after switching to see the billing banner for the property you are on.

If the switch fails, nothing is shown on screen and the old property stays. Reload the page and try again. Only properties that are paid for and set up appear in the **Property** dropdown: a property you set aside with "Not now" is listed under **Properties not set up yet** on the billing page, where **Set up** brings it back.

Most sign-in and billing problems have a one-line fix, and the message on screen says what to do. There is no password reset link yet, so email us from the address you signed up with. A card check moves no money, so you were not charged twice. The billing page and the Team page need General Manager or Hotel Admin access, and a property that is not paid for never appears in the property dropdown.

The sign-in card shows "Invalid login credentials" when the email or password is wrong. Check the email address you signed up with and retype the password. Passwords are at least 8 characters.

If you have forgotten your password, there is no reset link yet. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Password%20reset) from the address you signed up with, and we send you a link to set a new one. Read [Reset your password](@92).

**Not yet** · There is no forgot-password link, no way to change your email address or password inside the app, no two-factor sign-in and no Google or single sign-on. Email us for a password reset.

You pressed **Create Account** with an address that already has a MAYA login. The card has switched to sign-in mode for you. Sign in with that address. If a colleague created it and you do not have the password, ask them, or email us for a reset.

You may be asked to confirm your address when you create an account. The card reads "Check your email" with "A confirmation link is on its way to" your address. Look in spam. For a Cloudbeds Marketplace arrival the property waits for you: "Your Cloudbeds property is saved and will be waiting." If nothing arrives after a few minutes, press **Back to sign in** and try to sign in. If that fails, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Confirmation%20email).

The hand-over link from the Cloudbeds Marketplace lasts 24 hours. After that you see "That connection link has expired. Reconnect the app from the Cloudbeds Marketplace." Go back to the Marketplace and press **Connect App** again. A fresh link brings you back to MAYA.
Another MAYA account already owns that Cloudbeds property. Ask whoever set it up to invite you from the **Team** page. If you set it up yourself with a different email, sign in with that one.

They invite you. On the **Team** page they enter your email, pick your role and press **Send invitation**. You get an email with a link to set a password and join. If you already have a MAYA account, you are added at once with no email, and the property appears the next time you open MAYA. Read [Inviting and removing people](@64).
The page has been open long enough for your sign-in to lapse. Sign in again and retype the code.

The message under the field says why:

- "We don't recognize that code" (check it for typos): the code is not one we issued. Codes are letters, digits and dashes, 3 to 40 characters, and capitals do not matter.
- "That code has been turned off." or "That code has expired.": that code is no longer valid. Ask us for a current one.
- "That code has already been used the maximum number of times.": the same.
- "This property already used that code.": one redemption per property. Restarting a cancelled subscription cannot reuse the old code.
- "Too many code attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.": 20 checks per person per 10 minutes.

Codes come from us. A property arriving from the Cloudbeds Marketplace needs none. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).

Because a property attached to your account is connected but not paid for. A Cloudbeds Marketplace property is connected first and paid for second, so until payment is set up, signing in lands on the subscribe screen. Set up payment, or press "Not now" if it is one of several properties and you want to come back to it. Read [Setting up payment](@8).
Your account has no property that is set up and active yet. Onboarding is where you pay, connect and review. If a colleague has the property, ask them to invite you.

After Stripe confirms, MAYA usually takes you straight on. When confirmation is slow you see "Payment received" with "Setting up your account" and a moving bar. After 25 seconds it reads "Your payment went through, but our side is taking longer than usual to catch up." with a **Check again** button, and after 5 minutes it stops checking.

Your payment went through and you have not been charged twice. You can leave the page and sign in again later; the property is waiting. The screen also says we will email you when it is ready. No such email exists today, so do not wait for one. If the screen is still stuck an hour later, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Payment%20received%20stuck).

No. MAYA checks your saved card twice with a zero-amount check that moves no money: once right after checkout, and again 48 hours after the subscription starts. Some banks briefly show a pending line that then disappears. It is never charged. The receipt for a real charge comes from Stripe.

Your card did not pass one of the two card checks: the one right after checkout or the one 48 hours later. Nothing has been charged and nothing has failed yet, but the next charge will. The billing page says when it was checked and the bank's short reason. Press **Update card, receipts & cancellation** to open Stripe and update the card. The warning clears by itself when a payment goes through. MAYA keeps working meanwhile. Read [Cards, payments and invoices](@60).

On every cycle MAYA adds up the rooms in your room types ticked as rooms. When that measured count is higher than the count you pay for, the banner appears, and an email with the same numbers goes to the address on your billing account. You have 7 days from that email to put it right. After the 7 days MAYA raises the count you pay for to the measured number, and the difference lands on your next invoice. Nothing is charged today and nothing is charged separately.

The banner clears once you pay for at least the measured count, or the measured count comes down. A number under **Rooms billed** that is still below the measured count does not clear it. Above 500 rooms there is no email and no automatic raise: [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Over%20500%20rooms).

Where the measured count comes from depends on your property system.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations does not report how many rooms each room type has. So every room type gets the same number: one rooms-per-type number that we set for your whole property, 100 unless we change it. The measured count is that number times your room types ticked as rooms. At 100, The Harbour Inn, with Standard, Deluxe and Suite ticked as rooms, sees "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 300".

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20room%20counts) your real room counts before you rely on this number. If the banner shows a count you do not have, email us straight away, before the 7 days run out. We can change that one number, not set a count for each room type.

**Mews:** Where Mews gives no room count for a room category, that category gets one rooms-per-type number that we set for your whole property, 100 unless we change it. The measured count then adds that number once for each such category ticked as a room, so it can be far from the rooms you run.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) your real room counts before you rely on this number. If the banner shows a count you do not have, email us straight away, before the 7 days run out. We can change that one number, not set a count for each category.

If MAYA is counting something that is not a guest room, untick it under **Room types** on the **PMS** tab and the count drops on the next cycle. If you pay for more rooms than you run, MAYA never lowers the count by itself: change it on the billing page under **Rooms billed**, and your next invoice drops. Read [Your room count](@59).

- "Update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off." The last payments failed and the bank's retries ran out. Press **Restart MAYA**, then **Update card, receipts & cancellation**, and update the card. Then pay the open invoice in Stripe, and the subscription restarts where it left off. Updating the card alone does not restart it, because nothing tries the payment again by itself.
- "Your subscription was cancelled, so starting again means a new one" (restart below whenever you are ready). Press **Restart your subscription** on the billing page. A new subscription starts on the same pricing; the old code cannot be reused.

Your rules, limits, history and settings are kept while paused. Rates already in your system stay as they are. Read [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@61).
One subscription per property. The message adds "Manage it at /account/billing." Open the billing page from the **Billing** button on the dashboard to change the room count, the card or the plan.

The billing page shows Stripe's own preview of your next invoice, which includes any code you used and, where it applies, tax. The calculator on the website shows the list price for your room count. The two agree once a discount ends. Read [The billing page](@58).

It needs General Manager or Hotel Admin access. Anyone else sees "Billing is handled by this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. Ask one of them for access if you need to change it." The **Team** page works the same way. Read [Roles](@63).

The **Property** dropdown lists only properties you belong to that are paid for and set up. A property you set aside with "Not now" during a group setup is listed on the billing page under **Properties not set up yet**, where **Set up** takes you back to pay for it. A property someone else owns needs an invitation from them.

Seats come with your room count: 2 seats for 1 to 20 rooms, 4 for 21 to 40, 5 for 41 to 60, 6 for 61 to 80, 8 for 81 to 500. Everyone listed on the **Team** page counts, including someone you invited who has not set a password yet. Remove someone, or raise the room count on the billing page if the property has grown.
