MAYA uses a small set of words on screen and in these docs. Each is defined here in a few plain sentences, in alphabetical order, with a link to the page that explains it fully. A word marked (screen) is a label you will see in the app, written here exactly as it appears there.

**ADR** (screen: ADR $150.00). Average daily rate: a room type's room revenue for a night divided by the rooms of that type booked that night. It is on the room type cards in the calendar's day detail. With nothing booked it shows $150.00, which is a placeholder, not a price. Read [The calendar](@45).
ADR

**Base price.** The price a rule starts from on a night and room type. It is your typed price if you set one, else your own rate as read from your property system, else the newest booking's rate for that night, else the last base price MAYA recorded for that night. Read [How prices reach your property system](@55).
Base price

**Base rate** (screen, Cloudbeds). The one rate plan per room type that MAYA writes to in Cloudbeds: the plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Derived plans follow it by Cloudbeds' own rules. In ThinkReservations, the Best Available rate type. The change log also says "set the base rate" for a price someone typed. There it means the night's starting price. Read [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).
Base rate

**Best Available** (ThinkReservations). The standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available". It is the rate type MAYA sends its prices to in ThinkReservations. If no rate type has that name, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. If two tie, neither is used and nothing is sent until you name one Best Available. Read [ThinkReservations](@13).
Best Available

**Booking.** For booking speed, one reservation for one night, however many rooms it holds: a 20-room wedding booked as one reservation in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations is one booking. In Mews each room is its own reservation, so each room counts as a booking, and so does each separate reservation made from a group block. For sellable occupancy and pickup count, each room counts, so the same wedding is 20 booked rooms. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Booking

**Booking speed** (screen). How many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with how many similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. Seven levels, from Stalled to Surging. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Booking speed

**Booking speed and pickup rules.** Any rule with a Booking speed or Pickup count condition. It fires, the change stays on the price, and after its wait it can fire again on the same night, so raises stack on raises and cuts on cuts. At most one of them fires on a night and room type per run. Read [How rules run](@39).
Booking speed and pickup rules
**Booking window** (screen: Booking window (days to stay)). The number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar. Tonight is 0, tomorrow night is 1. Read [Booking window](@33).
Booking window

**Ceiling** (screen). The highest price MAYA will publish for a room type. Setup fills it from your answer to the five questions where it fits, or else from your own rates if the room type has at least 200 room nights sold. Otherwise it stays at $99,999.99 (a number in your own currency), which stops nothing in most currencies, until you set one. Where rooms sell above 99,999.99, as they can in yen or rupiah, the default ceiling holds prices down, so set one before you go live. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).
Ceiling

**Change Log** (screen). The tab that shows the 10 most recent pricing runs and, for each change, which rule acted and why. A run happens about every five minutes and quiet runs count toward the 10, so it covers about the last 50 minutes. By default it lists only the runs among them that changed a price. Read [The change log](@46).
Change Log

**Changed in Cloudbeds** (screen: Changed in Cloudbeds · $123.00). The badge on a room type card for a rate you changed in your property system on a night MAYA had already sent to. MAYA keeps it like a manual price. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@50).
Changed in Cloudbeds
**Closed period.** A stretch when the whole property was shut, confirmed on the setup review. Its nights are left out of every comparison. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).
Closed period

**Code.** A signup code we give you that opens self-serve signup for a property system, or grants a trial or a discount. One code per property. A code's own free days replace the Marketplace trial rather than adding to it, while a discount code with no free days keeps the trial and discounts the invoices after it. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).
Code
**Comp night.** A night with a manual price of 0. No rule raises it. MAYA does not send 0 to any property system, so you set it there yourself. Read [Make a night free](@68).
Comp night

**Connected** (screen, on the PMS tab). The connection to your property system is working: MAYA reads your bookings and, once you are live, sends prices. The other words the **Connection** card can show are Pending, Degraded, Error and Disconnected, each defined here. Read [The PMS tab](@52).
Connected

**Counts as a room** (screen). The checkbox on the PMS tab that says a room type is somewhere guests sleep. Ticked types are what MAYA divides by for sellable occupancy, and what you are billed for. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@51).
Counts as a room
**Current price** (screen). The price MAYA has worked out for a room type on a night, after rules and limits. It is what the calendar shows and what is sent. Read [The calendar](@45).
Current price

**Cycle.** One run of MAYA for your property, about every five minutes: read bookings, refresh your rates if due, run every rule over the next 60 nights and, once you are live, send the prices that changed. For Mews, MAYA does not read rates or send prices yet. Cycles run on MAYA's side, day and night, whether or not anyone has MAYA open, and your own internet being down does not stop them. Only MAYA being unable to reach your property system's service does, or a stopped subscription. Read [How rules run](@39).
Cycle

**Degraded** (screen, on the PMS tab). Two meanings. On the **Connection** card (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only): MAYA is still reading and sending, and the lost-connection banner may show. It usually clears by itself on the next read. If it is still there in an hour, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects, which does no harm. On the **Health (last 24 hours)** card: 80% to under 98% of MAYA's requests to your system succeeded. Read [Reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).
Degraded

**Derived rate plan.** A rate plan in your property system that follows another plan by a rule of its own, such as 10% off the base rate. MAYA never writes to one. It moves when the base rate moves, by your system's own rules. ThinkReservations calls it a derived rate type. Read [How prices reach your property system](@55).
Derived rate plan

**Disconnected** (screen, on the PMS tab). MAYA's access to your property system is gone: the app was uninstalled, its permission was removed, or your system refused it. Nothing is read or sent until a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. Nothing is deleted. Read [Reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).
Disconnected
**Error** (screen, on the PMS tab). Your property system refused MAYA's saved access, so reading has stopped. A General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. Read [Connection lost](@100).
Error

**Expected** (in explanations). What similar past nights had received over the same stretch of their own run-up, averaged with the highest and lowest dropped once there are five or more. It can be a fraction, such as 0.4. On screen it reads "almost none" under 1 and is rounded to a whole number otherwise. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Expected

**Fired** (screen). The number of times a rule acted, counted once per night and room type, including changes that later came off. A booking speed or pickup rule can act on the same night more than once. Read [The rule builder](@31).
Fired

**Floor** (screen). The lowest price MAYA will publish for a room type. Setup fills it from your answer to the five questions, or else from your own rates if the room type has at least 30 room nights sold. Otherwise it stays at $1.00, which stops nothing, until you set one (a floor cannot be 0). Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).
Floor
**General Manager** (screen, a role). Everything except managing Hotel Admins: pricing, going live, the property system connection, billing and the team. Read [Roles](@63).
General Manager

**Go live.** Switching a property from simulation to live, so its changed prices are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations every cycle (nothing is sent to Mews yet). A General Manager or Hotel Admin does it with **Turn them on for real**, in the starter rules box on the review screen. The box is there only if setup added starter rules, and it is gone once someone uses **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. Without it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) and we switch the property live. One way in the app: only we can switch a property back. Read [Going live](@54).
Go live
**Guardrails** (screen, in the Rate Simulator). A room type's floor and ceiling, shown together as a range.
Guardrails

**Hold My Hand / Let Me Drive** (screen). The two setup paths. **Hold My Hand** asks five optional questions and walks you through the review. **Let Me Drive** goes straight to the dashboard, and the review stays available. Read [Hold my hand or let me drive](@24).
Hold My Hand / Let Me Drive

**Holiday.** One of 17 US holidays MAYA uses to pick similar nights: a night near Thanksgiving is compared with the same position around Thanksgiving in earlier years. No other holidays exist yet. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@105).
Holiday
**Hotel Admin** (screen, a role). Everything, including managing General Managers. The person who creates the account and pays is a property's first Hotel Admin. Read [Roles](@63).
Hotel Admin
**Hotel day.** A calendar date in your property's own time zone. The window, booking windows and "past week" all count in hotel days. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@105).
Hotel day

**How did we know?** (screen). The link under a booking speed change in the change log. It opens the counts behind the change, the nights MAYA compared with, and the way to set one aside. Read [How did we know?](@47).
How did we know?

**Last sync** (screen, on the PMS tab). The last time MAYA read your bookings from your property system successfully, about every five minutes on a healthy connection. It says nothing about sending prices. Read [The PMS tab](@52).
Last sync
**Level.** One of the seven booking speed readings: Stalled, Much Slower Than Normal, Slower Than Normal, Normal, Faster Than Normal, Much Faster Than Normal, Surging. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Level

**Live.** The state after going live. Every cycle, prices that changed are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. Nothing is sent to Mews yet, so a Mews property only shows as live. Read [Simulation mode](@53).
Live

**Manual price** (screen: Manual · $123.00). A price you typed for a room type on a night on the Calendar tab. It becomes the night's base price. Once you are live, it is sent as typed to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations (a night beyond the 60-night window goes when it enters the window). Nothing is sent to Mews yet, and a price of 0 is never sent. Rules already on that night pause for that room type, and rules that fire later stack on top. Read [Setting a price yourself](@49).
Manual price

**Marketplace.** The Cloudbeds Marketplace, where a Cloudbeds property installs MAYA with **Connect App**. Properties that arrive this way get the free trial and can come in as a group. Read [Cloudbeds](@12).
Marketplace

**Measure / Change** (screen). The two room type lists of a rule that watches one set of room types and prices another, shown when **Change prices on different room types** is ticked. Read [Measure one set, change another](@38).
Measure / Change
**Measured over** (screen). The booking speed window: **Past day**, **Past week** or **Past month**, counted in booking dates on your property's calendar, today included. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Measured over

**Momentum** (in explanations). The fallback reading when a night has no similar past nights: how nearby dates are filling now compared with the same dates a year earlier. Always treated as thin evidence. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Momentum
**Not a fair comparison?** (screen). The link on a compared night that lets you set it aside with a reason. Read [Not a fair comparison](@48).
Not a fair comparison?

**Package.** A rate plan that sells the room together with something else, such as breakfast or parking. MAYA never writes to a package. A package built on the base rate moves when the base rate does, by your system's own rules. Read [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).
Package

**Paused.** A word with four meanings, so these docs keep them apart. A rule you set to **Off** on the **Rules** tab is "switched off": it stops acting and its changes stay on the price (the switch says On and Off, and the list's filter says Enabled and Disabled). Rules on a night where you typed a price are "held": their changes come off that night, and the save's confirmation counts them, as in "Paused 2 rules on this night for this room". "MAYA has paused work on this property" is the banner shown while the subscription is not active, and "Paused" as a status on the Billing page means the subscription is on hold in Stripe. Read [Turning a rule off, deleting it, or changing it](@41), [Setting a price yourself](@49) and [The billing page](@58).
Paused
**Pending** (screen, on the PMS tab). Connected but not paid for yet, or set up and not switched on yet. Nothing runs until then. Finish payment, or wait for us. Read [The PMS tab](@52).
Pending
**Pickup count** (screen: Pickup count (advanced)). How many room nights, or how much revenue, a night gained over the last 1, 3 or 7 days, cancellations subtracted. Read [Pickup count](@37).
Pickup count
**PMS** (screen). Your property management system: Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations or Mews, where your bookings and rates live. In these docs, "property system". Read [Which systems work](@11).
PMS
**Price and rate.** In these docs, a price is what MAYA works out and sends. A rate is what lives in your property system, such as your base rate or a rate you changed there.
Price and rate
**Pricing run** (screen). One evaluation of every night and every rule for your property. The change log shows the 10 most recent, one entry per run. Read [The change log](@46).
Pricing run

**Rate Simulator** (screen). The tab where you make up a night and see what your rules would do to it. Nothing there is saved or sent unless you click **Save This Rule**, and a rule saved from there arrives switched Off. Read [The Rate Simulator](@43).
Rate Simulator

**Revenue Manager** (screen, a role). Day-to-day pricing: rules, typed prices, floors and ceilings, room types and rooms out of service, answering the Rules that keep adjusting banner, and setting dates aside. A Revenue Manager cannot go live, reconnect the property system, see billing or change the team. Read [Roles](@63).
Revenue Manager
**Revenue on the books** (screen). Room revenue from bookings already made for that night, shown on the calendar day card. Read [The calendar](@45).
Revenue on the books

**RevPAR** (screen). Revenue per available room: the whole property's room revenue for a night divided by the number of rooms in room types ticked **Counts as a room**. The calendar's colours rank your nights by it (the legend says "revenue per room"). Unticking a room type takes its rooms out of it. Read [The calendar](@45).
RevPAR
**Room count.** The number of rooms you are billed for. MAYA measures it from your property system every cycle, counting only room types ticked as rooms. Read [Your room count](@59).
Room count

**Room night.** One room for one night. A booking of 2 rooms for 3 nights is 6 room nights. Pickup count and the import's progress bar count room nights. For a single night, room nights are the rooms booked.
Room night

**Rooms out of service** (screen). Rooms you take off sale for a stretch, entered on the PMS tab. They come off the sellable count for those nights only. Nothing is sent to your system. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@51).
Rooms out of service

**Rule.** One sentence you write once: when a night looks like this, change its price by that much. MAYA checks every rule against your bookings about every five minutes. Read [Build your first rule](@30).
Rule
**Rules that keep adjusting** (screen). The amber banner that asks you what to do once a booking speed or pickup rule has adjusted the same night three times. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@42).
Rules that keep adjusting
**Season.** A stretch of your year that books differently, found from your own history and never set by hand. It only ever appears inside an explanation. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Season
**Seats.** How many people can be on a property's team, members plus pending invitations: 2, 4, 5, 6 or 8, following your room count. Read [Inviting and removing people](@64).
Seats

**Sellable occupancy** (screen). Rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms, with rooms out of service taken off first. Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89%. Read [Sellable occupancy](@32).
Sellable occupancy
**Set aside** (screen: Set this date aside). Marking a past night as not a fair comparison so it is left out of comparisons from the next run. Read [Not a fair comparison](@48).
Set aside

**Similar nights.** The up to eight past nights MAYA compares a night with, from the last three years: same weekday (or, near a holiday, the same position around it) and same time of year. A night near a holiday has at most three, one a year. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Similar nights
**Simulation mode.** The starting state of every property. Everything runs and is written to the change log, and nothing is sent to your property system. Read [Simulation mode](@53).
Simulation mode

**Standard rule** (screen, in the How rules behave panel). A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions. It holds one change while its condition holds and takes it off when the condition stops. It never stacks on itself. Read [How rules run](@39).
Standard rule

**Starter rules.** The five booking speed rules MAYA adds at setup when your property has about two months of history and no rules yet: Slow-date rescue, Slow-date trim, Warm-date bump, Hot-week surge and Sudden-spike catcher. Every property gets the same settings, and each rule compares a night's bookings with your own similar past nights. Read [Your starter rules](@27).
Starter rules

**Stopped on N nights** (screen). The chip under a rule's switch that counts the nights still to come on which you told it to stop, with **Let it run again** beside it. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@42).
Stopped on N nights

**Then waits** (screen: Then waits (advanced)). How long a booking speed rule leaves a night alone after acting on it: 1 day to 2 weeks, 1 week when unset. A rule with a pickup count condition waits at least its lookback. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Then waits
**Three-times question.** Another name for the Rules that keep adjusting banner.
Three-times question

**Trial.** Free days before your first charge. Properties that arrive from the Cloudbeds Marketplace get a 7-day free trial. A code can carry its own trial, which replaces the Marketplace one rather than adding to it. A card is taken and nothing is charged until the trial ends. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).
Trial
**Viewer** (screen, a role). Can look at everything and change nothing. Read [Roles](@63).
Viewer
**Wait.** See Then waits. The wait is counted per rule, night and room type, from that night's last counted change, or from a price you typed if it came later.
Wait
**Weekend.** Friday and Saturday nights. Used when similar nights are chosen and seasons are read. Rules have no weekday control yet. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@105).
Weekend

**Window (60 nights).** Tonight and the next 59 nights on your property's calendar: the nights your rules price every cycle and, once you are live, the nights whose prices are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. A price you type further ahead is sent when its night enters the window. Read [How prices reach your property system](@55).
Window (60 nights)
**Your corrections** (screen). The panel at the top of the change log that lists every date you have set aside, each with **Undo**. Read [Not a fair comparison](@48).
Your corrections

If you have used another revenue tool, these are the words you may be looking for, and what MAYA calls them.

**Comp set** (competitive set). Not used. MAYA reads no competitor rates and no data from other hotels, only your own bookings and rates. Read [What MAYA does](@0).
Comp set
**Lead time.** MAYA calls it the booking window: the number of days from today until the night. A rule uses it through the **Booking window (days to stay)** condition. Read [Booking window](@33).
Lead time

**Length of stay (LOS).** Not used by rules. There is no condition for how long a guest stays, and MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type. Keep length-of-stay prices and minimum stays in your property system. Read [What rules cannot do yet](@44).
Length of stay (LOS)

**Pace.** MAYA calls it booking speed: how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with what similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Pace

**STLY** (same time last year). There is no STLY report. The nearest thing is similar nights: each night is compared with similar past nights from the last three years, read at the same distance before arrival. When none can be found, momentum compares nearby nights now with the same nights a year ago. Read [Similar nights](@36).
STLY

**Yield rules.** MAYA calls them rules: one sentence you write once, such as "when a night is more than 80% full, raise every room type by 10%". If your property system has yield rules of its own that change the base rate, switch them off before you go live. Read [Build your first rule](@30).
Yield rules

MAYA works on your property's own calendar, using the time zone read from your system when you connected. Tonight is today's date there, and weekends are Friday and Saturday nights. The holidays MAYA uses are 17 US holidays, and any other can be set aside. Prices are in your property's currency, worked out to two decimal places, while billing is in US dollars.

MAYA counts days on your property's calendar. "Today" is the date at your property, in its time zone, at the moment MAYA checks. The docs call that a hotel day.

Everything that counts nights starts from it:
- **Tonight** is night 0 of the booking window, and tomorrow night is night 1. [Booking window](@33)
Tonight
- **The 60-night window** your rules price every cycle is tonight and the next 59 nights. [How rules run](@39)
The 60-night window
- **A typed price** can be set from tonight onwards, never on a night that has passed. [Setting a price yourself](@49)
A typed price

- **Past day, past week and past month** in booking speed are counted in hotel days. [See how they are counted](#past-day-past-week-and-past-month).

**Example: Midnight at The Harbour Inn**

The Harbour Inn is on US Pacific time. A check at 11 pm on Friday still treats Friday night as tonight, night 0. A check at 12:30 am on Saturday treats Saturday night as tonight and Friday as past, so Friday leaves the window and a price can no longer be typed for it.

An illustration with made-up numbers, not your property.
Past day, past week and past month

MAYA reads your property's time zone once, when you connect, and keeps it.

**Cloudbeds:** The time zone set on your property in Cloudbeds.

**ThinkReservations:** The time zone set on your hotel in ThinkReservations.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read it from Mews. We set it with you when we connect the property.

If your system gave none, MAYA uses universal time (UTC) until we set yours. No screen in MAYA shows the time zone, and it cannot be changed from the app. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone) to check or change it. Changing it in your system later does not change it in MAYA.
- **Pricing** always uses your property's date.
Pricing

- **Times on screen** use your own browser's clock: the time of each run in the **Change Log** (with its zone, such as PDT), the "Updated" time on the calendar, and **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab. Two people in different places see different clock times for the same run.
Times on screen

- **One label** follows universal time (UTC): the day detail's "revenue on the books", which switches to "revenue" at midnight UTC. At a property in the Americas that happens in the evening. It changes no number. [Calendar and change log questions](@101)
One label

These are the choices under **Measured over** in a booking speed rule. They count booking dates, today included:

| Choice | Counts bookings dated |
|---|---|
| **Past day** | today only |
| **Past week** | today and the 6 days before it (7 dates) |
| **Past month** | today and the 29 days before it (30 dates) |

So **Past day** is not the last 24 hours. Shortly after midnight at your property it has almost nothing in it yet, and it fills up through the day. [Booking speed](@34)

**Booking dates.** A booking counts on the date it was made:

**Cloudbeds:** The creation date exactly as Cloudbeds records it. MAYA does not convert it to another time zone.

**ThinkReservations:** The moment ThinkReservations recorded the booking, put on your property's own calendar. An 11 pm booking in California is dated that day.

**Mews:** The moment Mews recorded the booking, put on your property's own calendar.

If a booking's date looks a day off from what your system shows, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Booking%20date) with the booking and we check it.

Two things are counted in hours rather than hotel days:

- **A rule's wait.** After a booking speed or pickup rule changes a night, it leaves that night alone for its wait: 1 day to 2 weeks for a booking speed rule, the lookback for a pickup rule. The wait is counted in 24-hour periods from the moment the rule acted. [How rules run](@39)
A rule's wait
- **A pickup lookback.** "The last 3 days" means from exactly 3 times 24 hours before the check. A check at 3:05 PM reaches back to 3:05 PM three days earlier. [Pickup count](@37)
A pickup lookback

Hotel days follow your property's local calendar, so the change to or from daylight saving time moves no night: tonight is still tonight. Waits and pickup lookbacks are 24-hour periods, so across the change they end an hour earlier or later by the clock on the wall.

Weekends are Friday and Saturday nights, and Sunday night counts as a weeknight. That is how MAYA reads them when it picks similar past nights: a Friday is compared with other Fridays and, if too few are found, with Saturdays, but never with a weeknight. (Near a holiday, nights are matched by their place around the holiday instead.) It is also how MAYA reads the weekly shape of your seasons. [Similar nights](@36)

Rules have no weekday setting: every rule runs every night. For a weekend price, type it on those nights. [What rules cannot do yet](@44)

MAYA uses 17 US holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Valentine's Day, Presidents' Day, St. Patrick's Day, Easter, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Father's Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Halloween, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Each has a stretch of days around it.

A holiday never changes a price by itself, and there is no holiday rule. It changes which past nights a night is compared with: the Saturday after Thanksgiving is compared with the Saturday after Thanksgiving in earlier years, not with the same date. [Similar nights](@36) has each holiday's stretch.
Seasons are stretches of your year that book differently, found from your own history, never set by hand. They only ever show inside an explanation under **How did we know?**. [Similar nights](@36)

Your property's currency is read once, when you connect: from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, and set with you for Mews. MAYA never converts anything. Every price is a number in your own currency.

The symbol depends on the screen:

- **Your currency's symbol** in the change log's sentences, the **Rules that keep adjusting** banner and the typed-price messages. That is $ for US dollars, € for euros and £ for pounds, and the three-letter code in front of the amount for any other.
Your currency's symbol

- **Always $**, whatever your currency, on the calendar's day cards and day detail, the room type cards, the typed-price box and the Rate Simulator. The first line of each change in the change log also shows $. The numbers are still yours. [Calendar and change log questions](@101)

Your MAYA subscription is billed in US dollars, whatever your property's currency. [What it costs](@3)

To check which currency MAYA has for your property, read the sign in the sentences under any change in the **Change Log**, not the bold line above them. The currency cannot be changed from the app. If MAYA has the wrong one, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Currency).
Always $

**The default floor and ceiling are numbers in your currency.** Every room type starts with a floor of 1.00 and a ceiling of 99,999.99, whatever the currency. In most currencies they stop nothing. Where a room type sells above 99,999.99 (yen, won, rupiah or dong, for example), the default ceiling holds its prices down to 99,999.99, and a price you type above it is refused, until a real ceiling is set. Set ceilings before you go live: through the five questions, a suggestion card, or by email. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28#when-your-rates-are-above-the-default-ceiling).
The default floor and ceiling are numbers in your currency

**Typing amounts.** The price box on the calendar and the amount and threshold boxes in the rule builder are your browser's number boxes. Type a point for decimals, as in 180.50, and no thousands separator, as in 1250. Whether a box also takes a comma (180,50) depends on your browser and its language. If it cannot read what you typed, the box counts as empty: **Save** stays greyed out, or the rule is not added, so nothing wrong is saved.
Typing amounts

MAYA works out every price to two decimal places, whatever the currency, and sends it that way. A price you type, a floor and a ceiling are rounded to two decimal places too. There is no setting to round to whole units.

For a currency with no cents, such as Japanese yen, that means a percentage rule can produce a price with decimals. MAYA sends that number as it is. If your system keeps whole units, it rounds the price its own way. When MAYA reads the rate back, a whole number less than 1 away from the price MAYA sent counts as MAYA's own price, rounded, and not as a rate you changed. So the rounding never turns into a manual price, and MAYA does not keep sending the price again.

To keep prices whole, set rules to change by a fixed amount rather than a percentage, and use whole numbers for floors, ceilings and typed prices. As long as your own rates are whole, prices then stay whole. The starter rules change prices by percentages, so they can produce decimals.

Going live, cancelling and deleting data need an email from a General Manager's or Hotel Admin's own address. Deletion is permanent: once we have verified the request, we delete or de-identify the property's data within 90 days, and MAYA ends for that property without a refund.

Can we change your prices for you? No. We do not type, raise or cut prices on your behalf. The Terms of Service (section 4.1) make you responsible for every price MAYA publishes, and the change log names who typed each price in MAYA.

What we do instead:
- **Talk it through.** Send us the change log entry and we look at the same night with you, and say which rule acted and why.
Talk it through
- **Stop the sending.** At your request we put a live property back into simulation. Nothing more is sent, and the prices already in your system stay as they are.
Stop the sending

- **Change a setting you cannot change on a screen yet**, such as a room count, a time zone or a currency, using the numbers you send us. Whatever we change at your request, we change on your instruction (Terms section 3.3).

The change itself is quicker in your hands anyway. Anyone with the Revenue Manager, General Manager or Hotel Admin role can type a price on the **Calendar** tab, and [Setting a price yourself](@49) shows how. On Mews, where MAYA does not send prices yet, you change the rate in Mews itself.
Change a setting you cannot change on a screen yet

Support is by email only. There is no phone line, no chat and no public status page.

To check your own connection, open the **PMS** tab. The **Connection** card says whether your system is connected, and **Last sync** says when bookings were last read. On Mews, keys that stop working show no warning, so **Last sync** is the thing to watch. Problems sending prices sit at the top of the **Change Log** while they last. Read [the PMS tab](@52).

On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, setup is designed so nobody needs a call: connect, answer five optional questions, review what MAYA found, go live. Mews we connect with you by email. If you would rather have a person walk you through any of it, email us and say so.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Something%20is%20not%20working) with the subject "Something is not working", and include:

1. Your property's name, and the tab or page you were on.
2. What you did, click by click.
3. What you expected, and what happened instead, with the exact words of any message.
4. A screenshot, and your browser's name and version.
5. When it happened, as the time your screen showed.

If the screen showed a message, [Messages you might see, explained](@103) may already cover it.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Feature%20request) with the subject "Feature request". Say what you would like MAYA to do and the situation you would use it in. It helps us see how many owners want the same thing.

We do not promise dates. These docs describe only what MAYA does today, so a feature appears here once it is in the app. [What rules cannot do yet](@44) lists what rules cannot do today, with what to do instead.

Our staff can open your property to help, for example to switch it back to simulation at your request or to check a price with you. We never need your password for that, so never send one. [Roles: who can do what](@63) has the details.

Requests about your data (a copy, a correction or a deletion) go to the same address. The [Privacy Policy](https://www.get-maya.com/privacy) (section 10) lists your rights.

For anything formal under the Terms, email the same address with "Legal Notice" in the subject line, or write to Modern Hospitality Solutions LLC, 1515 E Cesar Chavez St. Suite 100, Austin, TX 78702 (Terms section 18.2).

These pages describe MAYA as it works today, including what it cannot do yet. The **Ask MAYA docs** button opens the docs helper, which answers with the passage from these pages that best matches your question, word for word. It matches your question inside your browser. We count each question asked, without its words, and your words reach us only if you press **Send**. Never type guest names, card numbers or passwords into it.

Every page describes MAYA as it works today. We check each page against the app before it is published, and we change it when the app changes. Where MAYA cannot do something yet, the page says so plainly and says what to do instead. We do not promise dates.

Each page is built from the same few pieces:

| On a page | What it is |
|---|---|
| **In plain words** | The answer to the page's question in two to four sentences. It stands on its own, so if you read one thing, read this. |
| **Not yet** | Something MAYA cannot do today, and what to do instead. |
| **Careful** | Something that costs money, sends a price or cannot be undone. |
| **Good to know** | A useful fact you did not ask for. |
| **Example** | A worked example, closed until you open it, so the page stays short. |
| **Try it** | A small tool where you change the numbers and watch the result. It uses the same numbers MAYA uses, with made-up bookings and rates, not your property's. |
| **Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations and Mews tabs** | The same topic for each property system. Pick yours once and pages open on it in this browser. |

Every worked example uses one imaginary property, so the numbers stay consistent from page to page. The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms: 12 Standard, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suites, plus a meeting room that does not count as a room. It is on US Pacific time and prices in US dollars. Sam is its Hotel Admin and Priya its Revenue Manager. It is not a real hotel, and no example uses a real guest.

- **Search.** The box at the top of the menu on the left (on a phone, **Search** in the bar at the top). Press the / key to jump to it from anywhere on a page. Results appear as you type, with the page, its section and the heading that matched. Searching happens in your browser.
Search
- **On this page.** The list beside each page (above it on a phone) jumps to any heading. A thin bar across the top shows how far through the page you are.
On this page
- **Reading time.** Under each title, with the date the page was last updated where it has one.
Reading time
- **Related, previous and next.** Each page ends with up to three related pages, then the previous and next page in order.
Related, previous and next
- **Light or dark.** The sun and moon button switches the theme, and this browser keeps your choice.
Light or dark
- **Printing.** A printed page opens every example and shows every property system's tab.
Printing

If you are signed in to MAYA in this browser, the names of places in MAYA on these pages open that place in a new tab, with a small arrow after the words. Some how-tos also show a button that opens MAYA with the rule, filter or choice from the page already filled in.

A link never saves or changes anything. You still click **Add Rule**, **Save This Rule** or **Send invitation** yourself, and MAYA still checks what your role allows. A link opens your active property. Signed out, you see the same words without links.

It works the other way too. **Help** at the top of MAYA's screens opens the page about the screen you are on, and **Learn more** in a "?" panel opens the passage that explains it in full.

The **Ask MAYA docs** button sits at the bottom right of every docs page, the docs home and the support page. On a phone, tap **Ask** in the bar at the top. It opens a panel with a box to type in. While the panel is empty, it offers a few common questions to start from.

To see how it works, open it and ask "Is there a status page?", then compare the answer with the page it links to.

The docs helper does not write anything. Every answer is a passage copied from these pages, word for word, or one of a few short replies written in advance for general questions such as "hi", "what can I ask?" or "can I talk to a person?". Ask "how does this work?" or "what is this page?" and it answers about the page you are on, with its In plain words box and its headings.

When you ask a question, it compares your words with:

- the words in every section of every page,
- the questions each page lists as the ones it answers,
- a list of words people use for the same thing, such as "price" and "rate", "undo" and "put back", or "wedding" and "group".

When the match is weak, it says so. It shows the closest section under "This might help", followed by "Not quite it? Send us your question." and a **Send** button, which works like the one below. When nothing matches, it shows no section, only the message below.

**Example: What an answer looks like**

Sam types "forgot my password". An answer looks like this. First, word for word, the In plain words box of [Reset your password](@92). Then a link to that page, and "Did this help?" with **Yes** and **No**.

The panel says "No clear answer in the docs.", links the pages that came closest (when any came close) and a few good places to start, and gives you two ways forward:

- **Send** sends your question to us so we can write the missing page. It carries no name or email address, so we cannot reply to it.
Send
- **The email link** opens an email to us with the subject "Docs question". Use it when you want an answer. We aim to reply within one business day.
The email link

Your question is matched inside your browser. Your words reach us only if you press a button that sends them. Each question asked is also counted, without its words.

| When you | What reaches us |
|---|---|
| Ask a question | A count, never your words: the kind of reply (a passage, a set reply, "This might help" or no answer), the part of the docs you were in, whether you were signed in to MAYA and, if **Help** in MAYA opened the docs, which screen it was on |
| Press **Yes** under "Did this help?" | Nothing |
| Press **No** under "Did this help?" | Nothing yet. A box opens for an optional note, with a **Send** button |
| Press **Send** | Your question, your note if you wrote one, the page you were on and which sections were shown |
| Press a button under "Was this page useful?" at the foot of a page | Which page it was and which button you pressed. No text |

Before anything you send is stored, email addresses, phone numbers and long runs of digits (such as a card number) are replaced with "[removed]". It is kept as text only, with no name, account, IP address or cookie attached. The only other thing noted is whether you were signed in to MAYA when you sent it. Treat that clean-up as a safety net, not a reason to type personal details. The count is stored with the day, not the time, and with no name, account, IP address or cookie.

Your conversation stays in the browser tab you asked it in, and is gone when you close the tab. Apart from that count of questions, these pages run no visitor counting, and they set no cookies of their own. The [Privacy Policy](https://www.get-maya.com/privacy) explains the rest.

The docs helper answers from these pages, not from your account, so it never needs:

- guest names, or anything about a guest,
- card numbers or bank details,
- passwords, yours or your property system's.

It has no access to your property. It has these pages and nothing else: not your prices, bookings, rules, bill or change log. Ask "why did Deluxe go up on November 13?" and it can only show you a page such as [Find out why a price changed](@65). Your property's own reasons are in the change log and behind the **How did we know?** button.

It cannot do anything for you either. It cannot reset a password, switch a property back to simulation or change a setting. For those, [contact support](@110).

Use the words on your screen

Paste a message exactly

Name your property system

Ask one thing at a time

If an answer misses,

Include the page, the sentence and what you see instead. Pressing **No** and then **Send** in the docs helper tells us about an answer that missed.
